papers.title: Potential of Anaerobic Digestate for Bioremediation and Biofertilization
papers.abstract: Anaerobic digestate derived from the gut contents of slaughtered beef cattle presents a promising dual-purpose resource for environmental remediation and agricultural enhancement. This study investigated the physicochemical properties and microbial diversity of digestate, focusing on its potential for hydrocarbon degradation and phosphate solubilization. Physicochemical analysis revealed a nutrient-rich composition with a near-neutral pH (7.6), low biological oxygen demand (3.294 mg/L), and favourable levels of nitrogen (0.238%), phosphorus (0.0184%), and potassium (0.235%). Microbial screening identified four hydrocarbon-degrading species: Ruminococcus sp., Clostridium sp., Pseudomonas diminutis, and Mucor hachijoensis, with P. diminutis exhibiting the highest population density. Bacillus subtilis was isolated as a phosphate-solubilizing bacterium, confirming the digestate's potential for biofertilization. The coexistence of aerobic and anaerobic microbial species highlights the adaptability of digestate across diverse environmental conditions. These findings align with previous studies on the application of anaerobic digestate for biostimulation and bioaugmentation in contaminated soils and its role as a carrier for beneficial microbes in sustainable agriculture. The study contributes to the growing body of evidence supporting the valorization of organic waste via anaerobic digestion, offering a low-cost, eco-friendly solution to petroleum pollution and soil nutrient depletion. Future research should focus on quantifying the degradation and solubilization efficiencies of the isolated strains and exploring their genetic traits to enhance their performance and scalability under field conditions.

This study investigated the physicochemical properties and microbial diversity of digestate, focusing on its potential for hydrocarbon degradation and phosphate solubilization. Future research should focus on quantifying the degradation and solubilization efficiencies of the isolated strains and exploring their genetic traits to enhance their performance and scalability under field conditions.

papers.title: Evaluation of a Deep Q-Network with a Quadratic Reward Function for Two-Phase Traffic Signal Control
papers.abstract: Adaptive traffic signal control can respond to changing traffic demand more effectively than fixed-time operation, but deep reinforcement learning performance depends strongly on environment design, state representation, and reward formulation. This study evaluates a tuned Deep Q-Network (DQN) with a quadratic congestion penalty for two-phase traffic signal control. A dataset-driven environment paired two street segments as conflicting approaches and applied chronological training, validation, and test splits. No external microscopic traffic simulator was used; instead, the observed demand sequences drove a custom queue-based Gymnasium environment. Hyperparameters were tuned using the validation set, while final models were evaluated across three random seeds under normal, peak, incident, and imbalanced-demand scenarios. The quadratic DQN was compared with a linear-reward DQN, a fixed 50:50 controller, and a rule-based adaptive controller. Under normal traffic, the quadratic DQN achieved a mean queue of 22.16 vehicles, a 95th-percentile queue of 35.11 vehicles, throughput of 594.24 vehicles, and a service rate of 95.42%. Compared with the linear DQN, it reduced queue imbalance by 5.15% and action changes by 12.82%, although mean queue and throughput did not improve. The rule-based controller produced the best overall performance. These findings indicate that quadratic reward shaping can improve policy balance and stability, but simpler controllers may remain competitive when training data are limited. Fair baselines and multi-seed evaluation remain essential practices.

These findings indicate that quadratic reward shaping can improve policy balance and stability, but simpler controllers may remain competitive when training data are limited.

papers.title: Landslide Susceptibility and Runout Modelling Along the Karakoram Highway Using PS-InSAR and Hybrid CNN-LSTM–XGBoost
papers.abstract: The Karakoram Highway (KKH) traverses a tectonically active and climatically sensitive mountain corridor that is repeatedly affected by landslides. This study develops an integrated hybrid framework combining convolutional neural network–long short-term memory (CNN-LSTM) learning, extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), persistent-scatterer interferometric synthetic aperture radar (PS-InSAR), runout modelling, climate projections, and multi-hazard risk assessment along a 320-km section of the KKH in northwestern Pakistan. Eighteen topographic, hydrological, geological, climatic, anthropogenic, and geodetic conditioning factors were used. The CNN-LSTM was pre-trained on the NASA Cooperative Open Online Landslide Repository and fine-tuned using an inventory of 612 landslides, while class imbalance was addressed using SMOTE and focal loss. The stacked hybrid model achieved an AUC of 0.974, accuracy of 0.928, and Cohen’s κ of 0.856, outperforming standalone CNN-LSTM (AUC = 0.951) and XGBoost (AUC = 0.938) models. SHAP and Grad-CAM analyses identified slope, PS-InSAR line-of-sight velocity, annual rainfall, and elevation as the dominant controls. Flow-R and RAMMS simulations reproduced representative runout patterns with κ = 0.74. Under CMIP6 SSP5-8.5, high-to-very-high susceptibility is projected to increase from 24.0% at baseline to 35.2% by 2050 and 41.6% by 2100. The multi-hazard assessment further indicates that 23.7% of the highway lies within high-to-very-high composite risk zones. The framework provides an explainable, climate-sensitive, and operationally transferable basis for landslide-risk reduction along high-relief transport corridors.

The multi-hazard assessment further indicates that 23.7% of the highway lies within high-to-very-high composite risk zones.

papers.title: Liver transplantation for intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma: From contraindication to biology-driven selection
papers.abstract: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA) has historically been considered a contraindication to liver transplantation (LT) because early outcomes in unselected patients were marked by high recurrence and poor survival. Liver resection remains the standard curative-intent treatment when technically feasible and oncologically appropriate. Contemporary evidence challenges this binary view, suggesting that transplant benefit depends less on diagnosis or anatomy alone than on careful candidate selection and disease behavior over time. This narrative review examines LT for iCCA within current transplant oncology practice. Current evidence supports cautious consideration of LT in two distinct settings. The first is very early iCCA in cirrhotic patients, particularly solitary tumors ≤ 2 cm, for which explant-based retrospective studies have shown better outcomes than those observed in larger or multifocal disease. Evidence for this setting derives mainly from incidental or explant-based series. Selected solitary tumors ≤ 3 cm may be considered within consensus-based, guidance-based, trial-based, or registry-based frameworks after documented stability and exclusion of nodal or extrahepatic disease, although this threshold is less well validated than the 2-cm threshold. The second is unresectable, liver-limited iCCA controlled by neoadjuvant systemic therapy with or without locoregional therapy, where durable radiologic response or stability, usually for at least 6 months, serves as a dynamic test of disease behavior. Evidence for this setting derives from highly selected neoadjuvant cohorts and remains investigational. In both settings, histological confirmation when feasible, careful staging, and exclusion of nodal or extrahepatic spread are essential. LT should be framed not as routine indication expansion, but as a highly selective treatment strategy for patients with liver-limited disease and sustained disease control.

papers.title: POLÍMERO PEEK COMO ALTERNATIVA NA RETENÇÃO INTRARRADICULAR: UMA REVISÃO INTEGRATIVA DE LITERATURA
papers.abstract: The search for materials with improved biomechanical and aesthetic performance for intraradicular retainers has driven the investigation of high-performance polymers, such as polyetheretherketone (PEEK). This study aimed to evaluate the clinical feasibility of PEEK as an intraradicular post, comparing its mechanical, adhesive, and aesthetic properties with those of fiberglass posts. An integrative literature review with a qualitative approach was conducted, based on the PICO model criteria and adapted guidelines from the PRISMA protocol. The search was carried out in the PubMed, SciELO, and Google Scholar databases, using MeSH descriptors related to dental posts, biomechanical analysis, and restorative materials, including publications from 2013 to February 2025. A total of 25 articles addressing the use of PEEK in comparison to fiberglass posts were included. The data demonstrate that PEEK exhibits an elastic modulus similar to that of dentin, promoting more favorable stress distribution during mastication and resulting in potentially more reparable fractures. However, limitations remain regarding its adhesion to resin cements and aesthetic mimicry. It is concluded that, although PEEK shows promise as an alternative to conventional intraradicular retainers, further clinical studies are necessary to validate its application in diverse clinical scenarios. Keywords: Tooth fractures; Dental post; Polymers; PEEK; Restorative dentistry.

papers.title: Kinetic Analysis of the Combustion Reaction of Sub-Bituminous Coal Blended with Empty Fruit Bunch (EFB) Waste
papers.journal: Scientific Experiences in Energy and Thermal Engineering
papers.abstract: This study evaluated the effect of blending ratios of sub-bituminous coal and Empty Fruit Bunch (EFB) biomass on the activation energy (Eₐ) of the combustion process using Thermogravimetric Analysis (TGA) and the Coats–Redfern kinetic approach. The fuel samples consisted of 100% coal, 80% coal–20% EFB, and 60% coal–40% EFB blends. The results showed that the average activation energy during Stage I decreased from 91.16 kJ/mol for pure coal to 86.69 kJ/mol for the 20% EFB blend, before increasing to 91.64 kJ/mol for the 40% EFB blend. During Stage II, the activation energy decreased from 61.88 kJ/mol for pure coal to 48.70 kJ/mol for the 20% EFB blend, and then increased slightly to 49.50 kJ/mol for the 40% EFB blend. These findings indicate that the addition of 20% EFB produces a synergistic effect by enhancing the thermal reactivity of the fuel mixture, whereas increasing the EFB content to 40% results in a higher activation energy due to the greater complexity of lignin decomposition and the formation of an ash layer on the char surface. It can therefore be concluded that the 20% EFB blend represents the optimum co-firing ratio from a kinetic perspective.

papers.title: Utilization of the Refrigeration Effect from LPG Expansion for a Refrigerated Display Cabinet (RDC): An Experimental Study of a Half-Cycle System
papers.journal: Scientific Experiences in Energy and Thermal Engineering
papers.abstract: Energy demand for commercial refrigeration continues to rise alongside the global transition toward environmentally benign natural refrigerants, while conventional cooling systems for refrigerated display cabinets (RDCs) remain heavily dependent on electricity and synthetic refrigerants. This study investigates the utilization of the refrigeration effect arising from the pressure reduction of LPG (a propane-butane mixture) prior to combustion, known as a half-cycle refrigeration system, as an alternative cooling source for a small-scale (192 L) beverage RDC. Liquid LPG is expanded isenthalpically through an expansion valve into an evaporator placed inside the RDC, while the resulting LPG vapor is routed to a burner. Testing was conducted for 60 minutes with data logged at 1-minute intervals using PT100 RTD sensors, PSAN pressure transducers, and humidity sensors connected to an Autonics data acquisition system. Results show the system reaches quasi-steady state within ±10 minutes on the refrigerant side, with an actual cooling power of ±263 W based on the measured LPG mass flow rate (3.07 kg/h) and a specific refrigeration effect of ±309 kJ/kg. Although only ±1.23% of this cooling capacity was utilized as net RDC air energy reduction, indicating a substantial parasitic heat load from suboptimal insulation, the test RDC successfully reached the operating temperature range of commercial minimarket RDCs (5.4–8.3 °C, verified via thermal imaging) within the test duration. These findings thermodynamically demonstrate that the otherwise-wasted LPG refrigeration effect has potential as a supplementary (pre-cooling/auxiliary) cooling system for small-to-medium beverage RDCs, particularly for businesses that already consume LPG routinely, while pointing toward further research on insulation optimization and frost management for broader commercial application.

papers.title: Thermocatalytic transcarbonation with diethyl carbonate for valorization of glycerol : recycling siliceous bauxite residue waste components and exploring the potential of sodalite hydroxide reservoir
papers.journal: Repository of the Academy's Library (Library of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences)
papers.abstract: Bauxite residues contain katoites and desilication products (sodalite and cancrinite), which are excellent candidates for Earth-abundant heterogeneous base catalysts from industrial waste sources. For the first time, they were tested in synthetizing the renewable and promising fuel or fuel additive glycerol carbonate for the purpose of recycling glycerol by-products from biodiesel production. Incorporation of silicate was found to enhance the previously established excellent catalytic activity of tricalcium aluminate (Si-free katoite). Performance of sodalites containing four different cage anion-designed (OH, CO3, SO4, Cl) and carbonated cancrinite was determined to a much greater extent by their Brönsted OH content than by the basicity of the caged anions. Direct catalytic use of bauxite residue resulted in a glycerol carbonate yield of over 80%, but it was quickly deactivated due to the limited reusability of many of its most active components (i.e., Si-free and Si-containing katoites, chloride sodalites). However, hydroxysodalites showed excellent reusability, with a glycerol carbonate yield of around 80% even after 5 reuses. The activity of katoites and sodalities overtook that of many complex systems containing relatively rare metals, such as Ni, Cu, Zr, and Ce. Their excellent activity has made it possible to use diethyl carbonate solvent/reagent, which is more favourable in terms of sustainability, instead of the more widely applied dimethyl carbonate, even with as short reaction times as 30–60 min.

papers.title: Hypoxia-responsive supramolecular systems based on macrocycles and self-assembly structures.
papers.abstract: Hypoxia is closely associated with tumor progression, metastasis, therapeutic resistance, and diagnostic challenges. The timely detection of hypoxia in live cancer cells is critical for early cancer diagnosis and for monitoring the effectiveness of anticancer therapies. Recently, there has been growing interest in non-covalent supramolecular design strategies for the development of hypoxia-sensitive sensors and prodrugs. Unlike the widely employed covalent approach, supramolecular chemistry eliminates the need for complex and time-consuming synthetic processes. Instead, the individual components of the sensor autonomously self-assemble into the desired structure. This review provides an overview of hypoxia-targeted and hypoxia-activated supramolecular probes, along with their mechanisms of action in tumor diagnosis and therapy. The supramolecular systems considered are classified according to the use of certain classes of macrocycles. The role of macrocyclic derivatives in the various proposed approaches and the response patterns of hypoxic targets will also be analyzed. Various representatives of the macrocyclic platforms, namely cyclodextrins, cucurbiturils, pillararenes, (thia)calixarenes, due to their properties such as molecular recognition, are used as molecular containers-carriers for pharmaceuticals and bio-organic fluorescent dyes. As a result of complex formation, the photostability and the signal-to-noise ratio of dyes increase. In addition, the solubility of hydrophobic guests in water improves, cytotoxicity is reduced, and targeted delivery promotes the accumulation of drugs/dyes in tumor cells.

papers.title: Nitric oxide in the occurrence and development of ischemic cerebrovascular disease.
papers.abstract: Since nitric oxide is a chemically highly reactive free radical that can act as both an oxidizing agent and a reducing agent, it is assumed that it has diverse effects on biological tissues. Nitric oxide is fundamentally important for the regulation of immune, reproductive and neuromuscular system functions and is the main signaling molecule and effector that can dilate blood vessels and modulate energy metabolism. This review examines the key role of nitric oxide in the mechanisms underlying the response to hypoxia, as well as in the effects of factors induced by hypoxia. The available conflicting information allowed us to conclude that at present, there is no consensus about the role of endogenous nitric oxide in the processes occurring after ischemic cerebrovascular disease.

papers.title: Hyperbaric oxygen for the treatment of traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
papers.abstract: The therapeutic efficacy of hyperbaric oxygen therapy for traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury remains a subject of debate. To comprehensively evaluate the impact of hyperbaric oxygen on motor function, sensory function, and activities of daily living in patients with traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury, we conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis. We performed a comprehensive search across PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and major Chinese databases for randomized controlled trials published through June 2025. A total of 15 randomized controlled trials were included. The pooled results indicated that hyperbaric oxygen therapy significantly improved the American Spinal Injury Association motor score (mean difference = 10.30, 95% confidence interval: 7.70-12.90), the total American Spinal Injury Association sensory score (mean difference = 29.29, 95% confidence interval: 18.82-39.75), the American Spinal Injury Association light touch score (mean difference = 9.84, 95% confidence interval: 6.15-13.53), and the American Spinal Injury Association pinprick score (mean difference = 8.75, 95% confidence interval: 4.40-13.11). Furthermore, hyperbaric oxygen therapy was associated with significant enhancements in the Barthel Index (mean difference = 16.60, 95% confidence interval: 10.51-22.68) and the Functional Independence Measure (mean difference = 17.41, 95% confidence interval: 10.83-23.98). In conclusion, adjunctive hyperbaric oxygen therapy appears to improve motor function, sensory function, and activities of daily living in patients with traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury compared to conventional treatments alone. However, due to methodological limitations and potential publication bias in the included studies, these findings should be interpreted with caution, and further high-quality, multi-center randomized controlled trials are warranted.

papers.title: High levels of nitric oxide and peroxynitrite with protein nitration: a new therapeutic target for gliomas.
papers.abstract: The gap junction signaling pathway is a core hub mediating intercellular communication, which plays a vital role in maintaining tissue homeostasis, and its dysfunction is closely related to glioma. Nitroproteomics studies have shown that protein tyrosine nitration plays an important role in the progression of glioma, and gap junction is one of the significantly enriched nitroprotein signaling pathways in glioma; proteoformics reveals that nitration can produce various proteoforms of related proteins, which have different functional states in different subtypes of glioma, suggesting that nitration may alter the functional states of related proteins in gap junction pathways. When levels of nitric oxide and peroxynitrite (ONOO-) rise, they induce the tyrosine nitration of key proteins in the gap junction pathway; this nitration not only interferes with the function of the gap junction pathway, but also affects other gap junction-linked signaling networks. Forming an attack network on the gap junction pathway through multi-pathway cross-regulation has great potential for therapeutic strategies targeting the gap junction pathway. We recommend in-depth studies of the gap junction signaling pathway and potential drugs targeting gap junction signals, including drugs that target gap junction communication activators, nitration inhibitors, and drugs that directly target specific nitroproteins, combined with conventional chemotherapy or immune checkpoint inhibitors, as well as the construction of personalized medical frameworks as important future research directions.

papers.title: Semiparametric Inference for Functional Survival Models
papers.abstract: In recent years, there has been growing interest among researchers in modeling right-censored survival data with functional covariates.While existing functional methods primarily focus on the Cox model, its proportional hazards assumption can be challenging to verify and may be violated in practice.To address this issue, we extend the ordinary differential equation (ODE) framework for survival data to incorporate functional covariates and develop an inference procedure for both scalar and functional parameters.Specifically, we establish asymptotic normality and semiparametric efficiency for the scalar coefficient estimators, enabling a valid inference procedure.Additionally, we derive an asymptotic simultaneous confidence band for the functional parameter.Simulations are conducted to evaluate the finite sample performance of the proposed method.

papers.title: Improved WOA-Based Multilevel Resource Coordinated Scheduling Strategy for Active Distribution Network
papers.abstract: To address the operational complexity caused by the high proportion of new energy integration into distribution networks, a multilevel resource-coordinated operation strategy based on an improved whale optimization algorithm (improved WOA) is proposed for active distribution networks (ADNs). A bilevel optimization model is established to ensure the economic and safe operation of ADNs. The upper level is used to minimize the total system operation cost, while the lower level is used to optimize the power balance. Subsequently, the improved WOA, integrated with an adaptive weight and chaotic disturbance mechanisms, is used to solve the bilevel model and obtain a multi-resource coordinated operation strategy. This framework can help to enhance convergence and avoid local optima. In the simulation section, the IEEE 33-bus system is used to test the performance of the multilevel resource coordinated operation strategy. The simulation results reveal that the proposed approach can reduce the total system operation cost to 9.72 × 104 CNY. Moreover, the fossil fuel consumption of the diesel generator and the charging cost of electric vehicles are reduced by 15% and 18%, respectively. In addition, the power supply–demand matching accuracy is increased to 99.8%. Compared with the multi-element heuristic algorithm, the improved WOA shows significant superiority and robustness. This research provides an economical and stable multi-resource coordinated scheduling solution for distribution networks with a high proportion of renewable energy.
papers.summary: To address the operational complexity caused by the high proportion of new energy integration into distribution networks, a multilevel resource-coordinated operation strategy based on an improved whale optimization algorithm (improved WOA) is proposed for active distribution networks (ADNs). The simulation results reveal that the proposed approach can reduce the total system operation cost to 9.72 × 104 CNY. Compared with the multi-element heuristic algorithm, the improved WOA shows significant superiority and robustness.

papers.title: Interlaboratory Comparison Tests of Coal for Fuel and Energy Complex Enterprises
papers.abstract: The study focuses on four key indicators selected from eleven parameters characterizing hard coal quality. It presents and substantiates statistical approaches for processing the results of interlaboratory comparison testing, with particular attention to the assessment of sample homogeneity and stability. The stages of organizing and conducting interlaboratory comparisons are described, taking into account the specific features of fuel and energy sector enterprises. Selected statistical methods were applied to analyze coal quality indicators and to evaluate the reliability of the obtained measurement results. Based on the analysis, recommendations were developed to improve measurement procedures, enhance the interpretation of statistical outcomes, and increase the reliability and trueness of test results. The findings may be applied by fuel and energy enterprises in the validation and optimization of measurement procedures for hard coal quality indicators. The interlaboratory comparison involving 63 laboratories demonstrated that the measured values of gross calorific value (32225–32275 kJ/kg), volatile matter yield (11.558–11.73%), ash content (8.68–8.74%), and mass fraction of total sulfur (0.241–0.256%) are comparable and fall within permissible limits, with no outliers detected according to robust statistical analysis. These results confirm the homogeneity of the prepared coal samples and the reliability and consistency of the measurement procedures used by participating laboratories.

papers.title: Influence of Heat Treatment on Structure Density and Hardness of Al–Mg–Fe–Ni Alloys for High-Density Nuclear Applications
papers.abstract: The development of aluminum-based cladding materials for nuclear fuel confinement is advancing in line with the increasing demand for high-density fuels. Alloying aluminum with magnesium (Mg), iron (Fe), and nickel (Ni) is expected to improve mechanical strength and thermal stability, thereby compensating for the higher hardness associated with high-density fuels. Heat treatment is a proven strategy to further enhance the performance of Al-based alloys in nuclear applications. In this study, Al–Mg–Fe–Ni alloys were fabricated by arc melting, homogenized, rolled, and subjected to heat treatment at 500 °C for 1.5, 3, and 4.5 h. Structural analysis using XRD and GSAS confirmed the formation of a substitutional solid solution with partial preferred orientation. Heat treatment decreased hardness due to recovery and partial recrystallization, but increased bulk density. The sample treated for 1.5 h exhibited the best balance, with a hardness of 82.81± 0.06 HV and a density of 2.7232 ± 0.0002 g/cm³. These results demonstrate that controlled thermal treatment can be used to optimize the structure–property relationship of Al-based alloys, offering valuable insights for the design of advanced cladding materials for high-density nuclear fuels.
papers.summary: The development of aluminum-based cladding materials for nuclear fuel confinement is advancing in line with the increasing demand for high-density fuels. Heat treatment is a proven strategy to further enhance the performance of Al-based alloys in nuclear applications. These results demonstrate that controlled thermal treatment can be used to optimize the structure–property relationship of Al-based alloys, offering valuable insights for the design of advanced cladding materials for high-density nuclear fuels.

papers.title: Thermal and Economic Assessment of Cooling Technologies in a Combined Cycle Power Plant: A Case Study Bandar Abbas Hengam Power Plant
papers.abstract: The present study examined the Bandar Abbas Hengam combined cycle power plant (CCPP) equipped with a three-pressure heat recovery steam generator (HRSG) with reheat. Fogging and absorption chiller systems were used to improve power plant performance. The proposed power plant was simulated using the Thermoflow software and the GT PRO module. This research assessed the power plant’s thermal and economic performance in warm months (March–October), with and without cooling systems. The technical and economic simulation results were extracted using Thermoflow and COMFAR software. The energy analysis results indicated that the absorption chiller is the best alternative for boosting the power production capacity. However, the cycle without a cooling system was found to have the highest thermal efficiency. On the other hand, the economic analysis results demonstrated that the highest net present value (NPV) 638.27 Billion Rials ($1.06 Million) was obtained for the combined cycle with the absorption chiller cooling system, which also had an internal rate of return (IRR) of 43.65%. The next highest NPV 633.35 Billion Rials ($1.05 Million) was obtained for the combined cycle with the fogging cooling system, which had an IRR of 44.09%. Finally, the combined cycle without a cooling system had an NPV of 586.27 Billion Rials ($0.98 Million) and an IRR of 43.3%. Therefore, for short-term investment and quick returns, fogging is most economical due to its higher IRR. For long-term investment focused on maximizing net value, the absorption chiller is more viable.

papers.title: Investigation of Interdependencies in an Environmentally Sustainable Energy Generation System Utilizing Coalbed Methane: A Statistical Analysis Approach
papers.abstract: This paper presents a study analyzing the potential of coalbed methane as an alternative fuel source for power generation at thermal power plants in the Russian Federation. Statistical methods, including time series forecasting and multivariate correlation-regression analysis, are used to project fossil fuel demand trends in Russia's Unified Energy System (UES) through 2026. A comparative evaluation of pollutant emissions (CO₂, NOₓ, SO₂) associated with the utilization of coalbed methane, natural gas, coal, and fuel oil is conducted. Based on the developed models, performance of coalbed methane is substantiated. Practical recommendations for the modernization of power generation equipment are proposed, notably advocating for the transition from conventional steam boilers to advanced gas turbine units (e.g., GTD 110M), which enables a significant increase in thermal efficiency and a substantial reduction in harmful emissions.

papers.title: Autonomous Inflow Control Devices for Development of Oil Rims in Condensate Reservoirs
papers.abstract: The current stage of oil and gas industry development is characterized by the need for efficient field exploitation in challenging geological and technological conditions. In Russia, the majority of the growth in the oil resource base is primarily provided by hard-to-recover reserves associated with oil rims in gas-cap reservoirs underlain by aquifers. The small thickness of oil rims, significant oil reserves, and high reservoir heterogeneity in terms of permeability require mitigation of the risks of water and gas breakthrough to the bottomholes of producing oil wells during the optimization of the field development system. Breakthrough of unwanted fluids to producing wells has a significant impact on production stability and reduces the overall efficiency of developing oil rims with large reserves in contact reservoirs. In this regard, there is a need for modern technologies capable of controlling the inflow of target fluids and extending the water-free production period of wells. One of the promising solutions is the application of inflow control devices (ICDs), which enable regulation of the production profile, reduction of water cut, and minimization of gas breakthrough into producing oil wells.

papers.title: Balanced Risk Assessment and Management in Development of Hard-To-Recover Reserves Using Example of Heavy Oil
papers.abstract: Depletion of conventional oil fields and increasing requirements for the economic justification of investment projects enhance the significance of developing hard-to-recover reserves, including heavy oil, which is characterized by technological complexity, high energy intensity, and multifactor uncertainty. This study proposes a balanced risk assessment framework that integrates Monte Carlo simulation with a Mamdani-type fuzzy inference system. Quantitative project parameters are modeled as random variables, while poorly formalized geological, technical, operational, environmental, social, and political-regulatory risks are aggregated into an integral fuzzy risk index. The proposed framework is tested using open data for a heavy oil project and four integration variants: a baseline Monte Carlo model without fuzzy risk adjustment, a model with risk-adjusted mean values, a model with risk-adjusted standard deviations, and a combined model. The fuzzy inference system produced a high integral risk index, Rhtr = 0.782. In the baseline model, expected NPV was −1.79 billion USD and the probability of negative NPV was 66.52%. When the integral risk index was incorporated through shifts in expected values, expected NPV decreased to approximately −6.76 billion USD and the probability of negative NPV increased to 89.90%. The combined model produced a similar central shift, with expected NPV of −6.75 billion USD and P(NPV < 0) of 89.44%, while also reflecting increased distributional uncertainty. The results show that the main economic effect of integral risk is associated with systematic changes in expected CAPEX, OPEX, production rate, and decline rate, whereas variance-only adjustment has limited influence on central project metrics. The proposed approach provides a transparent tool for linking qualitative risk assessment with probabilistic economic evaluation and supports more conservative investment decision-making in heavy oil development projects.

papers.title: Ionic Transport Enhancement in Sodium Salt–Modified Graphene Oxide Solid Electrolytes
papers.abstract: Graphene oxide (GO)–based solid electrolytes offer a safer and more stable alternative to conventional liquid electrolytes for energy storage systems. This study examines the influence of sodium salt incorporation specifically sodium sulfite, sodium nitrate, and sodium chloride on the characteristic, thermal, and ionic transport properties of GO-based solid electrolytes. The solid electrolyte membranes were fabricated using the vacuum filtration method. X-ray Diffraction (XRD) analysis revealed an increase in the interlayer spacing of GO nanosheet after the addition of sodium salts. Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR) results indicated the occurrence of ring opening or the cleavage of C–O–C bonds into C–O–H bonds, suggesting enhanced oxidation through the conversion of epoxy groups into carbonyl groups. Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) images showed that the addition of sodium salts widened the interlayer spacing. Thermal analysis using Thermogravimetric Analysis (TGA) demonstrated that the membranes exhibited lower mass loss at each stage after the addition of sodium salts, indicating improved thermal stability compared to those without sodium salts. Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS) results confirmed an increase in ionic conductivity of GO-based solid electrolytes following sodium salt incorporation, with the highest conductivity of 4.07 × 10⁻⁴ S/cm observed for GO-NaCl at room temperature with a 20 wt.% concentration. These results demonstrate that controlled sodium salt modification promotes favorable ion–GO interactions, thereby enhancing ionic transport and improving the performance potential of GO-based solid electrolytes for energy storage applications.
papers.summary: Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR) results indicated the occurrence of ring opening or the cleavage of C–O–C bonds into C–O–H bonds, suggesting enhanced oxidation through the conversion of epoxy groups into carbonyl groups. Thermal analysis using Thermogravimetric Analysis (TGA) demonstrated that the membranes exhibited lower mass loss at each stage after the addition of sodium salts, indicating improved thermal stability compared to those without sodium salts. These results demonstrate that controlled sodium salt modification promotes favorable ion–GO interactions, thereby enhancing ionic transport and improving the performance potential of GO-based solid electrolytes for energy storage applications.

papers.title: Control of Acid-Base Surface Properties of Saponite by Targeted Modification with Cationic Surfactants
papers.abstract: This article presents a comprehensive study of saponite from the Arkhangelsk deposit and its organic modification. The crystal-chemical formula was calculated using chemical and thermogravimetric data. A three-dimensional structural model was constructed using VESTA to visualize the layered structure and cation distribution. Modification with dialkyldimethylammonium chloride (DADMAC) provided the highest hydrophobicity, with a contact angle of up to 87.66°, and the lowest interaction energy with hydrocarbons (0.031 J/m2). The Tanabe method revealed complete suppression of Lewis acid sites and an increase in Brønsted basic sites to 38.1% after DADMAC treatment. Textural analysis showed a significant increase in mesopore content (22.54–22.95%), and NMR spectroscopy revealed distinctive features of DADMAC-induced modification.

papers.title: Rights and Duties of Parents and Children with Emphasis on the Legal Systems of Iran and England
papers.journal: Journal of Historical Research Law and Policy
papers.abstract: Family law is one of the most important branches of civil law and plays a fundamental role in preserving the dignity, security, and welfare of family members, particularly children. Child maintenance, as one of the major duties of parents, holds a special legal and jurisprudential position, as it guarantees the provision of the child’s basic needs and healthy development. Using a comparative approach, this study examines the rights and duties of parents in the legal systems of Iran and England and analyzes the status of child maintenance from the perspective of Islamic jurisprudence and domestic laws. The comparative analysis indicates that, in both legal systems, the protection of children is of great importance; however, there are differences in the way parental duties and children’s rights are defined and enforced. In the Iranian legal system, jurisprudential and Sharia-based foundations play a key role in determining family rights and duties, whereas in the English legal system, greater emphasis is placed on the welfare of the child and international human rights law. By using the method of analyzing legal texts, international documents, and jurisprudential sources, the researcher identifies the strengths and weaknesses of each system. The findings show that strengthening protective legislation and promoting legal education can be an effective step toward guaranteeing children’s rights and ensuring the proper fulfillment of parental duties.

papers.title: A decadal analysis of land surface temperature dynamics in response to urban expansion and vegetation loss in Faridpur
papers.abstract: Land-atmosphere interactions, urban thermal environments, and the impacts of land-use and land-cover (LULC) alterations are effectively grasped through the precise measurement of land surface temperature (LST). In this work, Landsat-8 OLI/TIRS imagery from 2014 and 2024 was utilized to track ten-year variations in LST and plant health across Faridpur District of Bangladesh. Supervised classification was used to categorize the landscape into four specific LULC categories: vegetation, bare soil, built-up areas, and water bodies. Each examined year featured calculations for both LST and the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI). Between 2014 and 2024, a massive urban expansion from 21.35% to 45.25% was recorded. Conversely, total vegetated area was reduced from 41.09% down to 25.87% over the same timeframe. A widespread surface warming pattern was clearly established by the thermal metrics. Specifically, the regional maximum LST increased from 42.69 °C to 45.33 °C, alongside a minimum LST increase from 15.55 °C to 21.31 °C. The deterioration of thick ecological canopies was signaled by a drop in peak NDVI scores from 0.999 to 0.883 over the past decade. Built-up and bare-soil surfaces primarily showed the highest LST values, according to spatial mapping. Meanwhile, cooler microclimates were sustained by water-covered zones and vegetated patches. These outcomes highlight the urgency of conserving green cover in Faridpur. Moreover, establishing small-scale urban green areas in the rapidly expanding towns and cities across the region is necessary to counteract the thermal consequences of ongoing urbanization.

Moreover, establishing small-scale urban green areas in the rapidly expanding towns and cities across the region is necessary to counteract the thermal consequences of ongoing urbanization.

papers.title: Performance Degradation Mechanisms and Mitigation Strategies for PEM Fuel Cell Systems in High-Altitude Environments
papers.abstract: As proton exchange membrane fuel cell systems are increasingly considered for transportation and stationary power applications in high-altitude regions, their performance degradation under low-pressure and oxygen-deficient environments has become a critical barrier to practical deployment. This review summarizes the key mechanisms responsible for PEMFC performance loss under high-altitude conditions, including reduced oxygen partial pressure, aggravated activation and concentration polarization, increased compressor load, and decreased system net power. Recent progress is reviewed from the perspectives of stack materials and components, air supply subsystems, system integration, control strategies, and energy management. Particular attention is given to catalyst-layer design, bipolar plate flow-field optimization, high-pressure-ratio air compressors, turbine-assisted energy recovery, oxygen excess ratio control, and net-power optimization. The analysis indicates that the major technical challenges for high-altitude PEMFC operation are no longer limited to stack materials, but are strongly associated with the coupled optimization of air supply, flow-field design, compressor operating boundaries, and altitude-adaptive control. Future research should therefore focus on integrated material–stack–system testing platforms, long-term field validation, and predictive models that couple degradation mechanisms with system-level control. This review provides a systematic reference for the design and optimization of PEMFC systems for high-altitude applications.

papers.title: Location‐Allocation Optimization of Residential Photovoltaic Systems with Local Energy Sharing
papers.abstract: Residential buildings, due to their considerable share of total energy consumption and the availability of rooftop space for photovoltaic installations, represent a significant opportunity for deploying clean energy solutions. The emergence of peer-to-peer energy trading among neighboring buildings further enhances this potential by enabling the exchange of surplus PV generation. To promote residential Photovoltaic systems, governments often allocate annual budgets and establish long-term contracts with private companies for photovoltaic installations. Within this framework, contractors play a key role in selecting suitable buildings and maximizing project profitability under budget constraints. This paper presents a mixed-integer linear programming optimization model for selecting residential buildings suitable for photovoltaic installation and for selling surplus electricity to neighboring buildings. The objective is to maximize the contractor’s profit within a peer-to-peer energy trading framework. In addition to selecting suitable buildings and allocating neighboring consumer buildings, the proposed model determines the optimal sizes of photovoltaic systems and batteries so that generation and consumption are managed efficiently. The problem is formulated within the framework of a government-funded contracting scheme and is evaluated using real-world data from Yazd, Iran. The results demonstrate that integrating peer-to-peer energy trading with battery storage increases the contractor’s profitability and facilitates more effective utilization of locally generated PV electricity through local energy sharing.

papers.title: Numerical Analysis of Heat Transfer of Nanofluid Flow in Circular Cavity: Effects of Reynolds and Richardson Numbers
papers.abstract: Flow inside circular cavities with a barrier in the middle has not been studied much for hybrid nanofluids, especially when the flow changes from laminar to turbulent. This work looks at how the Reynolds number (1000, 2000, and 3000) and the Richardson number (0.01 and 0.10) affect heat transfer and flow behaviour of a SiO₂-CuO-water hybrid nanofluid inside such a cavity. The finite element method is used to solve the unsteady equations over 20 seconds. What makes this study novel is that it looks at both the change from laminar to turbulent flow and the mixed convection effect together in this particular setup. The results show that when the Richardson number goes up, the fluid moves faster. When the Reynolds number goes up, the horizontal speed increases a bit but the vertical speed slightly drops. At the highest Reynolds number, the warm region spreads more than the hottest isotherms. The best heat transfer happens when Richardson number is 0.10, and among all cases, the highest Nusselt number belongs to Re = 3000.

papers.title: MnO2/Co3O4 COMPOSITE ELECTRODES FOR POTENTIAL SUPERCAPACITOR APPLICATIONS
papers.abstract: As the global energy landscape shifts toward more sustainable and high-performance storage solutions, the development of next-generation supercapacitor electrodes has become increasingly critical. Addressing this demand, we developed a straightforward chemical co-precipitation method to synthesize manganese dioxide (MnO2) and cobalt oxide (Co3O4), incorporating a conductive carbon framework as a potential electrode material for supercapacitors. The resulting mixture was further combined with poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) (PEDOT) and deposited onto a nickel foam/graphene monolayer substrate to fabricate test electrodes. This method bypasses the complexity of multi-step fabrication and post-processing, offering a streamlined, scalable approach to building multifunctional hybrid electrodes. The resulting composite exhibits rapid ion transport and enhanced charge storage, while Energy-Dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) confirmed the successful incorporation of Mn and Co elements. Furthermore, X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns indicated that the composite possesses an amorphous structure. Cyclic Voltammetry (CV) and Galvanic Charge/Discharge (GCD) measurements revealed excellent long-term cycling stability, indicating the viability of the fabricated composite for potential supercapacitor applications. Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS) was also performed to evaluate the internal resistance and charge-transfer properties, providing complementary insight into the electrode’s electrochemical behavior.

papers.title: SYNTHESIS AND CHARACTERIZATION OF Co+2, Ni+2, Cu+2 and Cd+2 COMPLEXES WITH (4-(TERT-BUTYL) BENZENETHIOL) ALKANE LIGANDS AND EVALUTION OF ITS BIOLOGICAL ACTIVITY
papers.abstract: The research demonstrates that thioether-based coordination complexes obtain their physicochemical properties and biological activity from both the metal ion type and the ligand molecular structure. The synthesized complexes showed tetrahedral coordination geometries, as evidenced by spectroscopic, magnetic, and conductivity measurements, which demonstrated that sulfur atoms function as the main donor sites. The behavior follows the soft donor–soft acceptor interaction framework, which allows the creation of stable metal–sulfur chemical bonds. The biological properties of metal coordination compounds produced better antibacterial effects than the unbound ligands. The improved results stem from two factors: enhanced lipophilicity after chelation, which enables better cell membrane penetration by bacteria, and decreased metal ion polarity due to electron delocalization within the chelate ring structure. The complexes become more accessible to the cell through these combined effects. The Ni(II) complex derived from ligand L1 exhibited the most effective antibacterial activity against both bacterial species. The d⁸ electronic configuration of Ni(II) leads to enhanced activity because it produces the best possible match between structural stability and electronic flexibility when the metal center binds to a tetrahedral coordination site. The compound shows better biological performance because its L1 structure contains a short ethylene bond, which produces a compact molecular arrangement that improves metal-sulfur bonding through its optimized metal-ligand electronic interactions. The research shows that thioether metal complexes exhibit antibacterial properties because their electronic structure interacts with their coordination and ligand structures in a combined manner, leading to the development of biologically active metal-based compounds.

papers.title: ELECTROCHEMICAL SYNTHESIS OF NANOMAGNETITE MODIFIED WITH BIOCOMPATIBLE SURFACTANTS
papers.abstract: Magnetic nanoparticles are currently gaining significant attraction in various fields, including modern engineering and ecology, particularly in biomedical, therapeutic, and diagnostic technologies. An environmentally friendly electrochemical synthesis method was used to produce magnetic nanoparticles. Iron sulfate was dissolved in a mixture of water-ethanol, while polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) was used to enhance the biocompatibility of the magnetite nanoparticles. Particle size in a sol obtained with 1 vol% PVP, at a current density of 20-60 A/dm2, and at varying water and ethanol ratios, was measured using the dynamic light scattering (DLS) method transmission electron microscopy (TEM). Zeta potential was measured to determine the stability of the magnetite sol. In the presence of PVP, the best results (12-18 nm) were obtained with water/ethanol ratios of 50/50 and 60/40 vol.%. Magnetite nanoparticles were characterized using a Zetasizer Malvern instrument, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), and thermogravimetric analysis.

papers.title: EVALUATION OF CALCIUM AMMONIUM NITRATE MODIFIED WITH POTASSIUM CHLORIDE: APPLICATION AND CONSUMER PROPERTIES
papers.abstract: Potassium-calcium-ammonium nitrate samples were obtained by varying the amounts of dolomite mineral (DM) and potassium chloride (KCl) from 0.5 to 25 g per 100 g of ammonium nitrate (AN) melt. The carbonate-chloride-nitrate melt was granulated by the prilling method. At 170 °C, the nitrate melt activated the dolomite mineral, converting CaO and MgO into plant-available forms. The simultaneous addition of DM and KCl significantly improved the mechanical strength of the fertilizer granules while reducing caking, porosity, and diesel fuel absorbency by a factor of 2–3 compared with AN granules containing magnesite. The optimal composition (AN:DM:KCl=100:12:12) was characterized by EDS, SEM, and DTA analyses, which confirmed its favorable structural and physicochemical properties. These findings demonstrate the potential of NKCaMg as a mechanically stable and agronomically effective fertilizer formulation.

papers.title: A THEORETICAL INVESTIGATION OF NITROBENZENE HYDROGENATION: GASPHASE, SOLVENT EFFECTS, AND Pd CATALYSIS
papers.abstract: This study presents a comprehensive density functional theory (DFT) investigation into the stepwise reduction of nitrobenzene to aniline via nitroso and hydroxylamine intermediates. Two mechanistic pathways were explored: a non-catalyzed route in both gas and ethanol phases and a surface-catalyzed route facilitated by a palladium (Pd) catalyst. Geometry optimizations, thermodynamic parameters, frontier molecular orbital (FMO) analysis, and vibrational frequency (IR) simulations were carried out for all key species involved: nitrobenzene (Ph-NO₂), nitrosobenzene (Ph-NO), phenylhydroxylamine (Ph-NHOH), and aniline (Ph-NH₂). A comparison of gas-phase and solvent-phase geometries revealed solvent-induced elongation of N–O and N–H bonds, particularly in polar intermediates, consistent with ethanol’s stabilizing effect. FMO analysis showed a notable decrease in HOMO–LUMO energy gaps in the solvent phase, indicating enhanced reactivity. IR spectra further supported these findings, with observable shifts in characteristic stretching frequencies upon solvation. In the Pd-catalyzed pathway, adsorption of reactants and intermediates on the Pd surface significantly altered molecular geometries and lowered reaction energy barriers. Calculated adsorption energies and bond elongations suggest strong Pd–O and Pd–N interactions that facilitate bond activation. The overall energy profile indicates a smoother and more favorable reduction pathway on the Pd surface compared to the noncatalyzed routes. These results provide mechanistic insight into the catalytic role of Pd in hydrogenation reactions and highlight the importance of solvent effects in modulating electronic and structural properties. This comparative approach enhances our understanding of nitroarene reductions and offers valuable guidance for catalyst design and process optimization.

The overall energy profile indicates a smoother and more favorable reduction pathway on the Pd surface compared to the noncatalyzed routes. These results provide mechanistic insight into the catalytic role of Pd in hydrogenation reactions and highlight the importance of solvent effects in modulating electronic and structural properties.

papers.title: ONE-STEP ELECTROGENERATED MANGANESE OXIDE/CARBON COMPOSITE ASPOTENTIAL ELECTRODE MATERIAL FOR PSEUDO-SUPERCAPACITORS
papers.abstract: The increasing demand for energy worldwide has led to the development of supercapacitors, which are energy storage devices known for their high-power density, quick charging and discharging capabilities, large capacity, long lifespan, and environmental benefits. Here, we discuss the method for synthesizing manganese oxide/carbon composite materials through a one-step electrolysis process for potential application as supercapacitive electrode materials. The deposition of manganese oxide on graphite, together with the exfoliation of carbon flakes from the graphite electrodes induced by gas evolution during water electrolysis, led to the electrogeneration of a manganese oxide–carbon composite powder. After investigation of physical properties, the powder of manganese oxides/carbon composite was coated onto planar indium tin oxide (ITO) electrodes. Evaluation of the electrochemical performance and charge storage capacity revealed that ITO electrodes modified with the electrogenerated composite exhibited superior electrochemical performance compared with those modified only with a physical mixture of manganese oxide and carbon nanotubes.

papers.title: A Digital Borsa (Stock Exchange) for Grain: Epistemic Infrastructure, Competition Law, and the Reconstitution of Market Legibility in EU and BRICS Commodity Governance
papers.journal: European Journal of Privacy Law & Technologies
papers.abstract: Transnational grain trade is indispensable to food security yet structurally resistant to legal visibility. Price-relevant facts, contractual risk allocations, and informational architectures are frequently constituted through private infrastructures, limiting their legibility to public authorities and non-incumbent market participants. The resulting governance embodies a private-law problem of market memory. Embracing an EU and BRICS+ perspective, this article defends the thesis of a digitally engineered “borsa” (stock exchange) as a hybrid institutional infrastructure enabling fairness through structured legibility; a competition-law and private-law architecture, not merely a transparency instrument, producing a shareable evidentiary substrate for markets reliant on private contractual memory, documentary finance and platform-based data accumulation.

papers.title: Mechanical and Electrical Characterization of Hybrid Polymer Composites Reinforced with Natural and Synthetic Fibers
papers.abstract: This study examines the effects of optimized stacking sequences and NaOH surface treatment on the mechanical and dielectric performance of hybrid polyester composites reinforced with natural fibers (flax, sisal) and synthetic fibers (carbon, glass). Twelve laminates were fabricated using hand lay-up technique to assess hybridization effects on strength, insulation, and cost efficiency. Results revealed that the all-carbon six-layer laminate achieved the highest tensile strength (86 MPa), while the optimized hybrid [2 Carbon/2 Flax/2 Carbon] retained 85% of this strength at 40% lower material cost. Alkali-treated flax laminates exhibited a 93% improvement over untreated samples, confirming enhanced fiber–matrix interfacial bonding. A semi-empirical model based on a modified rule of mixtures predicted tensile strength within an 8% error margin, validating its reliability for hybrid systems. Natural fiber composites showed elevated dielectric constants (ε′ = 9.5 at 0.5 kHz), indicating excellent insulation capability. The integrated experimental, theoretical, and microstructural analyses propose an economical pathway toward developing lightweight, multifunctional composites for aerospace, marine, and electrical insulation applications.

papers.title: A Hybrid Eulerian-Lagrangian Probability Model for Predicting Paraffin Deposits in Ball Valves During High-Paraffin Oil Transportation
papers.abstract: This paper develops a hybrid Eulerian-Lagrangian probabilistic model for predicting asphaltene-resin-paraffin deposit (ARPD) formation in ball valves. A new approach to describing the deposition process is proposed, in which the carrier phase ( highly paraffin oil) is specified by an analytical velocity field, and the dispersed phase is modeled by an ensemble of particles. The key element of the study is the probabilistic function of particle adhesion to the wall, which takes into account three factors: oil supercooling relative to the wax onset temperature (WAT), the distance to the wall, and the local flow velocity. A particle recirculation algorithm is implemented, ensuring the preservation of the total particle number and the statistical significance of the ensemble throughout the simulation. A series of computational experiments showed that the model correctly reproduces the threshold nature of paraffin deposits (deposition begins only at T < WAT ) and allows observing the three-phase dynamics of the narrowing of the flow area. The model revealed that the most intense fouling occurs not in the narrowest cross-section of the ball valve, but in the adjacent transition zones ("seats"), which is explained by hydrodynamic conditions. The model was verified, confirming that the boundary conditions for no-flow are met and particles remain in the system.

papers.title: A Machine Learning Approach for Cassava Leaf Disease Identification Using Constraint-Regularized Neural Networks and AJFO Meta-Optimization
papers.abstract: Early diagnosis of cassava leaf diseases is paramount to enhance the productivity of cassava and to support sustainable agriculture. Traditional deep learning methods, however, are not very robust in complex field conditions, suffer from manual hyperparameter tuning, and are not fully leveraging the structural information from the disease, which leads to poor classification accuracy and poor generalization. To cope with these challenges, this paper proposes a unified machine learning framework for cassava leaf disease identification, which combines with enhanced image preprocessing, Residual Multi-scale U-Net (RMUNet) segmentation, Multi-Level Feature Extraction (MLFE), Constraint-Regularized Neural Network (CRNN), and Artificial Jellyfish Optimization (AJFO). The proposed approach is different from the conventional RMUNet-based disease detection techniques, which involve disease-oriented multiscale segmentation along with structural regularization in feature space to enhance the classification resilience in the presence of illumination variations, background clutter, and noisy farming ground. Moreover, AJFO uses to tune the learning rate, batch size, dropout rate, training epochs, and regularization coefficient in an automatic way, which removes the manual tuning of these parameters and increases the stability of convergence. A computational complexity analysis also shows that the extra cost of optimization is only during offline training, and inference complexity is comparable to the conventional deep learning models. Experimental results on the Cassava Leaf Disease dataset show the effectiveness of the proposed framework with 99% classification accuracy for healthy leaves, 97% classification accuracy for Cassava Mosaic Disease (CMD), 95% classification accuracy for Cassava Green Mite (CGM), and 93% classification accuracy for Cassava Brown Streak Disease (CBSD) and consistently better precision, recall, and F1-score than CNN-PLDD, SVM-PLDD, and DENN-PLDD. Overall, the proposed integrated framework demonstrates its capability of achieving effective convergence, better generalization performance, and effective disease classification performance under different imaging conditions, which is considered as a strong solution for intelligent precision agriculture and automated crop health monitoring.

papers.title: Adsorption Performance of Cationic and Anionic Dyes Using a UiO-66COOH@GO Composite: Synergistic and Competing Effects in Multicomponent Adsorption
papers.abstract: The discharge of dye-contaminated wastewater poses a serious environmental challenge because of the persistence and toxicity of synthetic dyes. A UiO-66COOH@GO composite was synthesized by grafting graphene oxide onto solvothermally prepared UiO-66COOH at an optimized ratio and characterized by FESEM, BET, FTIR, TGA, and elemental analyses. The optimized composite was used to remove methyl orange (MO), an anionic dye, methylene blue (MB), a cationic dye, and their binary mixture. Solution pH was the key factor governing adsorption, with maximum capacities of 98.9 mg/g for MB at pH 8 and 57.4 mg/g for MO at pH 3. Equilibrium analysis revealed that the Langmuir–Freundlich and BET isotherms provided the best interpretation for MB and MO adsorption, respectively. The Avrami model well described the adsorption kinetics for both dyes. In binary MB/MO systems, synergistic effects enhanced MB adsorption, whereas competitive effects led to a reduction in MO uptake. These findings demonstrate that the UiO-66COOH@GO composite is an effective adsorbent for the simultaneous removal of cationic and anionic dyes, benefiting from the high aspect ratio of GO and the abundant functional groups of UiO-66COOH.

papers.title: Automated Indentation Geometry Detection for Hardness Measurement: A Vision-Based Nondestructive Evaluation Approach
papers.abstract: Hardness testing is one of the most widely applied methods for evaluating the mechanical properties of metallic materials in manufacturing and quality control. Among standardized techniques, Brinell, Vickers, and Rockwell are most commonly used, all relying on precise measurement of indentation geometry. However, conventional evaluation methods still depend on manual or semi-automated readings, which are prone to operator error and unsuitable for industrial automation. This study introduces an automated framework for indentation geometry detection and measurement using two complementary strategies: a classical image processing pipeline based on OpenCV and a YOLOv10n deep learning model. To replicate realistic industrial conditions, St37 steel blocks with unpolished, roughly machined surfaces and random markings were tested under Brinell, Vickers, and Rockwell A hardness standards. A batch of microscope images was gathered, manually annotated, and subsequently expanded via data augmentation to obtain a diverse and reliable labeled image set. The classical pipeline employed brightness enhancement, thresholding, morphological filtering, and contour-based geometry extraction, while YOLOv10n was trained on the augmented dataset and refined using geometry-based post-processing. The YOLOv10n model achieved a mean average precision (detection accuracy) of 94% and reduced mean absolute error by 42–51% compared with classical image processing (p < 0.05). Furthermore, it maintained 96–97% accuracy under brightness variation, rotation, and mirroring, whereas the classical approach deteriorated to 79–84%. YOLOv10n provides a robust, precise, and scalable solution for automated hardness testing, supporting the advancement of automation in industrial quality control.

papers.title: Prediction of Structural Defects During Solidification of Al-Si-Mg Alloy System by Scheil-Gulliver Method
papers.abstract: This study applies Scheil-Gulliver non-equilibrium solidification modeling, implemented in ProCAST 13.5.2 with the AlDATA 4.2 thermodynamic database, to predict defect-promoting intermetallic phase formation in an AlSi9Mg alloy (Si 9.2, Mg 0.45, Ni 0.19, Fe 0.2, Mn 0.3 wt.%) derived from automotive scrap remelting in Cuba. The model predicts solidification between 597 and 533 °C a 65 °C non-equilibrium window with a phase formation sequence that places brittle Al3Ni needles first, followed by Mg2Si and the π-phase (Al8FeMg3Si6) during eutectic arrest at ~558 °C. Predicted phase fractions reach 0.022, 0.081, and 0.048 wt.% respectively. All representing upper-bound estimates under the no-back-diffusion assumption. Computed thermophysical properties showed that thermal conductivity dropped 67 W/m·K across the solidification interval, while density decreased by 200 kg/m³, both critical inputs for shrinkage-porosity prediction. The Mn/Fe ratio of 1.5 in this alloy suppresses the formation of β-Al5FeSi in favor of less detrimental Al15(Fe, Mn)3Si2, a result the model captures without additional fitting parameters. Practical thresholds for Ni content, Mg/Si ratio, and cooling rate control are derived from the simulation and validated against published experimental data for comparable alloy systems. The results demonstrate that Scheil-Gulliver modeling with industrial-grade thermodynamic databases provides actionable guidance for secondary aluminum foundry operations where compositional variability is inherent.

papers.title: Analysis the Characteristics and Performance of Polyethersulfone-Carbon Nanotube Membranes Fabricated Using Electric Field Method for Water Filtration Applications
papers.abstract: This study aims to address the effect of Carbon Nanotube (CNT) addition on the characteristics and performance of polyethersulfone (PES) membranes fabricated using the Electric Field method. Four PES membranes were fabricated with addition of CNT and denoted as SM0 (0% CNT), SM1 (0.5% CNT), SM2 (1% CNT), and SM3 (1.5% CNT). SEM observations showed average pore sizes of 0.62±0.12 μm to 0.82±0.18 μm, and AFM images showed the ability of CNTs to increase topographical complexity. The tensile test results indicated that addition of CNT increased the tensile strength of the membrane. The TGA and DTG test graphs showed that addition of CNT can increase the thermal resistance of the membrane. FTIR spectra were in agreement with characteristic PES functional groups. The XRD data showed that the amorphous nature remains dominant, indicating that this composite membrane successfully combines the mechanical strength and functional properties of CNTs without sacrificing the intrinsic pore structure of the PES polymer. Addition of CNT to the membrane increased its hydrophilicity, as evidenced by decrease in water contact angle on the membrane. Addition of CNT can also increase the membrane permeability, as indicated by an increase in the membrane permeability values in the range of 1 to 6 bar. In terms of durability, adding CNT to the membrane can increase its durability, meaning that membranes with added CNT can last longer than pure PES membranes.

papers.title: Optimizing Cooling Mode Switchovers in Green Data Centers via a SC Metric and TRNSYS-PSO Simulation
papers.abstract: Driven by the demand for green and efficient data center cooling, this study develops a rack-level rear-door heat pipe (RDHP) cooling system and proposes a comprehensive metric SC by integrating Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE), Water Usage Effectiveness (WUE), Carbon Usage Effectiveness (CUE), and scoring components from the Chinese green data center standard GB/T 44989-2024. Optimizing the switchover between free, hybrid, and mechanical cooling modes is critical for improving the energy efficiency and reducing the carbon footprint of data centers. A delimiting temperature (Tdelimit) of 17°C was established to optimally balance enhanced free cooling utilization with operational safety, ensuring server inlet temperatures remained within the limits. The switchover temperatures were optimized for four climatically diverse Chinese cities using TRNSYS simulations coupled with the GenOpt tool and a Particle Swarm Optimization algorithm. Results show that SC-oriented optimization effectively prolongs free cooling duration, reduces PUE, WUE, and CUE simultaneously, and outperforms empirical temperature settings. Also, the SC metric presents higher sensitivity than single indicators, while its optimization remains stable under varying grid carbon emission factors. This work provides a valuable methodology and a practical tool for advancing the green and low-carbon transformation of data centers, offering significant implications for policy-making and sustainable infrastructure planning.

papers.title: Energy Portfolios and Food Security in Developing Countries: A Water–Energy–Food Nexus Analysis Using Panel Smooth Transition Regression
papers.abstract: Agricultural production, processing and distribution in developing countries are energy-intensive, so the composition of the electricity generation portfolio is a plausible determinant of both food prices and physical supply security. The existing evidence, however, represents energy through aggregated indicators, analyses price and supply security separately, and assumes linearity, leaving open which generation technologies matter and under what conditions. This study therefore estimates six technologies—nuclear, geothermal, hydropower, solar, wind and biomass—jointly against both food outcomes within one nonlinear panel framework. The dataset combines IEA, IRENA, FAOSTAT and World Bank indicators for 82 developing economies over 2000–2023. Estimation uses Panel Smooth Transition Regression (PSTR) with energy intensity as the transition variable, supported by dynamic panel system-GMM and common correlated effects (CCE) estimators and by a compositional-data robustness specification based on the centred log-ratio transformation. Linearity is rejected and a single energy-intensity threshold is estimated at 0.436, with a transition speed of 7.84. Above that threshold, biomass generation is positively associated with food prices (0.067) and negatively with supply security (−0.055), whereas the continuously dispatchable sources—nuclear (−0.081) and geothermal (−0.094)—are negatively associated with price pressure and positively with supply security. Solar and wind attain significance only in the high regime, and the hydropower relationship reverses sign between low- and high-water-stress subsamples. Because the panel is observational and generation shares may be jointly determined with food outcomes, the coefficients are interpreted throughout as regime-dependent conditional relationships rather than causal effects. For policy, the findings imply that the generation portfolio should be planned jointly with water resources, grid integration and rural electrification rather than steered by a single aggregated renewable-energy target: biomass incentives warrant feedstock-origin conditionality, hydropower requires seasonal allocation rules where water stress is high, and variable renewables deliver food-security value mainly when paired with storage and irrigation-linked distribution.

papers.title: Uncertainty Quantification of Energy Extraction in a Process of Carbon Sequestration in Fractured Reservoirs: A Coupled Heat Transfer Phase Transport Study
papers.abstract: Injecting CO2 into depleted oil and gas reservoirs is a cost-effective method for geological CO2 sequestration as these reservoirs commonly possess proven capacity and sealing structures, and require lower exploration costs. The extracted brine can also be utilized for various thermal purposes. The presence of both natural and induced fractures in depleted oil and gas reservoirs can significantly impact their capacity for CO2 sequestration and thermal exploitation. Accurate simulation of the multi-phase transport and heat transfer resulting from CO2 injection requires a clear definition of properties for both the fracture and porous media. However, estimation of these properties, especially those of fractures, can be challenging and subject to significant uncertainty. This paper evaluates the extent to which uncertainty in fracture and matrix parameters affects simulated flow and transport results and the associated CO2 sequestration and geothermal energy extraction metrics. This is done through Monte Carlo-based uncertainty propagation analysis and Sobol-based global sensitivity analysis. Polynomial chaos expansions are used to analyze continuous changes of response variables with variations in the input parameters within a reasonable computational time. The effect of uncertainty in fracture length, aperture and rotation angle, longitudinal and transverse dispersivity, reservoir permeability and anisotropy, and the van Genuchten-Mualem parameters are assessed. Based on the results, these parameters are ranked according to their influence on the mass of stored CO2, reservoir heat loss, brine-based heat flux in the production well, and a measure of the CO2 travel time.

papers.title: A COMPREHENSIVE REVIEW ON NON-NEWTONIAN FLUIDS IN POROUS MEDIA UNDER LTNE MODEL
papers.journal: Advances and Applications in Fluid Mechanics
papers.abstract: The study of non-Newtonian fluid flow and heat transfer in porous media under local thermal non-equilibrium (LTNE) conditions has become an important interdisciplinary research area due to its applications in geothermal systems, enhanced oil recovery, biomedical engineering, polymer processing, thermal insulation, catalytic reactors, energy storage devices, and chemical industries. Unlike Newtonian fluids, non-Newtonian fluids exhibit complex rheological characteristics such as viscoelasticity, shear thinning, shear- thickening, yield stress, and microstructural effects. Simultaneously, the classical local thermal equilibrium (LTE) assumption often fails in practical porous systems involving high heat fluxes, low porosity, rapid thermal transients, or large thermal conductivity differences between fluid and solid phases. Consequently, LTNE models employing separate energy equations for the fluid and solid phases provide a more realistic thermal framework. This review presents a detailed and critical survey of the existing literature on non-Newtonian fluids in porous media under LTNE conditions. The review discusses major rheological fluid models including Maxwell, Oldroyd-B, Jeffrey, Casson, power-law, micropolar, couple-stress, Williamson, Carreau, and nano-fluid models. The effects of visco-elasticity, anisotropy, magnetic fields, rotation, chemical reactions, double diffusion, internal heat generation, and Darcy-Brinkman corrections on convective instability and heat transfer are extensively analyzed. Analytical, numerical, and experimental approaches are summarized, and the role of important parameters such as conductivity ratio, Darcy number, interphase heat transfer coefficient, relaxation parameter, porosity, and thermal anisotropy is discussed in depth. Current challenges and future research opportunities are also identified.

The effects of visco-elasticity, anisotropy, magnetic fields, rotation, chemical reactions, double diffusion, internal heat generation, and Darcy-Brinkman corrections on convective instability and heat transfer are extensively analyzed. Current challenges and future research opportunities are also identified.

papers.title: Three-Dimensional Thermomechanical Analysis of Radial Friction Welding of Dissimilar Copper-Aluminum Alloys: Finite Element Modelling and Experimental Validation
papers.abstract: This study investigates radial friction welding of dissimilar AA2024 aluminum and Cu-DHP copper using a three-dimensional finite element model together with optical metallography, Vickers microhardness measurements, and thermocouple measurements. A coupled thermomechanical model was implemented in ANSYS Workbench 2023 R1 at 1 400 rpm and 30 MPa. The numerical solution predicts an asymmetric thermal field with a maximum of 750 °C at the Al-Cu interface, an equivalent plastic strain of 0.0177 mm/mm, and a maximum total displacement of 0.130 mm. The strain and displacement fields were interpreted together with the optical observations, which indicate localized thermomechanical modification and preferential material flow near the interface. The thermomechanically affected zone (TMAZ) reached approximately 157 HV. Direct comparison with thermocouple measurements and the measured aluminum-side TMAZ width supported the model for the directly comparable quantities. Microhardness provides complementary evidence of localized hardening but does not constitute direct strain measurement or phase identification. The model is useful for interpreting the thermomechanical response of AA2024/Cu-DHP radial friction welds, while the assumptions regarding friction and radiation, the absence of latent heat, and the absence of microstructural-kinetics modelling remain explicit limitations.
