papers.title: Design and Optimization of a Yokeless Segmented Axial Flux Motor for High-Torque Applications
papers.abstract: In recent years, electric vehicles have emerged as an effective solution for reducing environmental pollution and fossil fuel consumption; however, limited driving range remains one of their main challenges. In this context, improving electric motor performance plays a key role in enhancing vehicle efficiency and power density in order to improve its cruising mileage. In this regard, permanent magnet synchronous machines, particularly axial flux topologies, are considered promising candidates due to their high efficiency and favorable specific torque capability. Although their performance is superior to radial flux machines, many studies were conducted to improve their torque density while maintaining other key performance indices to reduce vehicle overall weight. In this paper, a double-sided, yokeless axial flux motor with a segmented stator is designed and optimized for light electric vehicle applications. The elimination of the stator yoke leads to a significant reduction in weight and an increase in power density, while the proposed structure maintains satisfactory electromagnetic performance. The results show that the designed motor, operating at a power density of approximately 1.29 kW/kg, achieves a torque ripple of less than 6%, demonstrating suitable performance in terms of output torque and torque quality for the intended application.

papers.title: Numerical and Experimental Investigation of Thermo-Hydraulic Performance Enhancement of Water-Cooled Photovoltaic Modules Using a Helical Pipe Network with Twisted Tape Inserts
papers.abstract: High and spatially non-uniform temperatures reduce the electrical output of photovoltaic (PV) modules and accelerate hotspot-related degradation. While previous research has looked into water-cooled PV/T systems and the use of twisted-tape inserts as separate solutions, there's a noticeable absence of studies that combine these approaches. Specifically, there is a lack of investigation into optimizing the arrangement of cooling pipes before incorporating internal flow enhancements. Moreover, experimental evidence is essential to confirm if such a dual strategy can genuinely improve the performance without imposing significant hydraulic disadvantages. This research directly tackles these issues by introducing and validating a two-step optimization strategy for water-cooled PV/T modules. Our work commenced with a computational assessment of four different helical pipe arrangements (100 × 150, 100 × 100, 100 × 50, and 80 × 80 mm). After this initial evaluation, the most promising configuration was further refined by adding either four or ten twisted-tape inserts. The best-performing layout was then enhanced using four and ten twisted-tape inserts. Simulations in three dimensions, investigating conjugate heat transfer, were performed using ANSYS Fluent. These simulations were carried out under a heat flux load of 800 W/m², with incoming water at a temperature of 25 °C, and across a range of Reynolds numbers from 5,000 to 11,000. The configuration featuring an 80 × 80 mm layout emerged as the optimal baseline. This setup successfully lowered the average temperature of the PV surface to 45.62 °C when the Reynolds number was 11,000. Concurrently, it achieved an electrical efficiency of 16.05% and an electrical power output of 205.49 W. The subsequent introduction of ten twisted-tape inserts led to a further reduction in temperature, bringing it down to 42.30 °C. This enhancement also boosted the electrical efficiency to 16.44% and the power output to 210.48 W. To confirm these findings, experimental validation was conducted. The results from these experiments showed mean absolute percentage errors of 1.46% for the baseline setup and a slightly lower 1.23% for the configuration enhanced with inserts. An important consideration, the pumping power required for these systems remained below 3 W across all tested conditions. The distinct contribution of this research lies in its comprehensive approach, which unifies several key aspects within a single design framework. This includes optimizing the helical pipe layout, harnessing the flow enhancement provided by twisted tapes, evaluating the uniformity of temperature, and undertaking experimental validation of the thermo-hydraulic performance. This integrated methodology effectively demonstrates that improvements in hotspot management and overall electrical performance can be realized without incurring substantial demands on hydraulic energy.

This integrated methodology effectively demonstrates that improvements in hotspot management and overall electrical performance can be realized without incurring substantial demands on hydraulic energy.

papers.title: ANALYSIS OF MHD CASSON HYBRID NANOFLUID FLOW AND HEAT TRANSFER IN A PARALLEL PLATE CHANNEL
papers.journal: Advances and Applications in Fluid Mechanics
papers.abstract: The present study investigates magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) Casson hybrid nanofluid flow and heat transfer through a vertical parallelplate channel. The flow is driven by pressure gradient and buoyancy forces, with an externally applied magnetic field perpendicular to the flow direction. The coupled nonlinear momentum and energy equations are transformed into dimensionless form and solved numerically using the finite difference method (FDM) and Gauss-Jacobi iterative technique. The effects of the Hartmann number, Casson parameter, Grashof number, Brinkman number, and hybrid nanoparticle volume fractions on velocity and temperature distributions are investigated. The results indicate that increasing the Grashof number enhances both velocity and temperature due to stronger buoyancy-driven convection. An increase in the Brinkman number intensifies viscous dissipation, leading to higher fluid temperature and enhanced flow velocity. The Casson parameter reduces the velocity profile by increasing resistance to fluid motion, while its influence on temperature is relatively small. The magnetic field suppresses fluid motion through the resistive Lorentz force, whereas its influence on temperature remains comparatively small under the considered conditions. These findings provide insights into momentum and thermal transport in MHD Casson hybrid nanofluids, with potential applications in heat exchangers, cooling systems, and industrial thermal management.

The results indicate that increasing the Grashof number enhances both velocity and temperature due to stronger buoyancy-driven convection.

papers.title: Antitrust Regulation of Algorithmic "Platform-Driven Involution'': From Governing the Corporate Person to Governing the Platform Ecosystem
papers.abstract: Digital platforms increasingly govern competition through algorithmically administered rules that allocate visibility, subsidies, commissions, participation opportunities, and sanctions. This article reconstructs ``platform-driven involution'' as a testable, portfolio-based theory-of-harm framework rather than a freestanding antitrust offense. Its application remains anchored in market definition, dominance, identified conduct under Article 22 of China's Anti-Monopoly Law, causal proof, competitive effects, and objective justification. The article clarifies that ecosystem analysis supplements rather than replaces relevant-market analysis and develops an evidence architecture for separating platform-induced effects from macroeconomic, demand, cost, and merchant-specific confounders. It then distinguishes preventive measures already supported by Chinese hard law or voluntary compliance guidance from compulsory competition-specific filing and pre-deployment assessment that would require clearer future authorization. The 2026 Trip.com decision is used to show how traffic allocation, exclusivity, lowest-price requirements, technical monitoring, and sanctions can form an integrated abuse architecture while liability remains tied to established statutory categories. Comparative analysis of EU platform regulation and Google Shopping supports calibrated procedural prevention, meaningful explanation, and causal discipline without protecting inefficient competitors or condemning aggressive competition.
papers.summary: Digital platforms increasingly govern competition through algorithmically administered rules that allocate visibility, subsidies, commissions, participation opportunities, and sanctions. papers.title: Digital-Twin-Driven Predictive Maintenance and Fault-Tolerant Control for Electrified Agricultural Machinery: A Multiphysics and Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for PMSM In-Wheel Drives
papers.abstract: Electrified agricultural machinery increasingly relies on permanent-magnet synchronous motor drives that must remain dependable under variable traction, terrain-induced vibration, thermal cycling, contamination, and intermittent duty. Existing work offers mature methods for motor fault diagnosis, digital twins, predictive maintenance, and distributed-drive fault-tolerant control, but their health information is often not shared across diagnosis, maintenance, and control. This article develops a multiphysics digital-twin framework in which electrical, thermal, mechanical, and vibrational evidence maintains a probabilistic health belief that constrains both supervisory maintenance decisions and torque redistribution. The framework formalizes observability, uncertainty-aware health factors, deterministic safety shielding, multi-rate fallback logic, and agriculture-specific traction constraints. Reproducible low-fidelity numerical studies provide preliminary support for context-conditioned residual diagnosis and the revised thermal-continuity trade-off underlying health-aware derating, including robustness and sensitivity analyses. They do not validate sim-to-real transfer or the reinforcement-learning policy itself; those hypotheses remain open for dynamometer and hardware-in-the-loop testing. The results are therefore interpreted as mechanism-level evidence rather than field-performance validation.

papers.title: Majority Filter For Enhancing Pixel-Based Random Forest Land Cover Classification In Sukajaya District, Bogor Regency
papers.abstract: High-quality land cover data are essential for environmental policy, spatial planning, and ecosystem monitoring. However, pixel-based classification methods, while widely used due to their practicality, often suffer from salt-and-pepper noise, which undermines map reliability. This study aimed to integrate Random Forest (RF) classification and majority filtering to enhance the quality of land cover mapping in Sukajaya District, Bogor Regency. RF was applied to Sentinel-2 image data with varying numbers of trees (ntree) to determine the optimal model performance. Subsequently, majority filtering was applied to each classification result to reduce noise and improve spatial coherence. The evaluation employed multiple accuracy metrics, including User’s Accuracy (UA), Producer’s Accuracy (PA), F1-Score, Overall Accuracy (OA), and Kappa Coefficient (KC). Comprehensive accuracy increased with the ntree until reaching an optimal point. Beyond this point, additional ntree resulted in diminishing returns. Applying majority filtering as a post-processing procedure led to further improvements in classification accuracy. While majority filtering can reduce classification noise and improve the visual quality of land cover maps, it also carries the risk of removing small, accurately classified land cover patches. This consequence is rarely discussed in similar studies. These findings highlight the importance of integrating pixel-based machine learning classification with majority filtering in land cover classification workflows, while emphasising a trade-off that tends to favour visual accuracy over the preservation of spatial detail.

papers.title: Extracellular vesicles in gastrointestinal diseases: A narrative minireview of translational readiness
papers.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) mediate communication among epithelial, immune, stromal, microbial, and tumor compartments in gastrointestinal diseases. This narrative minireview integrates inflammatory bowel disease and major gastrointestinal malignancies (colorectal, gastric, pancreatic, and liver cancers) using a five-stage translational-readiness framework: Discovery, analytical validation, clinical validation, regulatory development, and implementation. We distinguish discovery-stage and preclinical findings from clinically validated applications. EV cargo and engineered EV platforms show potential for biomarker panels, liquid biopsy, drug delivery, and regenerative medicine, but no broad EV assay or therapeutic platform is established for routine precision gastroenterology. Key barriers include pre-analytical variability, isolation-dependent results, incomplete cargo attribution, cohort heterogeneity, limited independent validation, and manufacturing and safety requirements. Progress will require standardized workflows, disease-specific comparators, prospective multicenter validation, and evidence-calibrated integration of EV data with conventional biomarkers and multi-omics.

papers.title: Helicobacter pylori status in gastric cancer immunotherapy: Conflicting clinical associations, immune-microbial mechanisms, and biomarker challenges
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have become an important treatment option for gastric cancer, but therapeutic responses remain highly heterogeneous. Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori ), a major risk factor for gastric carcinogenesis, may continue to influence tumor immunity and immunotherapy outcomes after cancer develops. However, current clinical findings are inconsistent, and the biomarker value of H. pylori remains uncertain. This review critically summarizes the clinical and mechanistic evidence linking H. pylori status to ICI outcomes in gastric cancer. Potential mechanisms include regulation of programmed cell death protein 1/programmed death-ligand 1 signaling, T-cell function, antigen presentation, myeloid immunosuppression, and microbial ecology. The divergent clinical results may reflect differences in infection status, detection methods, tumor molecular subtypes, disease stage, treatment setting, and previous therapeutic exposures. Current evidence does not support H. pylori as a validated predictive biomarker for ICI response. Rather, it may represent a context-dependent indicator of the tumor-immune-microbial background. Prospective longitudinal studies with standardized definitions of current active infection, previous infection of uncertain current status, successfully eradicated infection, and no evidence of previous infection are needed to determine whether specific H. pylori -related biological states modify the relative benefit of immunotherapy.

papers.title: Current status of room temperature magnetic compensation in impurity-doped Mn4N epitaxial thin films
papers.abstract: Mn4N, a ferrimagnet that does not contain rare-earth elements, possesses attractive properties for spintronics applications. In particular, Mn4N epitaxial films exhibit a small spontaneous magnetization of about 100 kA m(-1), a large spin polarization (p = 0.8), and large perpendicular magnetic anisotropy with a magnetic anisotropy constant of approximately 10(5) J m(-3). More importantly, achieving magnetic compensation at room temperature is possible through impurity doping. This property is particularly significant for spin-torque-based spintronics applications. In the vicinity of the magnetization and/or angular momentum compensation points, magnetization dynamics can be substantially accelerated, enabling high-speed switching and domain wall motion. This article surveys the magnetic properties of impurity-doped Mn4N epitaxial films grown on SrTiO3(001) substrates, highlighting recent results obtained with Cu-, Ag-, Au-, and Pd-doped Mn4N films in comparison with Ni- and Cr-doped Mn4N films. Furthermore, with a view to device applications of Mn4N, we present the formation of ultrathin (similar to 4 nm) Pt epitaxial films with a <100> orientation on MgO (001), which is essential for injecting spins into Mn4N-based overlayers by utilizing the spin Hall effect of heavy metals. papers.title: Reproducible chiroptical activity from aggregated chiral thienopyrroledione-fluorene π-conjugated polymers
papers.abstract: Chiral pi-conjugated polymers have attracted considerable interest because their chiral-aggregated structures can generate pronounced chiroptical responses. Here, we report the design, synthesis, and chiroptical characterization of fluorene - thienopyrroledione polymers bearing a single chiral center in each repeating unit, (R)- and (S)-PFTPD, prepared via direct arylation polycondensation to minimize structural defects. Although only weak chiroptical activity was observed in the solution, the addition of 1-butanol to CHCl3 solutions of the polymers induced the formation of stable aggregates that exhibited strong circular dichroism (CD) and circularly polarized luminescence (CPL). Systematic examination of the sample preparation parameters revealed that the mixing process critically influences the chiroptical properties. Dropwise addition of 1-butanol under controlled stirring provided the most reliable results, yielding highly reproducible CD spectra. Under these optimized conditions, the aggregates exhibited an average dissymmetry factor (|g abs|) of 1.5 & times; 10-2 and a CPL dissymmetry factor (|g lum|) of 1.9 & times; 10-2. These values rank among the highest reported for pi-conjugated polymer aggregates bearing only a single chiral source per repetition unit. This study demonstrates that precise control over the solvent-mixing process is essential for the reproducible emergence of chiroptical properties and highlights the chiral TPD unit as a promising platform for chiroptical polymer materials.
papers.summary: Chiral pi-conjugated polymers have attracted considerable interest because their chiral-aggregated structures can generate pronounced chiroptical responses. This study demonstrates that precise control over the solvent-mixing process is essential for the reproducible emergence of chiroptical properties and highlights the chiral TPD unit as a promising platform for chiroptical polymer materials.

papers.title: Somatosensory phenotyping in women with persistent genital arousal disorder: a case-control study.
papers.abstract: Introduction: Persistent genital arousal disorder (PGAD) is a rare and distressing condition characterized by persistent, unwanted genital arousal in the absence of sexual desire or stimulation. Persistent genital arousal disorder is increasingly recognized as a disorder of abnormal genital sensory processing, but objective neurophysiological data remain limited. Methods: We conducted an exploratory case-control study to characterize somatosensory function in women with PGAD. Thirty women with PGAD and 30 age-matched healthy controls were recruited at Leiden University Medical Center. Participants underwent quantitative sensory testing (QST) at hand and external genital sites, conditioned pain modulation, and corneal confocal microscopy. Results: Hand QST values were within normal range in both groups. In the genital region, PGAD participants showed altered thermal pain processing, with cold and heat hyperalgesia compared with controls. Mechanical pain thresholds did not differ between groups; however, PGAD participants reported higher pain intensity ratings to mechanical stimuli and showed significantly greater temporal summation of pain in genital regions. Genital dynamic mechanical allodynia occurred more frequently in PGAD participants but did not differ significantly at the group level. Conditioned pain modulation magnitude did not differ between groups and showed substantial interindividual variability. Corneal confocal microscopy abnormalities were observed in a proportion of participants in both groups without significant between-group differences. Discussion: These findings show that QST is feasible in women with PGAD and indicate that PGAD is associated with altered somatosensory processing demonstrating genital thermal hypersensitivity and central pain sensitization in a subset of patients.

Conditioned pain modulation magnitude did not differ between groups and showed substantial interindividual variability. papers.title: Designing an Integrated Play Therapy Program Based on the Cognitive-Behavioral Approach and Sensory Integration for Children With Autism
papers.journal: The Psychological Research in Individuals with Exceptional Needs
papers.abstract: The present study aimed to design an integrated play therapy program based on the cognitive-behavioral approach and sensory integration for children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). In terms of purpose, this was an applied study, and in terms of methodology, it employed a qualitative research design. Using thematic analysis based on Braun and Clarke’s (2006) six-phase framework, valid and up-to-date theoretical and empirical evidence was systematically reviewed and coded. A step-by-step framework illustrating the process of structuring and designing the integrated play therapy program based on the cognitive-behavioral approach and sensory integration for children with autism was developed according to Intervention Mapping (IM). The integrated cognitive-behavioral play therapy and sensory integration program was subsequently presented to 10 faculty members from the University of Tehran and experienced therapists working in a university clinic for children with neurodevelopmental disorders who were professionally involved in the field of autism spectrum disorder. They were asked to provide expert feedback on the developed intervention package to facilitate its refinement. Quantitative assessment of the content validity of the integrated play therapy program was conducted using the Content Validity Index (CVI) and Content Validity Ratio (CVR). The results indicated that the integrated program resulted in the development of a valid 12-session protocol. The inductive thematic analysis process progressed from 52 initial codes to 22 axial codes, 14 subthemes, and 8 main themes. These eight themes constituted the conceptual pillars of the protocol and integrated the cognitive-behavioral and sensory integration approaches within a spiral, play-based structure, thereby empirically demonstrating the feasibility of the proposed program design. Another finding of the present study was that the integrated program demonstrated satisfactory validity. The CVI calculated for each of the 12 items corresponding to the intervention sessions ranged from .80 to .90, with all values exceeding the accepted threshold of .79. Internal validity was confirmed through member checking and calculation of the CVI. The developed integrated program constitutes a valid intervention for improving sensory responses in children with sensory modulation disorder. Based on the findings, it is recommended that psychologists working with children with special needs use the 12-session integrated protocol developed in this study as a standardized intervention package.

In terms of purpose, this was an applied study, and in terms of methodology, it employed a qualitative research design. The results indicated that the integrated program resulted in the development of a valid 12-session protocol.

papers.title: 3D bioprinting of tissues and organs for systemic diseases and localized injuries
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting integrates engineering, materials science, and biology to fabricate living tissues with precise spatial control. By enabling the layer-by-layer deposition of cells and biomaterials, it overcomes many limitations of traditional scaffold-based tissue engineering and offers new opportunities for regenerative and personalized medicine. This review presents a comprehensive overview of recent advances in 3D bioprinting. It introduces a systematic, ASTM-aligned classification of key bioprinting modalities, extrusion, jetting, and vat photopolymerization, along with their respective material and biological design requirements. It also summarizes recent progress in bio-ink development and crosslinking strategies that improve print fidelity and functional tissue maturation. In addition, the review highlights applications in both systemic disease modelling and treatment (such as cardiovascular, endocrine/metabolic, and neurodegenerative disorders) and localized tissue repair (including skin, musculoskeletal, cartilage, and bone), emphasizing their relevance to civilian healthcare and military medicine. By combining technological innovation, biological insights, and regulatory considerations, this review outlines how advances in multi-modal bioprinting and intelligent process control can accelerate the translation of laboratory research into clinically viable, patient-specific therapies, driving the next generation of regenerative medicine.

papers.title: Enhancing mass transport in redox flow batteries with 3D-printed triply periodic minimal surface electrode structures
papers.abstract: Triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) structures offer a compelling route for designing porous electrodes with tunable architectures for electrochemical applications such as redox flow batteries. In this study, we fabricated carbonaceous TPMS electrodes, including gyroid, diamond, IWP, and cubic geometries, using digital light processing, and evaluated their performance in single-electrolyte flow cells using an organic redox couple. The printing process and subsequent thermal treatment produced conductive porous electrodes that closely replicated the intended TPMS geometries, preserving the characteristic features of each design. Through a detailed analysis of pressure drop, surface area, and electrochemical behavior, we identified the diamond design as particularly effective in enhancing mass transport while maintaining low hydraulic resistance. We further assessed gyroid structures, selected for being the most well-known among TPMSs, across a range of porosities, finding that higher porosity improved flow performance despite a reduction in surface area, an advantageous trade-off for electrolytes with facile kinetics and low ionic conductivity. Comparison with a commercial carbon felt electrode revealed comparable ohmic resistance and favorable flow characteristics, though reduced electrochemical surface area limited the achievable current densities. To isolate mass transport effects, a kinetically facile organic redox couple was employed, after which a representative 3D-printed gyroid electrode was evaluated in a proof-of-concept full-cell vanadium redox flow battery. A full-cell test demonstrated the feasibility of printed electrodes, achieving a voltage efficiency of 76% at a current density of 50 mA cm−2. These findings demonstrate the potential of architected 3D printed electrodes for future redox flow batteries and highlight the importance of tuning geometry and porosity to balance power output, mass transport, and system-level pumping losses.

papers.title: A Systematic Review of Alkali-Treated Polylactic Acid Biocomposites Relevant to Pineapple Leaf and Water Hyacinth Hybrid Design
papers.journal: Journal of Mechanical Engineering Science and Technology (JMEST)
papers.abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable materials has accelerated the development of biodegradable polymer composites. Polylactic acid (PLA)-based natural fiber composites have attracted significant attention due to their renewable characteristics; however, their performance remains limited by weak fiber–matrix compatibility, moisture sensitivity, and inconsistent interfacial behavior. Alkali treatment has been widely applied to modify lignocellulosic fibers by removing non-cellulosic components and improving surface characteristics, although its effectiveness remains dependent on treatment conditions and fiber properties. This systematic review evaluates the influence of alkali treatment on PLA-based natural fiber composites and assesses the available evidence supporting future pineapple leaf fiber (PALF) and water hyacinth fiber (WHF) hybrid composite development. The review followed the PRISMA 2020 framework using Scopus-indexed articles published between 2020 and 2026. A total of 336 records were identified, with 295 studies retained for evidence synthesis and classified into five categories (E1–E5) to distinguish direct evidence from transferable knowledge. The results indicate that no direct PLA/PALF-WHF hybrid composite study has been reported. Alkali treatment generally improves fiber surface modification and interfacial interaction; however, the resulting performance is highly condition-dependent, influenced by alkali severity, fiber characteristics, loading ratio, and processing route. WHF remains insufficiently characterized in PLA-based systems due to hydrophilicity and compatibility challenges. Therefore, future studies should focus on controlled PLA/PALF-WHF hybrid experiments, optimized treatment parameters, and multi-response performance evaluation.

papers.title: Effect of preheating palm oil biodiesel fuel on the performance and emissions of diesel engine common rail direct injection
papers.journal: Journal of Mechanical Engineering Science and Technology (JMEST)
papers.abstract: Fossil fuel consumption continues to increase while its reserves continue to decrease and produce high emissions that trigger global warming. Therefore, more environmentally friendly alternative energy is needed. Biodiesel is a sustainable choice because it is biodegradable, low in sulphur, and can replace fossil fuels. This study investigates the influence of biodiesel fuel preheating temperature on engine performance, fuel consumption, and emissions in a Common Rail Direct Injection (CRDI) diesel engine. The experimental method was carried out by heating B40 and B50 fuels at temperatures of 40°C to 60°C at intervals of 10 °C. Engine performance was evaluated using a chassis dynamometer at engine speeds of 1500 to 3000 rpm at intervals of 500 rpm, fuel consumption was measured with a digital scale, and exhaust emissions testing was carried out using an opacity smoke meter. Fuel preheating at 60°C in B40 and B50 blends improved engine performance, where power output increased by up to 1.03% (78.3 vs 77.5 HP), torque rose by up to 2.64% (178.6 vs 174 Nm), BSFC reduced by up to 7.30%, and opacity emissions decreased by up to 40% compared to fossil diesel. Fuel preheating improves atomization and promotes cleaner combustion in a diesel engine.

papers.title: Pacing in adults with complex congenital heart disease: A narrative minireview
papers.abstract: Congenital heart disease (CHD) is a growing health care problem, as more pediatric patients survive to adulthood every year as the number of patients with complex conditions also increases. As more patients survive, there has been an increase in the need for pacemaker procedures. Historically, there has been a focus on epicardial pacing in the most complex groups. In this review, we examine the background epidemiology, existing evidence for pacing, extraction data in three of the most complex CHD groups- transposition of the great arteries with an atrial switch procedure, patients palliated with a Fontan procedure and univentricular hearts. In this expert narrative review, we have used a broad search strategy of PubMed supplemented with evidence where available from non-congenital cohorts. The evidence in these most complex cohorts can be limited to expert centre opinion, small numbers and mixed paediatric/adult data. We discuss below the available data, the limitations and the novel approaches available in centres to deal with the most complex conditions such as conduction system pacing and leadless pacing with promising results albeit in expert centres only. Whilst current applicability to a wider range of institutions is not yet suggested by the paper, this review hopefully illustrates potential options for consideration and research in the future.

papers.title: Airdrop Sybil Attack detection framework supported by machine learning
papers.journal: International Journal of Electronics and Telecommunication Systems
papers.abstract: A skilled hunter may earn thousands of dollars in tokens from a single airdrop, making airdrop Sybil assaults a profitable endeavor. In this situation, Sybil assaults are not always wanted by projects and are often seen as improper behavior by honest individuals, which may negatively impact a project's image. It is thus to be anticipated that detection methods for Sybil assaults would be continuously enhanced. This study presents a multistep structure. Its concept is to sort blockchain addresses and give each one a score that indicates whether it belongs to the Sybil or regular class. Topologies were classified using a graph isomorphism network, whose parameters were adjusted using a dataset that the authors labeled. In subsequent phases, the account clustering operation was performed using a DBSCAN. Each stage in the framework may be given arbitrary weights by users, which will decide how essential a step is to them and provide a different score for a particular address. papers.title: Human–AI Divergence in Ego-Centric Action Recognition Under Spatial and Spatiotemporal Manipulations
papers.abstract: Abstract Humans consistently outperform state-of-the-art AI models in action recognition, particularly in challenging real-world conditions involving low resolution, occlusion, and visual clutter.e those utilised by humans Understanding the sources of this performance gap is essential for developing more robust and human-aligned models. In this paper, we present a large-scale human AI comparative study of egocentric action recognition using human-defined Minimal Identifiable Recognition Crops (MIRCs), defined as the smallest spatial or spatiotemporal regions sufficient for reliable human recognition. We used our previously introduced, Epic-ReduAct, a systematically spatially reduced and temporally scrambled dataset derived from 36 EPIC-KITCHENS videos, spanning multiple spatial reduction levels and temporal conditions. Recognition performance is evaluated using over 3,000 human participants, Side4Video, and Qwen 3.5 9B models. Our analysis combines quantitative metrics, Average Reduction Rate and Recognition Gap, with qualitative analyses of spatial (high-, mid-, and low-level visual features) and spatiotemporal factors, including a categorisation of actions into Low Temporal Actions (LTA) and High Temporal Actions (HTA). Results show that human performance exhibits sharp declines when transitioning from MIRCs to sub-MIRCs, reflecting a strong reliance on sparse, semantically critical cues such as hand object interactions. In contrast, the model degrades more gradually and often relies on contextual and mid- to low-level features, sometimes even exhibiting increased confidence under spatial reduction. Temporally, humans remain robust to scrambling when key spatial cues are preserved, whereas the model often shows insensitivity to temporal disruption, revealing class-dependent temporal sensitivities. Overall, our findings demonstrate that strong benchmark performance can obscure fundamental human AI misalignment and highlight limitations in current spatial and spatiotemporal representations, suggesting concrete directions for more efficient and human-aligned action recognition systems.

papers.title: Bacillus cereus PHB CMST1: a potential Halophilic Bacterium for cost-effective and sustainable production of polyhydroxyalkanoates
papers.abstract: Abstract Bacteria can spontaneously produce polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA), a thermoplastic and biodegradable substance. PHA is the best polymer substitute for plastic made from petrochemicals. In this investigation, we isolated sixteen bacterial strains from brine and sediment samples collected from a solar salt works facility. Among the sixteen bacterial strains screened for polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA) production, two strains, Z6 and Z9, exhibited promising results based on Sudan Black B and Nile Blue A staining. Subsequent morphological, biochemical, and molecular characterization identified strain Z9 as Bacillus cereus PHB CMST1 through 16S rRNA sequencing, which demonstrated superior PHA production compared to the other strain. To optimize PHA production, we employed a one-factor-at-a-time (OFAT) methodology, revealing optimal conditions of 35°C, pH 7, 2% salinity, and a 3-day incubation period, utilizing wheat bran as the carbon source and urea as the nitrogen source. Further optimization using Response Surface Methodology-Central Composite Design (RSM-CCD) indicated that B. cereus strain PHB CMST1 requires 5% wheat bran and 2% urea for enhanced PHA synthesis. The yellowish-green dots in the thin layer chromatography (TLC) plate indicated the presence of PHA. FT-IR analysis confirmed that, 𝛽-glycosidic linkages between the sugar monomers were found. The derivatives of polyhydroxybutyric acid confirmed the monomeric polymer by GC-MS analysis. PHA's XRD study showed wide peaks at 20° and 43°, indicating that the PHA had a semi-crystalline structure. Bacillus cereus shows considerable promise for cost-effective and large-scale production of PHA bioplastics, utilizing wheat bran as a non-expensive carbon source.

papers.title: A CGM-derived late-phase glycemic response phenotype during fasted moderate-intensity running
papers.abstract: Abstract Skeletal muscle is the principal site of glucose disposal during exercise, yet whether CGM-derived glycemic responses during exercise reflect muscle-related characteristics in healthy adults remains unclear. In this exploratory, repeated-measures study, we examined whether the late-phase glycemic response during fasted moderate-intensity running can be defined as a CGM-derived phenotype, and assessed its association with skeletal muscle index (SMI). Thirty healthy adults (19 men, 11 women) performed this exercise on a treadmill for 60 min, controlled within 40–60% heart rate reserve (HRR), on 2–3 occasions (76 trials). Glucose Increase (∆G) was defined as the change in mean glucose during the final 30 min relative to fasting baseline. Principal component analysis showed that the dominant axis of CGM time-series variation (67% of variance) corresponded closely to ∆G (R² = 0.92), supporting it as a task-specific summary metric. Single-trial reliability was low (ICC = 0.424) but reached a moderate level when averaged across repeated measurements (ICC = 0.642), indicating that ∆G should be interpreted as a repeated-measurement average rather than a single-session value. ∆G showed a negative association with SMI in the recreational group, but this was not independent of sex, and no association appeared in the trained group, where matched HRR did not guarantee matched absolute exercise intensity. These findings suggest that ∆G is not a direct biomarker of muscle mass, but a candidate CGM-derived glycemic response phenotype that requires repeated measurement and careful consideration of sex, running experience, and exercise-load conditions.

papers.title: PET Accelerates the Decomposition of HDPE During Co-Pyrolysis: A Non-Additive Interaction from Thermogravimetry to Bench Scale
papers.abstract: Post-consumer polyolefin waste sent to pyrolysis commonly carries poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET), yet yield and kinetic models for such feeds often treat their components as decomposing independently. We tested that assumption by comparing the thermogravimetric response of blends of high-density polyethylene (HDPE) and PET with the mass-weighted sum of the pure polymers measured in the same campaign, in single runs at 10, 20 and 50 % PET. All blends lost mass faster than the additive prediction, by 19 %–41 % of the initial mass between 400 °C and 500 °C, and the sign of the deviation held in two campaigns run a month apart at 9.8 °C min−1 and 20.3 °C min−1, although the ranking of the blends did not. Evolved-gas analysis placed the volatile maximum of every blend within 5 °C of HDPE, but the aliphatic channel (m/z 57) of the blends left the baseline 14 °C–24 °C below that of HDPE, against a repeatability of 2 °C. Micro-pyrolysis at 600 °C gave aromatics and acids at 0.9 %–11.4 % of the identified product area for blends with 10 to 50 % PET, against 50.4 % for PET alone. In a horizontal tube reactor, a 90:10 HDPE:PET feed held for 60 min at 450 °C–550 °C gave 83 %–88 % wax and at most 5.1 % GC-quantifiable liquid, with mass balances closing to 92 %–95 %. Without a pure-HDPE reactor run, this slate cannot be assigned to PET. The additive superposition of pure-polymer curves therefore underestimates how early a PET-bearing polyolefin feed loses mass, and the evolved-gas profiles show that this earlier loss includes an earlier onset of the polyolefin fraction.

papers.title: 自噬在睾丸支持细胞中的双重作用：机制解析与研究进展
authors: 浙江杭州 311300 浙江农林大学动物科技学院·动物医学院
papers.abstract: Sertoli cells play a central role in maintaining testicular homeostasis and male fertility. Given their high metabolic activity and exposure to diverse stressors, the integrity and function of Sertoli cells are particularly dependent on intracellular quality control mechanisms. Autophagy, a conserved cellular degradation and recycling mechanism, plays a critical role in preserving Sertoli cell structure and function. Emerging evidence indicates that autophagy exerts a dual influence on Sertoli cell physiology: it is protective when moderately activated but becomes detrimental when excessively stimulated or impaired. This review summarizes recent advances in understanding how autophagy regulates Sertoli cell functions, including blood-testis barrier (BTB) dynamics, secretory activity, and energy metabolism. We highlight how oxidative stress, toxicant exposure, hormonal signaling, and autophagy-related genes modulate autophagic responses in Sertoli cells. Dysregulated autophagy has been associated with barrier disruption, aberrant cytokine secretion, and metabolic imbalance. These findings highlight autophagy as an important regulator that can function as both a guardian and a potential disruptor of testicular function. Understanding the mechanistic basis and regulatory thresholds of autophagy in Sertoli cells not only provides insight into testicular homeostasis but also lays the foundation for developing targeted intervention strategies aimed at key autophagy nodes to protect male fertility from environmental toxicants, metabolic stress, and aging-related challenges.

papers.title: Body-weight support is the dominant contributor to elevated walking cost in cerebral palsy
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Children with cerebral palsy (CP) exhibit substantially elevated energetic costs of walking, yet the biomechanical origins of this excessive cost remain unclear, limiting the effectiveness of current interventions. Methods We tested whether reducing the mechanical demands of body-weight support or mediolateral stabilization produced different energetic responses between children with CP and typically developing (TD) peers. Using a custom mechatronic system, we independently applied controlled vertical body-weight support (1–60% body weight) and mediolateral stabilization stiffness (50–1500 N/m) while children with CP and TD peers walked on a treadmill at a fixed nondimensional speed. We quantified steady-state energetic cost using indirect calorimetry and used linear regression models to determine energetic responses to each intervention. Results Providing body-weight support significantly reduced net energetic cost in both groups, with a 3.5-fold greater effect in the CP group ( n = 23) compared to TD peers ( n = 10). Across the 1–60% support range, energetic cost decreased by 41% in CP to a level not significantly different than TD participants. Higher baseline energetic cost and greater knee flexion stabilization produced negligible energetic effects in both CP (n=14) and TD groups, with negligible differences in energetic response between groups. Conclusions Energetic cost associated with body-weight support is the dominant contributor to elevated energetic cost of walking in children with CP, whereas mediolateral stabilization contributes minimally under the conditions tested. These findings identify gravitational support as a key biomechanical target for energy-focused rehabilitation and assistive technology interventions.

papers.title: Distinct DNA-binding modes of Sp8 and Sp6 shape a hierarchical regulatory network in limb ectoderm
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Sp8 and Sp6 are two closely related Sp genes expressed in the limb ectoderm, where they regulate proximo-distal and dorso-ventral patterning. Genetic studies in mice have shown that they act in a dose-dependent manner, with Sp8 exerting a substantially stronger effect than Sp6 . Here, we integrate ChIPmentation-seq and RNA-seq analyses to elucidate their genome-wide regulatory networks and mechanisms of action. Our results show that Sp8 has a dual mode of action either directly binding GC-rich motifs or indirectly binding AT-rich motifs through Dlx. In contrast, Sp6 primarily acts through AT-rich motifs, via interaction with cofactors such as Dlx5. Both factors regulate key components of the Wnt, FGF, and BMP signaling pathways, central to limb patterning, and display both cooperative and independent roles. We further show that Sp8 and Sp6 can form homo- and heterodimers, as well as interact with Dlx5, revealing a complex regulatory network. Our findings provide molecular insight into limb morphogenesis and have potential implications for understanding congenital limb malformations.

papers.title: Posttranscriptional regulation by TIA1 and TIAL1 controls the transcriptional program enforcing T cell quiescence
papers.abstract: Immune protection against infections relies on long-term maintenance of a highly diversified naïve T cell repertoire. Transcription factors cooperate to enforce T cell metabolic quiescence and maintenance. However, less is known about the posttranscriptional networks that preserve naïve T cells. Here, we describe the RNA binding proteins T cell antigen 1 (TIA1) and TIA-like 1 (TIAL1) as key promoters of CD4 and CD8 T cell quiescence. T cells deficient in TIA1 and TIAL1 undergo premature T cell activation, exhaustion, and death in the absence of cognate antigens. Mechanistically, TIA1 and TIAL1 promote the messenger RNA translation of quiescence-associated transcription factors such as forkhead box P1, lymphoid enhancer factor 1, and T cell factor 1 to restrain homeostatic T cell proliferation and activation. In summary, our study highlights a previously unrecognized dependency on posttranscriptional gene regulation by TIA1 and TIAL1 for implementing the quiescent transcriptional programs for long survival of T cells.

papers.title: “Should I Give Up Now?” Investigating LLM Pitfalls in Software Engineering
papers.journal: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
papers.abstract: Software engineers are increasingly incorporating AI assistants into their workflows to enhance productivity and alleviate cognitive load. However, experiences with Large Language Models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT vary widely. While some engineers find them useful, others deem them counterproductive due to inaccuracies in their responses. Researchers have also observed that ChatGPT often provides incorrect information. Given these limitations, it is crucial to determine how to effectively integrate LLMs into Software Engineering (SE) workflow. Analyzing data from 26 participants in a complex web development task, we identified nine failure types categorized into incorrect or incomplete responses, cognitive overload, and context loss. Users attempted to mitigate these issues through scaffolding, prompt clarification, and debugging. However, 17 participants ultimately chose to abandon ChatGPT due to persistent failures. Our quantitative analysis revealed that unhelpful responses increased the likelihood of abandonment by a factor of 11, while each additional prompt reduced abandonment probability by 17%. This study advances the understanding of human-AI interaction in SE tasks and outlines directions for future research and tooling support.

papers.title: Functional -PO2-mediated asymmetric CuN3 site enabled synergistic acetylene hydrochlorination
papers.abstract: Symmetric metal-N 4 (MN 4 ) sites represented a common configuration in single-atom catalysts (SACs) but often limited catalytic activity due to inadequate substrate polarization and activation. Herein, we overcame this fundamental limitation by precisely engineering the microenvironment around copper single-atom using P-doping to introduce non-coordinating -PO 2 group, which induced the transformation of symmetric CuN 4 site into low-coordinated, asymmetric electron-rich CuN 3 configuration. Crucially, the CuN 3 site and proximal -PO 2 group, co-located at pore defect, created an enzyme-mimicking catalytic pocket. When applied for the model reaction of acetylene hydrochlorination, these biomimetic CuN 3 and -PO 2 catalytic units enabled the profound synergistic effect, dramatically enhancing the adsorption, activation and dissociation of HCl to form the active Cu-Cl δ- /P-O-H δ+ intermediates. Once C 2 H 2 approached these activated species, it became polarized due to the local micro-electric field arising from the electronegativity differences between Cu-Cl δ- and P-O-H δ+ , thus lowering the barrier of rate-limiting step for C 2 H 3 Cl formation. This process endowed the P-doped Cu SAC with the enhanced acetylene hydrochlorination activity reaching comparable performance with the previously reported Cu-based analogues. This enzyme-mimetic strategy of creating synergistic catalytic microenvironment offered a powerful paradigm for designing highly efficient SACs for challenging chemical transformations.

papers.title: A revised genome annotation of the model cyanobacterium Synechocystis based on start and stop codon-enriched ribosome profiling and proteogenomics
papers.abstract: Abstract Cyanobacteria are important primary producers and popular in biotechnology. Synechocystis 6803 is a model cyanobacterium, yet many coding regions are ambiguous, or have remained undetected. Here, we present a riboproteogenomic analysis combining ribosome profiling with inhibitors that stall ribosomes at translation initiation and termination sites, and proteogenomic re-annotation of its genome. Based on proteogenomics, we report translation of 3055 annotated genes (83%), 3492 based on Ribo-seq (95.2%), and 3,018 supported by both methods (82%). The data suggest additional protein-coding genes and corrections for annotated ones. We validate 15 proteins translated from antisense, intergenic and intragenic loci and provide proteogenomic support for up to 69 additional, mostly small proteins. We identify three genes with ~300 nt long intragenic out-of-frame translons and demonstrate that internal and host translons are translated into interacting proteins. Our data are accessible at https://www.bioinf.uni-freiburg.de/~ribobase/ . They illustrate the enormous value of consolidating genome annotations with integrated experimental data.

papers.title: Neuron Patching: Semantic-based Neuron-level Language Model Repair for Code Generation
papers.journal: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
papers.abstract: Language Models (LMs) have become widely used in software engineering, especially for tasks such as code generation, where they are referred to as code LMs. These models have proven effective in generating code, making it easier for developers to automate coding activities. However, research has highlighted a significant limitation: despite their effectiveness, LMs often produce code that is incorrect, buggy, or not fully functional. Addressing this limitation is essential to fully realize LMs’ potential in practical applications. Yet, updating LMs, especially with only a small amount of feedback data, is highly challenging. In such cases, hot-fix techniques, which facilitate agile model updates with limited data, may be promising to maintain reliability and usefulness. In this article, we propose Model Improvement via Neuron Targeting ( MINT ) , a novel approach for repairing code LMs. MINT leverages the semantic property of LMs to perform neuron-level repairs in a novel way. Furthermore, by analyzing the relationships between the model’s latent representations, the incorrect outputs, and the desired outputs, MINT determines which neurons are worth updating. This approach ensures that only the neurons crucial to the model’s failure are targeted, avoiding unnecessary changes and allowing for a more efficient and precise repair process. MINT is effective, efficient, and reliable, capable of correcting a neural model by patching a minimum number of neurons (usually one neuron for short code, while two or more neurons for long codes). We introduce new measures to evaluate its generalizability and develop a new benchmark, which is made available for further study. Our approach is evaluated on three coding tasks: line-level code generation, shellcode generation, and intent-to-bash translation. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly outperforms the State-of-the-Art (SOTA) in both effectiveness and efficiency measures. With respect to the ExactMatch score, MINT achieves 5.7–20.8 \(\%\) improvements in StarCoder2-3B and 3.9–18.5 \(\%\) improvements in CodeLlama-7B concerning the SOTA. Regarding efficiency, MINT is 32.3–74.8 \(\%\) faster than the SOTA. In addition, we analyze and discuss the side effects of model repair techniques, including the balance between generalization and specificity and the performance after multiple repairs in succession.

The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly outperforms the State-of-the-Art (SOTA) in both effectiveness and efficiency measures.

papers.title: Tuning Cu/diamond interfacial thermal conductance via nitrogen-termination engineering
papers.abstract: Cu-diamond composites are recognized as promising high-thermal-conductivity candidates for electronic cooling, offering tunable properties and competitive cost. However, their performance is significantly limited by the poor Cu/diamond interfacial thermal conductance (ITC). Here, we propose a nitrogen-termination strategy to tune the ITC of Cu/diamond interfaces and unravel atomistic mechanisms by which nitride interlayers tailor phonon transport. Based on the MACE machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP) framework, we fine-tune the pre-trained MACE-MPA-0 foundation model by incorporating customized C-N-Cu training datasets. Incorporating non-equilibrium molecular dynamics with MLIP-driven lattice dynamics simulations, we demonstrate that anharmonic effects contribute ∼60% to the ITC, and simply introducing N-termination on the diamond surface enhances the ITC by 10% compared to the bare Cu/diamond interface. However, the enhancement of harmonic phonon transmission contributes ∼80% of the ITC improvement. Mode-resolved phonon spectroscopy reveals that the LA phonons with frequencies above 4 THz and wavevectors near the Γ-X and Γ-U directions are selectively modulated by N-termination engineering. Analyses of local vibrational states and interfacial bonding further indicate that the N-termination on diamond tunes the interfacial heat conduction via surficial mass modification and chemical bonding regulation, as evidenced by variations in LDOS overlaps and COHP spectra. These findings open venues for tuning heat transfer across Cu/diamond interfaces via non-metallic modification-which avoids the graphitization issues associated with metallic coatings-and provide novel guidelines for upgrading the phonon-mediated heat transfer in Cu-diamond composites.

papers.title: Dino-cd:marrying DINOv3 with dual-branch complementary reconstruction for remote sensing change detection
papers.journal: International Journal of Machine Learning and Cybernetics
papers.abstract: Abstract The goal of remote sensing change detection (RSCD) is to accurately distinguish land-surface changes. Recently, Vision foundation models (VFMs), such as the self-supervised DINOv3, have demonstrated strong semantic parsing capabilities across various visual tasks. However, directly applying DINOv3 to RSCD remains challenging. First, DINOv3 produces low-resolution, single-scale feature representations, which are unfavorable for pixel-wise change classification. Second, DINOv3 is not tailored for RSCD and thus struggles to model geospatial differences along the temporal dimension. To address these issues, Marrying DINOv3 with Dual-Branch Complementary Reconstruction for Remote Sensing Change Detection (DINO-CD) is proposed. Specifically, a dual-branch complementary reconstruction module is introduced to enable interaction between DINO and CNN branches for complementary feature enhancement, producing multi-scale representations that preserve global semantic consistency while strengthening local detail discrimination. In addition, a hierarchical difference aggregation module is designed to comprehensively enhance temporal discrepancies via explicit frequency learning and multi-scale directional aggregation, thereby highlighting effective change regions and reducing false alarms and missed detections. Extensive experiments on multiple datasets demonstrate that DINO-CD outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving gains of 6% in F1-score and 8% in IoU on the CLCD dataset.
papers.summary: Abstract The goal of remote sensing change detection (RSCD) is to accurately distinguish land-surface changes. Recently, Vision foundation models (VFMs), such as the self-supervised DINOv3, have demonstrated strong semantic parsing capabilities across various visual tasks. Extensive experiments on multiple datasets demonstrate that DINO-CD outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving gains of 6% in F1-score and 8% in IoU on the CLCD dataset.

papers.title: Pten regulates neurogenic radial glia lineage progression and tunes neocortical astrocyte production in Mapk1/3 -dependent pathway
papers.abstract: The cerebral cortex consists of immense numbers of diverse cell types derived from radial glial progenitor (RGP) cells. How RGPs generate appropriate quantities of distinct cell types to safeguard a brain of correct size is not well understood. However, genetic aberrations in human, including mutations in PTEN , lead to cortical malformation such as macrocephaly, albeit with unknown etiology. Here, we used mosaic analysis with double markers (MADM)–based clonal analysis and single-cell phenotyping to decipher the role of Pten in RGP lineage progression during cortical ontogeny. Although neurogenic RGP lineage progression was altered and projection neuron production doubled in the absence of Pten , cortical astrogenesis was drastically increased. Through epistasis experiments, we show that the loss of Pten uncouples astrogenesis from essential growth factor signaling hubs, funneling into MAPK (mitogen-activated protein kinase). Collectively, our results suggest that Pten regulates RGP lineage progression with distinct sequential functions in corticogenesis to safeguard the emergence of a correctly sized cortex.

papers.title: A Tailor-Made Guanidine Ionizable Lipid as a Bifunctional mRNA Carrier and Nitric Oxide Production Inhibitor
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract: Abstract Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are the leading clinical platform for mRNA delivery, yet their capacity to trigger macrophage-driven inflammatory responses remains a fundamental barrier to therapeutic safety and efficacy. Here, we introduce a design principle in which a tailor-made nitric oxide (NO) inhibitory motif is embedded directly into the ionizable lipid, creating a single molecular scaffold that simultaneously delivers mRNA and suppresses macrophage inflammation. Screening of a focused acyl-guanidine library in LPS-induced peritoneal macrophages identified G9 as a potent NO inhibitor and reprogrammed macrophage polarization from the pro-inflammatory M1 to the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype. Conjugation of the G9 headgroup to a lipid tail yielded G9-1, an NO-inhibitory ionizable lipid that retains anti-inflammatory activity and preferentially delivers mRNA to pulmonary vascular endothelial cells and alveolar macrophages in vivo. In a murine model of acute lung injury (ALI), G9-1 LNPs loaded with IL-10 mRNA reduce pulmonary immune cell infiltration, suppress inflammatory cytokine production, and attenuate systemic inflammation. These results establish NO inhibition as an actionable molecular design principle for intrinsically anti-inflammatory LNPs and position G9-1 as a dual-function ionizable lipid for safer and more effective mRNA therapeutics.

papers.title: A new method to probe conducting filaments in MoS 2 -based memristors
papers.abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), such as molybdenum disulfide (MoS₂), are emerging as promising materials for next-generation electronic devices. They have proved to be serious candidates for integration with memristors in non-volatile memory and radio frequency (RF) applications. However, the physical mechanisms behind their resistive switching, particularly the formation and resorption of conducting filaments, remain unclear. In this study, we present a novel mechanical exfoliation technique that selectively removes the top metallic electrode from MoS₂-based memristors by exploiting the weak van der Waals interaction between MoS₂ and the top electrode. This method enables direct and multi-scale characterization of the MoS₂ surface in different states (initial, ON and OFF) using Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy (KPFM) and Raman spectroscopy mapping. To complete this study, cross-sectional Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) was also performed in different conductive states. Our results reveal that the conducting filament is formed by metallic atom migration from the top electrode into the MoS₂ layer. Additionally, we demonstrate that the choice of metallic electrodes (gold vs. nickel) significantly impacts the switching behavior due to differences in adsorption and diffusion energies. This work not only clarifies the filament formation mechanism and introduces a reproducible approach for in-operando characterization but also represents a real progress in the understanding and optimization of 2D material-based memristors.

papers.title: Phase-morphology evolution and apparent preferential localization of barium titanate in poly(vinylidene fluoride) and epoxidized natural rubber blends with tunable mechanical and dielectric properties
papers.abstract: Abstract Non-vulcanized blends of poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) with epoxidized natural rubber containing 50 mol% epoxide (ENR-50) in 80/20–20/80 wt% ratios were prepared by melt blending. The PVDF/ENR-50 blends at 80/20 and 50/50 were filled with 5 vol% barium titanate (BT). SEM analysis revealed a change in morphology from PVDF continuity to apparent co-continuity at 60/40–50/50, followed by ENR-50 continuity at higher ENR-50 content. Increasing the ENR-50 content reduced stiffness and tensile stress but increased extensibility, with elongation at break values of about 1000–2200% in the ENR-50-rich blends. Furthermore, the PVDF crystallization temperature increased from 135.8°C in neat PVDF to 139.3°C at the 50/50 composition, whereas normalized PVDF crystallinity decreased from 54.2% at 60/40 to 43.7% at 20/80 due to phase confinement. Relaxation peaks at − 36 and − 9°C indicated phase separation with partial interface compatibility. The novelty lies in the identification of two-phase inversion boundaries and the correlation between phase continuity and mechanical, thermal, dynamic-mechanical, and dielectric behavior. Moreover, BT particles preferentially segregated to ENR-50, increasing the average size of ENR-50 domains in the 80/20 blend from 6.5 to 11.4 µm without altering PVDF continuity.

papers.title: PCR-based assays for determining mating status in field-weathered Ceratitis capitata with enhanced precision across conventional, quantitative, and droplet digital platforms
papers.abstract: Accurately determining the mating status of the agricultural fruit fly pest Ceratitis capitata , commonly known as Medfly, is essential for timely and effective eradication efforts. To overcome the limitations of subjective DAPI-based staining assessments of females captured in dry Jackson traps and liquid Multilure traps, we developed a multi-tier molecular diagnostic method that unequivocally detects mating status using DNA probes targeting the male-specific Y114 locus on the Y-chromosome of C. capitata . Our protocol integrates morphological evaluation with increasingly sensitive molecular assays through the following steps: (1) A preliminary quality assessment of the specimens’ physical condition, DNA preservation, and mating status using conventional polymerase chain reaction (PCR) followed by agarose electrophoresis (cPCR); (2) quantification and real-time detection of sperm presence via quantitative PCR (qPCR); and (3) detection of trace amounts of sperm through droplet digital PCR (ddPCR). This PCR-based framework is designed for samples collected in the field, enabling accurate analysis of specimens exposed to adverse environmental conditions and varying levels of preservation after 2 and 3 weeks of weathering in traps. It allows quantitative determination of mating status even when sperm concentrations are extremely low, such as during transient copulation, and achieves detection limits down to approximately 14 spermatozoa in a mated female. By accounting for variable specimen quality and the performance characteristics of each molecular platform, this tiered approach ensures highly sensitive and unequivocal detection of mated females. The methodology can be used to assist eradication efforts across the C. capitata geographic range through the timely detection of mated females, halting their expansion and establishment into novel regions, reducing control and eradication costs.

papers.title: Early Treatment with Oral Pirfenidone Improves Bladder Function after Contusive Spinal Cord Injury in Mice
papers.abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) disrupts innervation to the lower urinary tract, resulting in bladder dysfunction that predisposes to urinary infections and renal impairment. While inflammation is central to bladder pathology after SCI, the molecular events linking acute to chronic remodeling are poorly defined. We hypothesized that early treatment with pirfenidone, an anti-inflammatory and anti-fibrotic drug, would attenuate bladder pathology after SCI. Adult female C57BL/6J mice underwent contusive SCI or sham laminectomy, and bladders were collected at 2, 7, 16, and 45 days later. SCI induced bladder hypertrophy, edema, hemorrhage, neutrophil infiltration, cell proliferation and loss of voiding function in the first 48 hours. Transcriptomic profiling at this timepoint was characterized by activation of inflammatory and cytokine pathways including TNF-α, IL-6, the complement cascade, and TGFβ. Although bladder function partially recovered by day 7, inflammatory pathways persisted and extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling programs emerged. By day 16, robust activation of ECM-remodeling pathways was evident in all bladders. Treatment with pirfenidone during the acute inflammatory phase (day 2–7) reduced bladder hypertrophy and suppressed expression of pro-fibrotic, inflammatory, and neuroplasticity-associated genes including Bdnf and Chrm2 that encodes muscarinic receptor 2 (M2). Mechanistically, pirfenidone attenuated TGFb signaling as shown by downregulation of phosphoSmad2 protein in whole bladders and decreased M2 receptor expression in the urothelium. These molecular changes correlated with improved function in pirfenidone-treated mice as shown by fewer voiding events with larger urine volumes up until 45 days after SCI. Early treatment with pirfenidone limits inflammation and fibrosis, normalizes neural signaling, and improves bladder function after SCI.

papers.title: Preclinical trial supports dual inhibition of BCL2 and Aurora kinase A for high-risk neuroblastoma
papers.journal: Journal of Experimental & Clinical Cancer Research
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Treatment for children with high-risk neuroblastoma relies on conventional chemotherapy and anti-GD2 immunotherapy. However, 5-year survival is only 50%, with high rates of late effects. Targeted therapy combinations are a major priority for these patients. The BCL2 inhibitor venetoclax, in combination with cyclophosphamide/topotecan, has clinical activity in relapsed and refractory neuroblastoma. We sought more effective and safer venetoclax combinations through systematic preclinical testing. Methods Synergistic combinations were identified by high-throughput screening using patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models and confirmed in vivo. The leading combination (venetoclax-alisertib) was compared to combination chemotherapy in a clinical trial-like study using 22 PDX models, in scheduling experiments designed to reduce short-term toxicity, and in combination with anti-GD2 immunotherapy. BCL2 and Bim-BCL2 complex protein levels were assessed as predictors of sensitivity. Results In vitro synergy with venetoclax was observed for standard-of-care chemotherapies and targeted agents, including DNA topoisomerase, microtubule, HDAC and Aurora kinase A (AURKA) inhibitors. Venetoclax-alisertib was particularly effective in vivo. In an n = 1 study, venetoclax-alisertib induced objective response in all models. Activity was most striking in models of MYCN -amplified disease ( n = 12), doubling median survival time compared to cyclophosphamide/topotecan, and outperforming venetoclax-cyclophosphamide-topotecan. Efficacy was maintained with discontinuous schedules, minimizing hematological toxicity without substantially compromising activity. Venetoclax-alisertib was strikingly effective with anti-GD2 immunotherapy, allowing long-term survival of PDX-engrafted animals. BCL2 expression and BCL2-Bim complex levels were of limited value for predicting response. Conclusions Our findings support advancement of BCL2-AURKA inhibition to clinical trial for high-risk neuroblastoma with or without anti-GD2 immunotherapy, particularly in patients with MYCN -amplified disease.

papers.title: From Rim to Core: Nitrile Coordination Creates an Electronic Gradient across Cu12 Nanocluster Nodes for CO2-to-Formate Electrosynthesis
papers.abstract: Abstract Atomically precise copper nanoclusters offer an opportunity to program catalysis across individual metal positions, yet reticulation has largely been used to stabilize clusters rather than differentiate them electronically. Here, nitrile coordination converts a Cu12S9 nanocluster node into a radially polarized catalytic ensemble in Cu12TPN metal–organic framework (MOF). Single-crystal analysis resolves a thiolate-supported Cu12 architecture whose four terephthalonitrile linkers selectively address peripheral Cu sites. Bader analysis reveals an electronic gradient from electron-deficient nitrile-bound rim sites (∼+0.57 |e|) to an electron-rich Cu–S/Cu interior (∼+0.32–0.37 |e|). This coordination-encoded asymmetry translates directly into CO2 reduction, delivering 63.32% Faradaic efficiency for formate (HCOO–) with negligible CO formation. Density functional theory identifies a 0.91 eV energetic separation favoring O-bound *OCOH over *COOH at the pathway bifurcation, while H adsorption remains unfavorable. Postelectrolysis spectroscopy confirms persistence of the cluster-derived environment. These results establish reticulation as an electronic programming strategy within, rather than around, atomically precise nanocluster nodes.

papers.title: Sr-anchoring-directed gradient shell architecture in Sr 2 Fe 1.5 Mo 0.5 O 6− δ cathodes for reversible protonic ceramic electrochemical cells
papers.abstract: Abstract Strontium segregation remains a critical challenge for Sr-containing double perovskite cathodes, wherein outward-migrating Sr species accumulate at the surface and severely deteriorate interfacial electrochemical kinetics in reversible protonic ceramic electrochemical cells (R-PCECs). Herein, we develop a Sr-anchoring-driven interfacial catalytic architecture on Sr2Fe1.5Mo0.5O6−δ (SFM) via vanadium-assisted near-surface phase engineering. The incorporation of V introduces Lewis-acidic centers that effectively immobilize migrating Sr species and simultaneously induce the in situ reconstruction of a nanoscale SrMoO4/SrVO3 (SMO/SVO) heterointerface. More importantly, this reconstructed interface functions as a catalytically active region with enhanced electronic delocalization and optimized oxygen defect chemistry, which collectively promote oxygen adsorption, dissociation, and charge-transfer kinetics. The gradient shell architecture not only suppresses detrimental Sr segregation but also establishes fast and continuous pathways for coupled ion–electron transport across the interface. Electrochemical impedance and distribution of relaxation time (DRT) analyses reveal substantially reduced polarization resistance and decreased activation energy, indicating accelerated oxygen electrocatalysis. Consequently, the V-modified Sr2Fe1.5Mo0.5O6−δ-Vx (SFM-V) cathode exhibits markedly enhanced reversible electrochemical performance compared to pristine SFM, delivering a peak power density of 1.23 W·cm−2 at 650 °C together with high electrolysis activity and robust cycling stability, ranking among state-of-the-art SFM-based air electrodes for R-PCECs. This work demonstrates that Sr-anchoring interfacial engineering is an effective strategy to stabilize perovskite cathodes while maintaining fast interfacial kinetics.

papers.title: Recent Advances in Medical Imaging Segmentation: Generative, Few-Shot, Foundation and Universal Models
papers.abstract: Medical imaging is a cornerstone of modern healthcare, driving advancements in diagnosis, treatment planning, and patient care. Among its various tasks, segmentation remains one of the most challenging problems due to factors such as data accessibility, annotation complexity, structural variability, variation in medical imaging modalities, and privacy constraints. Despite recent progress, achieving robust generalization and domain adaptation remains a significant hurdle, particularly given the resource-intensive nature of some proposed models and their reliance on domain expertise. This survey explores cutting-edge advancements in medical image segmentation, focusing on methodologies such as Generative AI, Few-Shot Learning, Foundation Models, and Universal Models. These approaches offer promising solutions to longstanding challenges. We provide a comprehensive overview of the theoretical foundations, state-of-the-art techniques, and recent applications of these methods. Finally, we discuss inherent limitations, unresolved issues, and future research directions aimed at enhancing the practicality and accessibility of segmentation models in medical imaging. We maintain a GitHub Repository to continue tracking and updating innovations in this field.

papers.title: Ultrafast kilowatt-range microwave pulsing for enhanced CO₂ conversion in atmospheric-pressure plasmas
papers.abstract: Ultrafast microwave power pulsation is demonstrated as an effective strategy to enhance CO2 conversion in atmospheric-pressure plasma reactors. While initial experiments at several hundred watts in a compact coaxial plasma torch showed improved performance, the present study investigates the scalability of this approach to kilowatt-range microwave power. Conversion and energy efficiency were examined in two reactor configurations: a Surfaguide-based system (KIT) and a cavity-based plasma torch (IPP), and benchmarked against the compact coaxial torch. Both kilowatt-scale setups share similar microwave coupling schemes, power levels, reactor tubes, and gas injection geometries, but differ in afterglow treatment. The torch at IPP employs rapid nozzle-based quenching, whereas the Surfaguide-based reactor relies on slower cooling along an extended quartz tube. Stable plasma operation was achieved at pulsation peak powers of ~4 kW and pulse durations from sub-microseconds to microseconds, with stability limited to inter-pulse times of ~10 us (cavity-based torch) and ~12 us (Surfaguide-based reactor). In contrast to the coaxial torch, no plasma reignition regime was observed in either kilowatt-scale reactor, resulting in weaker plasma temperature modulation. Notably, the period-averaged gas temperature in the Surfaguide-based reactor exceeded that under continuous-wave operation. Under these conditions, relative enhancements of <40% in CO2 conversion and <20% in energy efficiency were measured compared with continuous-wave operation. These improvements were largely suppressed in the torch at IPP, presumably due to rapid afterglow quenching. Finally, analysis of the instantaneous reflected microwave power provided qualitative insights into electron density dynamics during the power-OFF and power-ON phases.

While initial experiments at several hundred watts in a compact coaxial plasma torch showed improved performance, the present study investigates the scalability of this approach to kilowatt-range microwave power. In contrast to the coaxial torch, no plasma reignition regime was observed in either kilowatt-scale reactor, resulting in weaker plasma temperature modulation.

papers.title: Preparation of alginate oligosaccharide–based ternary composite active film and its application in sweet cherry preservation
papers.abstract: Sweet cherries are highly perishable due to their delicate exocarp and rapid deterioration. Biodegradable active packaging offers a sustainable solution for extending postharvest shelf life. This study developed a ternary composite film using alginate oligosaccharide (AOS) as matrix, gelatin (G) as reinforcements, with clove essential oil (C) and tea polyphenols (T) as bioactive components. In result,the AOS-7%G-1.0%C formulation exhibited optimal integrated performance with significantly enhanced mechanical properties and bioactivity compared to commercial polyethylene (PE) films. FTIR, XRD and DSC analyses confirmed successful incorporation of functional constituents. In sweet cherry preservation trials, the bioactive composite film demonstrated superior antibacterial and antioxidant activities, effectively delaying spoilage and senescence versus PE-packaged and non-wrapped controls.The developed ternary composite film substantially outperformed conventional packaging, markedly extending postharvest shelf life of sweet cherries. These findings validate its promising translational potential for perishable fruit preservation applications.
