papers.title: Scoping review of digital pathology for neoadjuvant rectal cancer response
papers.abstract: Aim: Neoadjuvant therapy for locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC) yields variable patient responses. Artificial intelligence (AI) and digital pathology offer a novel approach to preoperatively predict treatment outcomes using histomorphological features, potentially guiding organ-preserving strategies. This scoping review maps the current literature on AI-driven neoadjuvant response prediction in LARC to evaluate algorithmic performance and identify methodological gaps. Methods: Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for scoping reviews (PRISMA-ScR) guidelines, a structured search of PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library was conducted for studies published within the last 10 years. Studies applying AI algorithms to pretreatment whole-slide images (WSIs) to predict neoadjuvant response in LARC were included. Results: Eleven publications were included. Ten studies used retrospective cohorts only, whereas one study also included a prospective validation cohort of 100 patients. Algorithmic frameworks predominantly featured classical machine learning, using software extraction of predefined features, and deep learning for autonomous pixel analysis. Across heterogeneous endpoints and cohorts, standalone classical machine-learning models reported external validation area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.811-0.908 (prospective: 0.733), a hybrid microenvironment model reported external AUCs of 0.643-0.656 (prospective: 0.630), and standalone deep-learning models reported an external AUC of 0.723 (internal: 0.710-0.81). Critical limitations across the field include heterogeneous clinical target endpoints, inconsistent baseline staging, and a reliance on “black box” algorithms lacking true biological explainability. Conclusion: AI-driven digital pathology demonstrates strong potential for predicting neoadjuvant treatment response in LARC. However, safe clinical implementation will require standardized endpoints, multimodal integration, and prospective multi-centre validation of algorithms anchored in verifiable tumour biology.
papers.summary: Aim: Neoadjuvant therapy for locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC) yields variable patient responses. This scoping review maps the current literature on AI-driven neoadjuvant response prediction in LARC to evaluate algorithmic performance and identify methodological gaps. Conclusion: AI-driven digital pathology demonstrates strong potential for predicting neoadjuvant treatment response in LARC.

papers.title: First measurement of sub-GeV ν μ charged-current coherent pion production on argon in MicroBooNE
papers.abstract: We report a measurement of the charged-current coherent pion production cross section on argon using the MicroBooNE liquid argon time projection chamber exposed to the Booster Neutrino Beam at Fermilab. The measurement uses the MicroBooNE data set corresponding to 1.26 × 10 21 protons on target with a mean neutrino energy of 0.8 ~GeV. The flux-averaged cross section is measured to be ( 9.1 ± 1.2 stat ± 1.2 syst ) × 10 − 40 cm 2 / Ar . This result represents the first measurement of charged-current coherent pion production on argon at sub-GeV neutrino energies. Due to its clean two-body kinematics, where the neutrino interacts coherently with the entire nucleus producing a forward muon and pion with no nuclear breakup, this process provides a useful tool for constraining neutrino flux uncertainties in current and future oscillation experiments such as DUNE.

papers.title: Suppression of the extrinsic anomalous Hall conductivity in a disordered parity anomalous semimetal
papers.abstract: We present an analytical investigation of the extrinsic contributions to the anomalous Hall conductivity in the context of the half-quantized Hall effect observed in a disordered parity anomalous semimetal emerged from semi-magnetic topological insulator thin films. The gapless Dirac cone surface state, which embodies the quintessence of the half-quantized Hall effect, exhibits remarkable robustness against disorder scattering. Two primary extrinsic mechanisms, the side-jump and skew-scattering mechanisms, are deemed irrelevant and make no contributions in the presence of symmetric short-range Anderson disorder. These results establish the parity anomalous semimetal as a disorder-resilient quantum phase, thereby providing insights into Dirac fermion physics.

papers.title: Porogen-Assisted PLGA Nanoparticles Prepared by Emulsification–Diffusion as Candidate Nanoscale Ultrasound Contrast Agents
papers.abstract: Ultrasound imaging combined with ultrasound contrast agents (UCAs) has broad diagnostic applications. However, commercially available UCAs are typically micrometer-sized (1–8 μm), which largely confines them to the vascular compartment and limits their access to tumor interstitium. This study aimed to optimize the hydrodynamic diameter and in vitro echogenicity of camphor-processed biodegradable poly(D, L-lactide-co-glycolide) nanoparticles (C-PNPs) prepared by the emulsification–diffusion method using a three-factor, three-level Box–Behnken design. The independent variables were camphor amount (mg), stabilizer concentration (% w/v), and homogenization speed (rpm). The optimized C-PNPs had a hydrodynamic diameter of 306.50 ± 2.09 nm, a polydispersity index of 0.05 ± 0.01, and a zeta potential of − 23.74 ± 0.23 mV. In vitro echogenicity studies showed that the optimized C-PNPs produced greater mean grayscale value (MGV) enhancement than porogen-free PLGA nanoparticles (23.86 ± 0.63% vs. 14.92 ± 0.58%). Scanning electron microscopy showed spherical particles, whereas differential scanning calorimetry indicated the absence of the camphor-associated thermal event after freeze-drying. Together with the increased echogenicity, these findings are consistent with the formation of low-density internal structures. The optimized C-PNPs are promising candidates for further investigation as nanoscale UCAs; however, direct structural confirmation and in vivo validation are still required.

Scanning electron microscopy showed spherical particles, whereas differential scanning calorimetry indicated the absence of the camphor-associated thermal event after freeze-drying.

papers.title: Pro/Ala/Ser (PAS) peptides as an alternative to polyethylene glycol (PEG) for the surface shielding of lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) carrying therapeutic mRNA
papers.abstract: Abstract Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs), comprising a mixture of cationic lipids, neutral phospholipids, cholesterol and, in particular, polyethylene glycol (PEG)-conjugated lipids on their surface, have emerged as a powerful technology to encapsulate and deliver protein-encoding mRNAs as modern vaccines or for therapeutic intervention. However, the common use of PEG for surface shielding of mRNA-LNPs has raised concerns, especially in the light of a growing prevalence of anti-PEG antibodies in the healthy population. PASylation offers a biological alternative to the chemical PEG polymer, employing recombinant or synthetic (poly)peptides made of the small natural L-amino acids Pro, Ala and Ser which, in contrast to PEG, are biodegradable. PAS sequences are conformationally disordered, fully uncharged but strongly solvated and, thus, closely match the biophysical properties of PEG chains. Based on this notion, we synthesized a novel PASylated lipid, Pga-PAS 40 -ditetradecylamine (PAS-DTA), by replacing the PEG moiety in a clinically approved PEG-lipid (ALC-0159) with a 40mer PAS peptide N-terminally protected with pyroglutamate (Pga). mRNA-LNPs were formulated with this PASylated lipid, adopting a published procedure for conventional LNPs, and their properties were compared with those prepared using common PEG-lipids. To this end, we designed template DNAs for the in vitro transcription (IVT) of mRNA encoding a PASylated murine interferon alpha-11 (mIFNα11) which, when systemically applied, is effective against hepatitis B infection of transgenic mice. mRNA-LNPs formulated with PASylated or PEGylated lipids showed practically identical RNA-encapsulation efficiencies (~ 50%), hydrodynamic diameters (85–120 nm) as well as Zeta potentials (− 4 to − 13 mV). In addition, cultured HepG2 and HEK293E cells transfected with the PASylated mRNA-LNPs encoding either enhanced green fluorescent protein (eGFP) or PAS 200 -mIFNα11 showed robust expression of both recombinant proteins. Furthermore, in a side-by-side experiment with HepG2 cells transfected with mRNA-LNPs that were prepared using PAS-DTA or two different PEG-lipids, comparable or slightly higher amounts of secreted PAS 200 -mIFNα11 were detected in the culture supernatant both by western blotting and ELISA. Taken together, our in vitro data indicate that PAS-lipids offer a viable alternative to PEG-lipids for the preparation of mRNA-LNPs, without immunochemical cross-reactivity but with potentially better tolerability for the transfected target cells.

papers.title: Airborne and marine microplastics in the Northern Indian Ocean: decoupled pathways traced by black carbon
papers.abstract: Microplastics (MPs) have been detected in both marine and atmospheric particulate matter, but their sources, transport, and air–sea exchange remain poorly constrained in remote marine regions. We investigated airborne microplastics (AMPs) and marine microplastics (MMPs) during a 1-month campaign at the Maldives Climate Observatory Hanimaadhoo and in adjacent coastal waters. Airborne particles were collected with a deposition box, and seawater was sampled at coastal sites. Particle morphology, size, and polymer composition were determined by optical microscopy and μ -Raman spectroscopy and evaluated alongside aerosol scattering and equivalent black carbon (eBC). AMP concentrations ranged from 0 to 10.3 MP m −3 (mean: 3.1 ± 2.8 MP m −3 ). MMP concentrations ranged from 120 to 2656 MP m −3 (mean: 876 ± 804 MP m −3 ), exceeding typical open-ocean values and indicating substantial local influence from inhabited islands and maritime activity. Significant differences in size distributions and pronounced compositional differences of AMPs and MMPs suggest weak coupling between the atmospheric and marine reservoirs. Low dry-season wind speeds probably suppressed wave breaking, bubble bursting, and sea-spray-mediated transfer from ocean to atmosphere. Instead, AMP variability coincided with polluted air-mass advection, elevated eBC, and enhanced aerosol scattering, indicating stronger control by regional atmospheric transport than by local marine emissions. These results show that remote island atmospheres are exposed to anthropogenic plastic aerosol transport and demonstrate the value of combining MP observations with established aerosol tracers to resolve plastic-particle pathways in marine environments.

Significant differences in size distributions and pronounced compositional differences of AMPs and MMPs suggest weak coupling between the atmospheric and marine reservoirs. These results show that remote island atmospheres are exposed to anthropogenic plastic aerosol transport and demonstrate the value of combining MP observations with established aerosol tracers to resolve plastic-particle pathways in marine environments.

papers.title: The DE-RADIATE study: protocol for a prospective, non-randomised biomarker-directed phase II study of 18F-FMISO PET-guided radical radiation dose de-escalation in HPV-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma
papers.abstract: Abstract Background HPV-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (HPV OPSCC) has excellent cure rates with standard high-dose radiation therapy (RT) and chemotherapy, but this comes at the cost of substantial long-term toxicity. De-escalation strategies aim to preserve oncologic outcomes while reducing treatment-related morbidity, with ¹⁸F-FMISO PET/CT emerging as a promising biomarker to guide patient selection based on tumour hypoxia. This study builds on prior pilot data to evaluate the feasibility and efficacy of ¹⁸F-FMISO-guided RT de-escalation in an independent healthcare setting and a distinct patient population. Methods DE-RADIATE is a phase II, non-randomised, uncontrolled, single institution prospective interventional study evaluating 18 F-FMISO PET-guided RT de-escalation in patients with AJCC 7th edition clinical stage T1-2N1-2b HPV OPSCC or squamous cell carcinoma of unknown primary of presumed mucosal origin (corresponding to ipsilateral nodal disease ≤ 6 cm, typically cT1-2N1M0 disease per AJCC 8th edition). After surgical resection of primary tumour, patients will commence RT. Patients will undergo 18 F-FMISO PET prior to RT and after two weeks of RT. Patients will be eligible for RT de-escalation (total prescribed dose 30 Gy in 15 fractions) in the absence of hypoxia on intra-treatment PET (irrespective of baseline hypoxia status). Remaining patients will receive standard of care RT to 70 Gy. All patients in both cohorts will receive concurrent platinum-based chemotherapy. Patients in the de-escalated cohort (Cohort A) will undergo neck dissection four months after RT to assess treatment response. Primary endpoint is pathologic complete response rate at neck surgery. Secondary endpoints include locoregional failure​, overall- and progression-free survival, toxicities, patient-reported quality of life, and correlation of hypoxic regions on 18 F-FMISO PET with oxygen-enhanced MRI. Conclusion The results will inform the design of larger prospective trials of hypoxia-guided RT de-escalation and may help identify patients most likely to benefit from reduced RT exposure.
papers.summary: Abstract Background HPV-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (HPV OPSCC) has excellent cure rates with standard high-dose radiation therapy (RT) and chemotherapy, but this comes at the cost of substantial long-term toxicity. Methods DE-RADIATE is a phase II, non-randomised, uncontrolled, single institution prospective interventional study evaluating 18 F-FMISO PET-guided RT de-escalation in patients with AJCC 7th edition clinical stage T1-2N1-2b HPV OPSCC or squamous cell carcinoma of unknown primary of presumed mucosal origin (corresponding to ipsilateral nodal disease ≤ 6 cm, typically cT1-2N1M0 disease per AJCC 8th edition). Conclusion The results will inform the design of larger prospective trials of hypoxia-guided RT de-escalation and may help identify patients most likely to benefit from reduced RT exposure.

papers.title: CAIGAN study protocol: complement activation in primary IgA nephropathy—study protocol for an international prospective multicenter observational cohort study
papers.abstract: Abstract Background IgA nephropathy (IgAN) is the most common primary glomerular disease worldwide and a leading cause of chronic kidney disease and kidney failure. Increasing evidence supports a central role for complement activation in disease severity and crescent formation. With the emergence of complement-targeted therapies, biomarkers identifying patients with active complement dysregulation are increasingly needed. Methods CAIGAN (Complement Activation in IgA Nephropathy) is an international, prospective, observational multicenter cohort study involving adult and pediatric nephrology centers in Switzerland, Italy, France, and Spain. Consecutive patients undergoing clinically indicated native kidney biopsy for suspected IgAN will be screened, and those with biopsy-proven primary IgAN will be enrolled. Clinical and laboratory follow-up data will be collected from routine care every six months for three years, with additional three-month data included where available. Blood and urine samples for complement analyses will generally be obtained after histopathological confirmation of IgAN, within 4 weeks after kidney biopsy and before initiation of immunosuppressive therapy. In patients with a rapidly progressive clinical course requiring prompt immunosuppressive treatment, sampling may precede histopathological confirmation and will be performed after informed consent and before administration of immunosuppressive agents. Complement profiling will include circulating complement proteins and activation products, functional pathway assessment, and complement-related genetic analyses. Kidney biopsies will be characterized using the Oxford MEST-C classification, with intrarenal complement deposition assessed in a subgroup. The primary objective is to validate prospectively the association observed in our retrospective pilot study between circulating sC5b-9 concentrations and the percentage of active glomerular crescents. Secondary exploratory objectives include characterization of the mechanisms underlying complement activation and dysregulation and evaluation of their associations with clinical phenotype, histopathological findings, renal tissue complement activation, genetic profiles, and longitudinal kidney outcomes. Discussion CAIGAN will integrate complement phenotyping, genetics, histopathology, and prospective clinical follow-up to characterize complement activation across the spectrum of primary IgAN and possibly support the development of biomarker-guided therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: The optical colors of hidden spiral-like features in nine Virgo early-type dwarfs
papers.abstract: Dwarf early-type galaxies (ETGs) are abundant in nearby clusters, offering a key laboratory for studying environmentally driven galaxy transformation. Although dwarf ETGs were once considered structurally simple, deep imaging has revealed embedded spiral-like features (e.g., bars and spiral arms) in some of them, contributing only a small fraction of the total galaxy light. The origin of these features at dwarf scales remains uncertain. As a pilot study, we investigated the nature of spiral-like features in nine Virgo dwarf ETGs with clear embedded arms. Our goal is to use optical colors to test whether these features differ from the surrounding diffuse component, which would constrain their formation pathways. In doing so, we established the methodology on a well-characterized sample, ahead of a future analysis of the much larger NGVS dwarf sample. Using deep (g)- and (i)-band images from the NGVS, we applied a residual-based image analysis method to separate excess light associated with the spiral-like component from the diffuse host. The residual images are used to define the arm and interarm regions, enabling direct measurements of light fractions and (g-i) colors for the spiral-like feature and the diffuse component in which they are embedded. The spiral-like features contribute only a few percent of the total galaxy light (approximately ( 1.5%!-!5.5%) in (i) and ( 1.7%!-!3.7%) in (g)). We find a diverse range of stellar colors across the sample: four galaxies host spiral-like features that are redder than their interarm regions, four show no robust color difference between the arm and interarm regions, and one exhibits a distinctly bluer spiral-like component. The latter is consistent with a recently quenched transition object, while the redder and color-uniform features are consistent with an older or more metal-rich stellar population. Spiral-like features in Virgo dwarf ETGs exhibit a surprising diversity in their photometric properties, implying that there are multiple evolutionary channels at work, rather than a single one. This pilot analysis also demonstrates the readiness for the much larger NGVS sample of dwarfs with potential spiral-like features.
papers.summary: Dwarf early-type galaxies (ETGs) are abundant in nearby clusters, offering a key laboratory for studying environmentally driven galaxy transformation. Using deep (g)- and (i)-band images from the NGVS, we applied a residual-based image analysis method to separate excess light associated with the spiral-like component from the diffuse host. This pilot analysis also demonstrates the readiness for the much larger NGVS sample of dwarfs with potential spiral-like features.

papers.title: A B ← N framework for highly selective adsorption of toluene
papers.abstract: Differentiating toluene (Tol) from xylene isomers is critical yet challenging in industry due to their nearly identical physicochemical properties. Here, we report the design of a B ← N framework that exhibits high adsorption selectivity for Tol over xylenes. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction analyses of the host-guest complexes and DFT calculations reveal that the selectivity stems from precise size matching and electronic complementarity.

papers.title: Aralar liver-specific knockout and citrin knockout mouse: a new citrin deficiency model with near-complete hepatic depletion of mitochondrial aspartate-glutamate carriers
papers.abstract: Citrin Deficiency (CD) is a metabolic disorder caused by mutations in CITRIN/SLC25A13/AGC2 , which encodes the hepatic mitochondrial aspartate–glutamate carrier (AGC), CITRIN. Loss of CITRIN-mediated aspartate export from mitochondria, either as part of the malate–aspartate shuttle (MAS) or through independent transport activity, underlies key clinical features including hypoglycemia, hyperammonemia, and aversion to carbohydrates and alcohol. Progress in the research of CD mechanisms and therapies has been hindered by lack of adequate models for the condition. For example, the citrin knockout mouse fails to recapitulate the human CD phenotype in vivo, likely due to compensatory expression of the neuronal AGC isoform aralar in murine liver, while the double citrin/glycerophosphate dehydrogenase 2 (gpd2) knockout mouse might present confounding results due to global gpd2 ablation. These limitations underscore the need for a physiologically relevant disease model to support translational research. We generated a double knockout (DLKO) mouse combining global deletion of citrin with liver-specific deletion of aralar using Cre-LoxP technology, resulting in a marked reduction of mitochondrial AGC-MAS activity in hepatocytes. Primary hepatocytes were used to assess cytosolic NADH/NAD⁺ ratios, gluconeogenesis, and urea production. In vivo characterization included biochemical and behavioral analyses, as well as indirect calorimetry to evaluate systemic metabolism. DLKO hepatocytes exhibited elevated cytosolic NADH/NAD⁺ ratios, severely impaired glucose production from lactate, and reduced urea synthesis. These alterations translated in vivo into key features of CD, including hypoglycemia, limited urea cycle capacity, and marked hepatic triglyceride accumulation in the absence of overt liver injury. Behavioral analyses revealed aversion to alcohol and carbohydrates, closely mirroring patient’s food preferences. Importantly, DLKO mice exhibit sex-associated metabolic adaptations: males show growth retardation, hyperphagia, increased energy expenditure, and elevated circulating FGF21 levels, whereas females demonstrate normal food intake and a shift toward lipid metabolism without changes in FGF21. The DLKO mouse represents a robust and physiologically relevant model for the study of Citrin Deficiency. This model overcomes limitations of previous approaches, uncovers distinct systemic metabolic responses in males and females to hepatic MAS dysfunction, and provides a powerful platform for mechanistic studies and preclinical evaluation of therapeutic strategies for CD.

papers.title: University Students’ Experiences and Participation in Using Online Teaching and Learning at a Zimbabwean State University
papers.journal: Journal of Research Innovation and Implications in Education
papers.abstract: The fact that even well before the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic online teaching and learning approaches to modern students` education and training programs were already being used in some countries cannot be denied.This mixed methods research study sought to explore university students' experiences and participation in online teaching and learning after the Covid-19 pandemic.Thirty (n=30) conveniently sampled first year students who were using online teaching and learning completed a structured questionnaire to indicate the approximate amount of time they spent on the internet each week, while10 of them participated in semi-structured interviews.Students expressed an admixture of experiences with using online teaching and learning pedagogies ranging from independent learning, cost-cutting advantages, improved use of ICT for teaching and learning to estrangement from using the unfamiliar technology, lack of resources, poor internet connectivity and difficulties in learning concepts in some subjects.Findings of this study also revealed a situation in which students indicated negligible participation in the use of internet facilities; the bedrock of online pedagogies.Recommendations were made for universities to: 1. rethink strategies and policies for enhancing more sustainable adoption and institutionalisation of the online teaching and learning pedagogies.2. Establish strategies for subsidizing students' connectivity costs 3. Establish strategies for improvement of online infrastructural facilities and 4. Facilitate the availability of online hardware devices to students, such as smartphones.

papers.title: How do dietitians estimate resting energy expenditure? A national survey of knowledge, perceptions and utilisation of metabolic rate equations
papers.abstract: Background Metabolic-rate prediction equations remain widely used when indirect calorimetry (IC) is unavailable, despite recognised limitations in their accuracy across patient populations. Evidence on how dietitians understand and apply these tools in practice remains limited. Objective To assess knowledge, perceptions, and utilisation of metabolic-rate prediction equations among dietitians in the Czech Republic, including IC accessibility and factors associated with equation utilisation. Methods A nationwide cross-sectional online survey was conducted between January and March 2026. The survey assessed IC accessibility, knowledge of metabolic-rate equations, perceptions of their importance and accuracy, perceived barriers, and utilisation practices. Results Among 181 eligible respondents, IC was accessible to 15.5% of respondents, and most users applied it in fewer than 40% of cases. Mean knowledge score was 3.40 ± 1.36/7, with no significant overall differences by education, practice duration, setting, or IC accessibility. Only 7.2% correctly recognised that none of the listed prediction equations achieved estimates within ±10% of IC measurements in 90% of White adults. Harris–Benedict was the dominant equation in both perceived usefulness and practice, being considered useful by 71.3% and reported as utilised by 84.5% of respondents. Weight-loss management was the most common indication for equation use (80.1%), followed by oncological patients (35.9%) and patients with diabetes (32.0%). Greater perceived importance of equations (aOR = 4.54, 95% CI 3.24–6.38) was independently associated with more frequent utilisation. Conclusion Czech dietitians showed limited knowledge of equation limitations, low IC access, and substantial reliance on Harris–Benedict. Updated education and improved access to objective metabolic assessment may strengthen evidence-based dietetic practice.
papers.summary: Background Metabolic-rate prediction equations remain widely used when indirect calorimetry (IC) is unavailable, despite recognised limitations in their accuracy across patient populations. Results Among 181 eligible respondents, IC was accessible to 15.5% of respondents, and most users applied it in fewer than 40% of cases. Conclusion Czech dietitians showed limited knowledge of equation limitations, low IC access, and substantial reliance on Harris–Benedict.

papers.title: Ovarian pregnancy in a spontaneous conception cycle following ipsilateral salpingectomy: a case report
papers.abstract: This report details the diagnosis and management of a rare case of ipsilateral primary ovarian pregnancy occurring six years after right salpingectomy. The patient had undergone right salpingectomy for a prior right tubal ectopic pregnancy. During the current pregnancy, three serial transvaginal ultrasound examinations were performed at our hospital, culminating in a definitive diagnosis of right ovarian pregnancy, confirmed intraoperatively and histopathologically. Laparoscopic resection of the ectopic gestational tissue was successfully performed. The patient recovered well after surgery, and her serum β -human chorionic gonadotropin ( β -hCG) level returned to normal at the one-month postoperative follow-up. Primary ovarian pregnancy is a rare condition, its occurrence following ipsilateral salpingectomy is exceedingly rare. This disease carries a high risk of diagnostic delay or misdiagnosis, potentially resulting in life-threatening rupture and hemorrhage. Thus, timely identification of this condition is critical. This article describes the causes, clinical features and treatment process of this rare ectopic pregnancy, and also discusses the related issues in its differential diagnosis. This case report serves two primary Objectives: first, to illustrate the diagnostic criteria and characteristic clinical manifestations of ovarian pregnancy; second, to raise clinical awareness of ovarian pregnancy as a rare but critical complication following ipsilateral salpingectomy.

papers.title: Surface Engineering of CdTe Quantum Dots for Improved Optical Stability and QLED Applications: A Review
papers.abstract: In the past several years, quantum dots (QDs) have gained considerable attention due to their unique properties and wide range of applications. Nevertheless, drawbacks and limitations of QDs still exist and affect their practical use. This review investigates surface engineering strategies that enhance optical stability and examines their application in quantum dot light-emitting diodes (QLEDs). It compares passivation mechanisms, advantages, and inherent limitations of organic ligand engineering (including small-molecule, long-chain, and multifunctional ligands) and inorganic shell engineering (including ZnS and CdS shells). It analyzes how these surface modifications impact optical stability, luminescent behavior, and QLED device performance. Furthermore, it discusses the significant challenges that researchers are facing, such as insufficient optical stability of CdTe QDs, long-term stability degradation, the complexity of regulating ligand–QD interactions, and the difficulty of balancing optical stability with charge transport. This review also clarifies the correlation between surface chemistry and optical stability of CdTe QDs, and outlines future research directions. It provides guidance for developing high-stability CdTe QDs for high-performance QLED applications.
papers.summary: In the past several years, quantum dots (QDs) have gained considerable attention due to their unique properties and wide range of applications. This review investigates surface engineering strategies that enhance optical stability and examines their application in quantum dot light-emitting diodes (QLEDs). It provides guidance for developing high-stability CdTe QDs for high-performance QLED applications.

papers.title: From single‑target conservation to comprehensive resource utilization: A case of VEP accounting for the eco-cultural heritage in Beijing
papers.abstract: Eco-cultural heritage faces the dilemma of transitioning from single-target conservation to comprehensive resource utilization. This study introduces the Value of Ecosystem Product in specific geographical units (VEP) theory to address this challenge, using Beijing’s Three Hills and Five Gardens as a case study. The research develops a three-dimensional analytical framework encompassing value identification, composite accounting, and layered transformation. Theoretically, it extends VEP from natural ecosystems to eco‑cultural composite systems by proposing a “three‑tier progressive” evaluation paradigm that distinguishes monetizable, quantifiable cultural services with partial monetization, and non‑quantifiable values, together with a “layered matching” transformation principle. This framework clarifies the identification criteria and transformation pathways for each value type while defining a normative “monetization boundary” that protects non‑tradable values from market forces. A simplified accounting of the Western Beijing rice fields is provided to illustrate the framework’s application in principle; this is a methodological demonstration rather than an empirical valuation, as it relies on secondary data and hypothetical assumptions rather than primary field surveys. The study also outlines a three-stage transformation model covering activation, appreciation, and realization, and identifies governance bottlenecks including fragmented property rights. The central argument is that value transformation should distinguish between tradable and non‑tradable values, and achieve a virtuous cycle of conservation and development through the synergy of market mechanisms and public safeguards. Policy implications are offered for the valuation and transformation of eco‑cultural heritage, though the proposed framework requires further empirical testing across diverse heritage contexts.

The central argument is that value transformation should distinguish between tradable and non‑tradable values, and achieve a virtuous cycle of conservation and development through the synergy of market mechanisms and public safeguards.

papers.title: Recent advances in production and optimization of bacterial cellulose/CMC/hydroxyapatite composite for biological targets: antibacterial, antioxidant, and wound healing
papers.abstract: Abstract The demand for sustainable medical biocomposites has intensified the search for biocompatible, eco-friendly alternatives. This study showed that the optimal cultivation conditions identified by the fractional factorial design (Run 6) resulted in a maximum bacterial cellulose yield of 2.3085 mg/L by Citrobacter freundii . Novel BC/carboxymethyl cellulose/hydroxyapatite (BC/CMC/HAp) composite was prepared and the effect of low-dose gamma irradiation (2.5, 5, and 10 kGy) was studied. FT-IR, XRD, ESR, TGA, zeta potential, SEM-EDX, and TEM analyses confirmed successful composite integration. TEM imaging revealed distinct nanocrystalline morphology with particles size of 34.2–125.5 nm. To enhance biological functionality, the matrices (5, 10, and 20 mg/mL) were integrated with plant extracts (clove, rosemary, and Aloe vera at 5 % and 10 % w/v). Antibacterial efficacy was evaluated against Staphylococcus epidermidis , Bacillus cereus , Escherichia coli , and Klebsiella pneumoniae . The 10 kGy-irradiated BC/CMC/HAp-Clove 10 % composite exhibited the most potent antibacterial activity, producing an inhibition zone of 37.47 ± 2.32 mm against S. epidermidis , while the highest biofilm inhibition was against K. pneumoniae by 61.2 ± 2.65%. This formulation demonstrated excellent cytocompatibility with normal epithelial cells, low hemolytic activity (IC 50 = 10.92 ± 0.23), and robust radical scavenging activity (97.5 % at 1000 µg/mL). In vitro scratching assays confirmed accelerated wound closure of 91.76 %. These findings suggest that low-dose gamma irradiation, when combined with medicinal plant extracts, mayenhance the biological performance of the BC/CMC/HAp composite and offer potential for its sterilization. The prepared BC/CMC/HAp composite could be an effective, eco-friendly alternative to chemical-based wound management.

papers.title: Diagnostic performance of APRI, FIB-4, and shear wave elastography for liver fibrosis assessment in children with chronic liver disease: impact of necroinflammatory activity in an autoimmune hepatitis–dominated cohort
papers.abstract: Background Liver fibrosis staging is central to managing children with chronic liver disease (CLD). Serum indices and shear wave elastography (SWE) offer non-invasive assessment, but pediatric validation remains limited. We evaluated the aspartate aminotransferase-to-platelet ratio index (APRI), fibrosis-4 (FIB-4), and two-dimensional SWE against biopsy fibrosis stage and explored associations with activity. Methods This prospective cross-sectional study included 45 children aged 6–18 years with CLD; eight of 53 recruited children could not complete SWE. Biopsy reports were retrieved from records. Continuous-marker diagnostic accuracy and exploratory numerical SWE-category agreement were evaluated. Results Autoimmune hepatitis (AIH) accounted for 27/45 (60%); all had recorded immunosuppression. Biopsy stages were F1 in 11, F2 in eight, F3 in 22, and F4 in four patients. APRI, FIB-4, and SWE correlated with fibrosis stage (Spearman rho 0.72, 0.68, 0.77; all p < 0.001). Areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve for significant fibrosis (≥F2) were 0.91, 0.85, and 0.92, and for cirrhosis were 0.88, 0.90, and 0.83, respectively. Exploratory SWE categories were concordant with biopsy in 40%, higher in 40%, and lower in 20% (weighted kappa 0.753). Median AST in higher-category, concordant and lower-category groups was 78.5, 56.0 and 33.0 U/L (overall p = 0.010). Observed cirrhosis negative predictive values were 100%, but estimates were based on four F4 cases. Conclusion The markers were associated with fibrosis stage, but cohort-derived thresholds and cirrhosis estimates require independent validation. Higher transaminases accompanied higher numerical SWE categories relative to biopsy; non-pediatric thresholds, temporal uncertainty, and biopsy sampling limitations preclude attributing discordance independently to inflammation.

Continuous-marker diagnostic accuracy and exploratory numerical SWE-category agreement were evaluated. papers.title: Process intensification of pectin extraction from dragon fruit peels using combined cold plasma and ultrasonication: optimization and functional properties
papers.abstract: Dragon fruit (Hylocereus spp.) peel is an underutilized agricultural side-stream and an excellent source of pectin, which can be efficiently extracted. In this paper, we developed a sustainable extraction strategy using cold atmospheric plasma (CAP) pretreatment along with ultrasound-assisted extraction (US), which addresses the limitations of conventional acid-thermal extraction. Response Surface Methodology was used to determine the plasma voltage, treatment time, ultrasonic power, and sonication time for pectin extraction. In terms of the effect of the CAP-US process, the extraction coefficients were higher in comparison to individual and traditional extraction techniques. The optimized process resulted in a pectin yield of up to 10.8%, with an acceptable GalA, retained high-methoxyl pectin characteristics (DE >70%), and the desired molecular and functional features. FTIR and XRD were also performed to confirm that the pectin structure was still preserved. CAP-US is an efficient, non-thermal, and resource-effective method to extract functional pectin from dragon fruit peel and is a valuable addition to a circular bioeconomy.

papers.title: Eco-friendly preparation and characterization of avocado waste-derived silver nanoparticles-embedded alginate films for potential wound dressing use
papers.journal: Journal of Metals Materials and Minerals
papers.abstract: The ever-increasing volume of waste generated in the avocado industry poses an environmental problem; however, thanks to the valuable bio-components contained within this waste, this situation presents a potential to be transformed from a problem into an opportunity. In this study, silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) were synthesized using a green method with avocado peel extract as a biogenic reducing and stabilizing agent; the synthesized AgNPs were embedded into sodium alginate (SA) films to obtain functional biomaterials for wound dressing applications. The changes in physicochemical properties (Water resistance, swelling index, gel fraction, degradation behavior, and water vapor transmission rate (WVTR)) of the prepared AgNPs@SA films were investigated by varying the amounts of their components (alginate amount, AgNO3 concentration, and extract concentration). In terms of the obtained physicochemical properties, the film formulation using 2.0 g alginate, 2.0 mM AgNO3, and 0.20 g·mL‒1 extract was selected as optimum. The film synthesized with the determined optimum formulation was found to have an average thickness of 0.351 mm, a suitable WVTR value, and antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Mechanical analysis results show that AgNPs@SA films exhibit a ductile and viscoelastic structure characterized by high elongation and sufficient tensile strength, indicating potential for use as a flexible and stable wound dressing. Characterization studies (SEM, EDX, FTIR, XRD, and XPS) supported the successful green synthesis of AgNPs and provided evidence consistent with their incorporation into the alginate films, while indicating the involvement of plant-derived components in nanoparticle synthesis. The findings indicate that avocado peel waste can be transformed into a value-added product for environmentally friendly wound dressing applications.

Mechanical analysis results show that AgNPs@SA films exhibit a ductile and viscoelastic structure characterized by high elongation and sufficient tensile strength, indicating potential for use as a flexible and stable wound dressing. papers.title: Genipin-Crosslinked Chitosan Hydrogel Scaffolds as Bioactive Delivery Platforms for Osseous Tissue Repair: Design Principles, Physicochemical Characterization and Preclinical Evaluation Strategies
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Reconstruction of large osseous defects remains a major clinical challenge in orthopaedics and craniofacial surgery because autografts are limited by donor-site morbidity, whereas allografts and synthetic substitutes seldom combine osteoconduction, osteoinduction and tunable degradation. Chitosan, a cationic polysaccharide structurally related to glycosaminoglycans, forms hydrogels and porous scaffolds that support cell adhesion and can carry bioactive cargo, but its weak mechanical strength and rapid, uncontrolled degradation limit its unmodified use as a bone scaffold. Genipin, a naturally derived iridoid crosslinker, covalently bridges chitosan amine groups and has shown markedly lower cytotoxicity than glutaraldehyde, allowing the stability, stiffness, swelling and degradation of the network to be tuned for bone applications. This review integrates bone biology, tissue-engineering principles, the chemistry of genipin crosslinking and the design variables that govern scaffold performance. Physicochemical characterization by FTIR, SEM, XRD, TGA, DSC, swelling and water-uptake studies, porosity determination, in-vitro degradation and compressive testing is critically examined, together with biological readouts and preclinical models.
papers.summary: Reconstruction of large osseous defects remains a major clinical challenge in orthopaedics and craniofacial surgery because autografts are limited by donor-site morbidity, whereas allografts and synthetic substitutes seldom combine osteoconduction, osteoinduction and tunable degradation. Genipin, a naturally derived iridoid crosslinker, covalently bridges chitosan amine groups and has shown markedly lower cytotoxicity than glutaraldehyde, allowing the stability, stiffness, swelling and degradation of the network to be tuned for bone applications. papers.title: Development and Characterization of Propylene Imine-Loaded Convolivine Dendrosomes for the Management of Neurodegenerative Diseases: A Comprehensive Review
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases are gradually developing diseases of progressive loss of structure and function of neurons; due to the complex and multifaceted pathophysiology of neurodegenerative diseases, there is a great challenge in their therapeutic management. Pathological mechanisms associated with these diseases include protein aggregation abnormalities, impaired autophagy, neuronal apoptosis, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and neuroinflammation in Parkinson’s disease, Huntington's disease, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis [2,3,5,8]. The progression of these disorders is also complicated by the blood–brain barrier (BBB), which can rigorously control the movement of molecules across the barrier and restrict the delivery of many therapeutic agents [1,4,7,14]. In this context, the development of efficient drug delivery devices towards the brain has become a key research direction in the fields of pharmaceutical and nanomedicine. The highly-branched nanoscale macromolecules called dendrimers have gained significant research interest as drug delivery systems due to their well-defined structure, surface functionality, internal cavities useful for accommodating drug molecules, the ability to conjugate and decorate their surface, and the ability to self-assemble into distinct particles [21-24]. The terminal functional groups enable the chemical modification of PPI dendrimers, and the nanoscale structure can be tailored to develop approaches in drug delivery and targeting, which makes them very interesting for neurological applications [23,29]. Recent research has shown that surface-functionalized PPI dendrimers can enhance their delivery into the brain and their cellular uptake, while retaining some of the advantages concerning the highly cationic dendritic systems [31,32]. The use of a natural product payload is a further objective that can be investigated in this platform, and convolivine, a compound found in Convolvulus species, could be a potential natural product payload since experimental evidence for the use of a convolivine-loaded PPI dendrosome remains to be established [33]. In the present review, the pathological basis of neurodegenerative diseases, the role of the BBB in restricting the entry of drugs into the CNS, structural and pharmaceutical properties of dendrimers and PPI dendrimers are discussed, and the rationale behind the development of propylene imine-loaded convolivine dendrosomes is discussed at last. In particular, formulation development and characterization, particle size, PDI, zeta potential, Cellular uptake, BBB transport, biological safety, morphology, drug-loading, entrapment efficiency, and in vitro release of the drug are given special mention. The review also analyzes existing evidence for the feasibility of dendrimer-mediated CNS delivery, significant research gaps, and future directions that need to be explored to improve the usage of PPI-based dendrosomal systems. Taking all this into consideration, propylene imine-loaded convolivine dendrosomes are a new, interesting research idea to improve brain targeting, but more systematic disease-appropriate, pharmaceutical, pharmacokinetic, and toxicological studies are required to confirm their therapeutic applications.

The terminal functional groups enable the chemical modification of PPI dendrimers, and the nanoscale structure can be tailored to develop approaches in drug delivery and targeting, which makes them very interesting for neurological applications [23,29]. The use of a natural product payload is a further objective that can be investigated in this platform, and convolivine, a compound found in Convolvulus species, could be a potential natural product payload since experimental evidence for the use of a convolivine-loaded PPI dendrosome remains to be established [33].

papers.title: Sustainable Waterborne Polyurethane-Based Coatings with Self-Healing Capability for the Protection of Bronze Artworks
papers.abstract: Abstract Waterborne polyurethane (WPU) coatings have emerged as promising sustainable alternatives to conventional solvent-based systems for the protection of cultural heritage objects. The incorporation of intrinsic self-healing functionality is particularly attractive for conservation, as it allows restoring coating integrity after mechanical damage, reducing maintenance interventions, and preserving the long-term integrity of protected artifacts. In this work, self-healing WPU coatings for the protection of bronze substrates were developed by incorporating different amounts of 4-aminophenyl disulfide (APDS), providing intrinsic healing through aromatic disulfide exchange. The effect of APDS content on the chemical structure, thermal behavior, mechanical properties, and self-healing performance was systematically investigated. To promote self-healing at temperatures compatible with cultural heritage conservation, the optimized formulation was physically blended with polyethylene glycol (PEG), which acts as a plasticizer. FTIR, DSC, and DMA analyses indicated that PEG increased the polymer chain mobility at low temperatures. As a result, the self-healing temperature was reduced from 80 °C for WPU to 40 °C for the PEG-containing formulations. Accelerated corrosion tests in HCl vapors demonstrated that PEG also improved the barrier performance of the coatings, while the incorporation of benzotriazole further enhanced corrosion resistance, maintaining the integrity of the bronze substrate after prolonged exposure. In addition, all coatings exhibited color variations below the acceptability threshold for conservation, satisfying a key requirement for cultural heritage applications. Overall, PEG-plasticized, disulfide-based WPUs offer an environmentally friendly and multifunctional strategy for low-temperature self-healing and durable protection of bronze cultural heritage artifacts.

The effect of APDS content on the chemical structure, thermal behavior, mechanical properties, and self-healing performance was systematically investigated. Accelerated corrosion tests in HCl vapors demonstrated that PEG also improved the barrier performance of the coatings, while the incorporation of benzotriazole further enhanced corrosion resistance, maintaining the integrity of the bronze substrate after prolonged exposure.

papers.title: Deubiquitination of C/EBPβ by FAM63A mediates resistance to glutaminolysis inhibition in MYC-amplified hepatocellular carcinoma
papers.abstract: Abstract Oncogenic MYC amplification drives glutamine addiction in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), rendering glutaminase (GLS) a promising therapeutic target. However, MYC-amplified HCC frequently exhibits intrinsic resistance to the GLS inhibitor CB-839, with the underlying adaptive survival mechanisms remaining elusive. Here, we demonstrate that MYC-high HCC cells critically depend on mitofusin 1 (MFN1)-mediated mitochondrial fusion to maintain survival under glutaminolysis inhibition. Furthermore, we show that glutaminolysis inhibition enhances the stability of CCAAT/enhancer-binding protein β (C/EBPβ), which directly activates MFN1 transcription. Mechanistically, MYC-dependent transactivation of FAM63A mediates the deubiquitination of C/EBPβ, specifically suppressing its K48-linked polyubiquitination to enhance C/EBPβ protein stability under glutamine deprivation. Importantly, inhibition of C/EBPβ abrogates MFN1-mediated mitochondrial fusion and triggers autophagic cell death, thereby sensitizing MYC-high HCC cells to GLS inhibition. Our findings identify a novel MYC-FAM63A-C/EBPβ-MFN1 signaling axis that confers adaptive resistance to GLS inhibitors in MYC-high HCC by sustaining mitochondrial fusion. Thus, targeting C/EBPβ represents a promising combinatorial therapeutic strategy to overcome CB-839 resistance in this clinically challenging HCC subtype.

papers.title: Cancer-associated fibroblast-derived lactate drives cholangiocarcinoma progression via H4K12la-mediated oxidative phosphorylation activation
papers.abstract: Background: Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) is a highly aggressive malignancy, and chemoresistance is a major cause of poor prognosis. This study aimed to elucidate the molecular mechanisms driving CCA progression from a tumor microenvironment perspective and to develop novel strategies to enhance chemosensitivity. Methods: Single-cell RNA-seq, untargeted metabolomics, and proteomics were used to identify the source of lactate in the CCA microenvironment and the metabolic reprogramming of cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs). To evaluate the impact of CAF-derived lactate on prognosis, we performed AAV-mediated MCT4 knockdown followed by hydrodynamic injection to induce a CCA model. Co-culture models were combined with genome-wide CUT&Tag, MeRIP-seq, and RIP-seq to resolve epigenetic and post-transcriptional regulatory mechanisms. The antitumor effects of 7ACC1 (a small molecule reported to inhibit lactate uptake), alone or in combination with gemcitabine, were assessed in subcutaneous and orthotopic liver xenograft models. Results: CAFs undergo glycolytic reprogramming, resulting in aberrant lactate accumulation. Mechanistically, CAF-derived lactate induces H4K12 lactylation (H4K12la) in CCA cells, which in turn activates the IGF2BP3/ATF3 axis to upregulate oxidative phosphorylation and promote tumor progression. The lactate shuttle inhibitor 7ACC1, combined with gemcitabine, exerts promising antitumor effects. Clinically, high levels of MCT4, α SMA, and H4K12la are associated with poor prognosis in patients with CCA. Conclusions: These findings reveal that CAFs drive CCA progression via lactate-induced H4K12la, which activates the IGF2BP3/ATF3 axis. The findings provide a preclinical rationale for further evaluation of lactate-uptake-targeting strategies in combination with gemcitabine for CCA.

papers.title: AI Personalization and Travel Booking Intention in GenAI-Assisted Travel Planning: The Roles of Recommendation Relevance, Perceived Decision Autonomy, and Travel Decision Satisfaction
papers.journal: Advances in management and applied economics
papers.abstract: This study examines the relationships among AI personalization, recommendation relevance, perceived decision autonomy, travel decision satisfaction, and travel booking intention in generative artificial intelligence (GenAI)-assisted travel planning. An online survey using convenience sampling yielded 348 valid responses from consumers in Taiwan aged 20 years and older with experience using GenAI for travel planning. Structural equation modeling was used to test seven hypotheses. The model demonstrated good fit, and six hypotheses were supported. AI personalization was positively associated with recommendation relevance and perceived decision autonomy. Recommendation relevance was positively associated with perceived decision autonomy, and both constructs were positively associated with travel decision satisfaction. The direct association between perceived decision autonomy and travel booking intention was not significant after accounting for travel decision satisfaction. The path from travel decision satisfaction to travel booking intention had the largest standardized coefficient. These findings distinguish perceived personalization from recommendation relevance and clarify the different roles of autonomy and satisfaction in travel decision-making. For practitioners, the findings suggest that tourism platforms and GenAI service providers should offer recommendations aligned with consumers’ needs, preserve their autonomy over choices, and improve the decision-making experience. The study provides evidence to inform the design of GenAI travel recommendation services. JEL classification numbers: D12, L83, O33. Keywords: Generative artificial intelligence, AI personalization, Perceived decision autonomy, Travel booking intention.

papers.title: Physiological and transcriptomic analyses reveal the inhibitory effect of pelargonic acid on adventitious root primordia formation in tissue culture seedlings of Toxicodendron succedaneum
papers.abstract: Introduction The lacquer tree synthesizes pelargonic acid as a secondary metabolite, which exerts an autotoxic effect on its tissue-cultured seedlings by inhibiting adventitious root formation. The inhibitory effect of pelargonic acid on adventitious root primordium formation has not been previously reported. This study examined the physiological and molecular mechanisms by which pelargonic acid prevents adventitious root primordia from forming in tissue-cultured Toxicodendron succedaneum seedlings. Methods Microscopic analysis was used to examine adventitious root primordium formation, and rooting rates were recorded. Physiological indicators, including malondialdehyde, soluble sugar, soluble protein, peroxidase, superoxide dismutase, catalase, and endogenous hormones, were measured in stem bases of tissue-cultured seedlings under control and pelargonic acid treatments. Transcriptome sequencing and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) were further performed to identify differentially expressed genes, hormone-related modules, and hub genes. Results The tissue-cultured seedlings of T. succedaneum had no latent adventitious root primordia, and pelargonic acid dramatically reduced the induction of adventitious root primordium formation; on day 45, the rooting rate was only 36.3%. Compared with the control, the pelargonic acid-treated group showed increased malondialdehyde, decreased soluble sugar and soluble protein, and an initial increase followed by a decrease in peroxidase, superoxide dismutase, and catalase activities. Pelargonic acid also disturbed hormonal balance: trans-zeatin riboside levels increased, indole-3-acetic acid concentration decreased considerably, and jasmonic acid and abscisic acid levels first decreased and then increased. Transcriptome analysis revealed that many genes in the plant hormone signal pathway were down-regulated. WGCNA identified four of 27 modules substantially correlated with IAA, ZR, ABA, and JA, respectively, and nine hub genes (RPS16, GSVIVT00020038001, T3_jg26140.t1, FZR3, CURT1B, IAA8, FRL4A, FLA11, and ACA13) plus one transcription factor-encoding gene (ASIL2) potentially important in pelargonic acid-mediated suppression of adventitious primordium formation; among these, the hub gene IAA8 is located within the plant hormone signal pathway. Discussion These results suggest that PA inhibits ARP formation by competing with IAA for PIN1 binding and disrupting auxin homeostasis, together with oxidative damage and secondary metabolic reprogramming. Crosstalk among IAA, cytokinin, ABA, and JA further contributes to this inhibition. Collectively, this study provides evidence that indole-3-acetic acid plays an important role in adventitious root primordium formation and highlights the involvement of the hormone signal pathway in the key gene network regulating this process. This work offers a multi-level framework for understanding PA-mediated rooting inhibition in lacquer trees, although the proposed PA–PIN1 mechanism requires direct experimental validation in future studies.

Transcriptome analysis revealed that many genes in the plant hormone signal pathway were down-regulated. Discussion These results suggest that PA inhibits ARP formation by competing with IAA for PIN1 binding and disrupting auxin homeostasis, together with oxidative damage and secondary metabolic reprogramming.

papers.title: Green Electrochemical Synthesis of Antimicrobial Polyaldehyde Starch
papers.abstract: Abstract Conventional aldehyde-based biocides raise environmental and safety concerns due to their toxicity and persistence in inhibiting microbiologically influenced corrosion (MIC) in numerous industrial applications. The present study introduces a rapid and sustainable method for synthesizing polyaldehyde starch through electrochemistry (PAS-EC) using soluble starch as feedstock in aqueous salt media with iridium–ruthenium electrodes. This approach has the potential to replace toxic oxidants with a safer alternative, while significantly reducing reaction time and enhancing overall process safety. By minimizing hazardous reagents and streamlining operational steps, it can also contribute to improved sustainability. Taken together, these features make electrochemical methods a promising pathway for application in industrial bioprocesses. Under optimized electrochemical conditions (15 mA cm–2, 15% NaCl, and 1 h), PAS-EC was obtained with 65% yield and a degree of oxidation exceeding 63%, surpassing the conventional periodate-oxidized dialdehyde starch (DAS-PO) with 50% yield and a 48% degree of oxidation. FTIR and NMR characterization confirmed the successful formation of aldehydic groups, while thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) revealed a decrease in thermal stability due to the modification in the structure of pure starch. Biocidal efficacy was assessed against six hydrocarbon-degrading bacterial strains that are extremely relevant to MIC and bioremediation under oil and gas field conditions. PAS-EC displayed promising and broad-spectrum antibacterial activity, with a maximum of 60% inhibition efficiency at 1000 ppm in comparison to glutaraldehyde. Overall, both PAS-EC and DAS-PO demonstrated promising biocidal performance, underscoring their potential as safer and more sustainable alternatives.

Overall, both PAS-EC and DAS-PO demonstrated promising biocidal performance, underscoring their potential as safer and more sustainable alternatives.

papers.title: Chemical Structure–Dynamics–Property Relationships in Glutaraldehyde-Crosslinked Poly(Vinyl Alcohol): Integrating FTIR, Dynamic Mechanical Analysis, and Time–Temperature Superposition
papers.abstract: Poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) is a polymer rich in hydroxyl groups, whose viscoelastic properties and other physical and chemical characteristics can be controlled using chemical crosslinking. In the present research, glutaraldehyde (GA) was used as a bifunctional crosslinker to explore the interrelationship between the chemical structure, acetal network formation, molecular motion, and mechanical properties of PVA. The samples of PVA with GA content from 5% to 40 wt% were synthesized and studied using Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), mechanical characterization, dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA), and time–temperature superposition (TTS). FTIR spectra showed a decrease in the absorbance of the hydroxyl group and changes in the C–O/C–O–C region, which proved the existence of acid-catalyzed acetalization between the PVA hydroxyl group and the GA aldehyde group and gradual acetal network formation. At the same time, DMA served as a complementary physicochemical technique to FTIR spectra: changes in storage modulus (E′), loss modulus (E″), tan δ, and glass transition behavior indicated restricted segmental motion and different relaxation dynamics. The above-mentioned changes on the molecular level manifested themselves in changes in the mechanical properties, where the tensile strength was found to have increased from 5.2 MPa in the neat PVA to 14.8 MPa in the case of GA content of 20 wt.% and the impact strength—up to 16.2 kJ m−2. An increase in GA content leads to an increase in network rigidity while reducing molecular mobility and energy dissipation, which indicates an overly constrained structure. Overall, 20 wt.% GA gave the best compromise between crosslinking, molecular constraint, mechanical reinforcement, and viscoelastic stabilization. In addition, an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) model was designed to predict the dynamic mechanical behavior of GA crosslinked PVA in terms of storage modulus (E′), loss modulus (E″) and damping factor (tan δ). The ANN model considered GA concentration, tensile behavior, flexural behavior, impact strength, hardness, and temperature as the eight inputs. A feedforward neural network with the architecture 8-10-3 was designed, which was trained using the Levenberg–Marquardt backpropagation algorithm. The correlations (R) obtained by the model were 0.9971, 0.9969, and 0.9940 for training, validation, and testing, respectively. A validation minimum mean squared error (MSE) of 2.8020 × 10−4 was obtained at epoch 34.
papers.summary: Poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) is a polymer rich in hydroxyl groups, whose viscoelastic properties and other physical and chemical characteristics can be controlled using chemical crosslinking. An increase in GA content leads to an increase in network rigidity while reducing molecular mobility and energy dissipation, which indicates an overly constrained structure. A feedforward neural network with the architecture 8-10-3 was designed, which was trained using the Levenberg–Marquardt backpropagation algorithm.

papers.title: Cyclodextrin encapsulation enhances the stability, anticancer, antimicrobial, and antibiofilm activities of chios mastic gum essential oil
papers.abstract: Abstract In this study, mastic gum essential oil ( Pistacia lentiscus var. Chia; PL) was encapsulated within 2-hydroxypropyl-β-cyclodextrin (CD). This formulation aimed to improve the limited compatibility, volatility, and stability of PL, while enhancing its biological performance. PL-CD nanoparticles were characterized using FTIR, ¹H NMR, 2D NOESY, thermal analysis, DLS, SEM, and TEM. These analyses confirmed successful encapsulation, with a high entrapment efficiency of 91.04 ± 0.76%. TEM analysis showed PL-CD nanoparticles ranging in size from 28.18 to 135.26 nm. In contrast, DLS showed a larger hydrodynamic diameter. Encapsulation also improved the thermal stability of PL and produced favorable degradation behavior. Short-term storage and photostability assessment showed no detectable changes in weight, color, clarity, or odor for up to 105 h under light or dark ambient conditions. Biological evaluation of PL-CD showed enhanced antimicrobial and antibiofilm activity. PL-CD exhibited MIC values of 2.5–5 mg/mL, representing up to an eight-fold improvement compared with free PL. It also inhibited biofilm formation by more than 92% across the tested bacterial strains. Biocompatibility studies using HSF cells showed that PL-CD showed a safe profile under the tested conditions. Anticancer evaluation using MCF-7 and MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells showed concentration- and time-dependent reductions in MTT-derived metabolic activity after PL-CD treatment. Annexin V/PI flow cytometry further showed increased apoptotic cell populations following PL-CD exposure. These findings indicate that the observed cytotoxic response was associated with apoptosis. The developed PL-CD nanostructures represent a promising platform for further investigation in antimicrobial, antibiofilm, and anticancer applications.
papers.summary: This formulation aimed to improve the limited compatibility, volatility, and stability of PL, while enhancing its biological performance. Anticancer evaluation using MCF-7 and MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells showed concentration- and time-dependent reductions in MTT-derived metabolic activity after PL-CD treatment. The developed PL-CD nanostructures represent a promising platform for further investigation in antimicrobial, antibiofilm, and anticancer applications.

papers.title: Association between clinical pharmacist intervention intensity and clinical outcomes in diabetic kidney disease: a real-world analysis utilizing K-means clustering
papers.abstract: Background Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is a key driver of end-stage renal disease, requiring intensive multidisciplinary care with clinical pharmacists as critical members. Though existing studies confirm pharmacist intervention efficacy, the relationship between intervention intensity and DKD patient outcomes remains poorly defined. Based on prior work, intervention intensity was quantified via two variable categories: (1) Clinical measures: therapeutic regimen optimization, Guideline-Directed Medical Therapy (GDMT) utilization and managing drug-drug interactions/adverse reactions; (2) Management metrics: medication education, physician acceptance of recommendation, medication rationality assessment and patient adherence evaluation. This study aimed to assess the association between clinical pharmacist intervention intensity and DKD patients’ key outcomes and prognosis via data-driven clustering. Methods Retrospective real-world cohort study at a Chinese Grade A tertiary hospital (May 2021–August 2025) assessed 148 inpatients, enrolling 97 patients were stratified via K-means clustering with uniform pharmacist intervention parameters; principal component analysis reduced dimensionality. Primary outcomes: eGFR. Secondary outcomes: UACR, HbA1c, readmission, dialysis initiation, MACE (heart failure, myocardial infarction, stroke, and cardiovascular death.). Results Of 97 inpatients, 58 had low-intensity and 39 had high-intensity clinical pharmacist intervention. Baseline characteristics were similar except for age. Changes from baseline to the 6-month follow-up, patients in the high-intensity group demonstrated significantly greater improvements in eGFR (median: 9.23 vs. −9.92 mL/min/1.73 m 2 , P < 0.05) and more pronounced reductions in UACR (median: −2038.21 vs . −901.92 mg/g, P < 0.05) and HbA1c (median: −1.17 vs. −0.24%, P < 0.05) compared with those in the low-intensity control group. In prognostic analysis, an eGFR decline (threshold: −10 mL/min/1.73 m 2 ) in the low-intensity group increased the incidence of MACE ( P = 0.020). Post hoc analyses identified medium-to-high adherence (OR = 4.058, 95% CI:1.167–14.111, P = 0.028) and ≥7 medication education sessions (OR = 6.250, 95% CI:1.996–17.574, P = 0.002) as independent predictors of eGFR improvement in DKD patients. Moreover, higher GDMT utilization/adherence correlated with greater eGFR improvement. Conclusion This study demonstrates that, compared with low-intensity intervention, high-intensity clinical pharmacist intervention is associated with better renal function and glycemic control, and may offer potential implications for delivering clinical value to high-risk patients. Limitations include the study’s limited follow-up duration and selection bias; future research will require larger samples and extended follow-up to confirm these findings.

papers.title: University Students’ Experiences and Participation in Using Online Teaching and Learning at a Zimbabwean State University
papers.journal: Journal of Research Innovation and Implications in Education
papers.abstract: The fact that even well before the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic online teaching and learning approaches to modern students` education and training programs were already being used in some countries cannot be denied.This mixed methods research study sought to explore university students' experiences and participation in online teaching and learning after the Covid-19 pandemic.Thirty (n=30) conveniently sampled first year students who were using online teaching and learning completed a structured questionnaire to indicate the approximate amount of time they spent on the internet each week, while10 of them participated in semi-structured interviews.Students expressed an admixture of experiences with using online teaching and learning pedagogies ranging from independent learning, cost-cutting advantages, improved use of ICT for teaching and learning to estrangement from using the unfamiliar technology, lack of resources, poor internet connectivity and difficulties in learning concepts in some subjects.Findings of this study also revealed a situation in which students indicated negligible participation in the use of internet facilities; the bedrock of online pedagogies.Recommendations were made for universities to: 1. rethink strategies and policies for enhancing more sustainable adoption and institutionalisation of the online teaching and learning pedagogies.2. Establish strategies for subsidizing students' connectivity costs 3. Establish strategies for improvement of online infrastructural facilities and 4. Facilitate the availability of online hardware devices to students, such as smartphones.

papers.title: Experimental assessment of active and passive cooling configurations for photovoltaic modules under outdoor conditions
papers.abstract: This study experimentally evaluated front-surface water-film cooling and rear-mounted aluminum heat sinks for polycrystalline photovoltaic modules under outdoor conditions. Two 100-Wp modules of the same model were monitored from November 2025 to March 2026, with temperature, voltage, and current recorded at 1-min intervals. During the representative active test, the maximum backsheet temperature was 42.0 °C for the water-film configuration and 50.5 °C for the reference module, a difference of 8.5 °C. Across nine monitoring days, differences between their daily maximum temperatures ranged from 8.5 °C to 18.96 °C. After subtracting 22.89 Wh of pump consumption, excluding power-supply losses and control-system consumption, the active configuration delivered 475.05 Wh of net electrical energy, compared with 438.06 Wh for the reference, corresponding to a difference of 8.44%. During the representative passive test, the heat-sink configuration showed a maximum backsheet temperature 1.50 °C below the reference and a daily electrical-energy difference of 1.70%, smaller than its reported expanded uncertainty. The investigated module operated with maximum power point tracking, while the reference used a fixed resistive load. Consequently, the electrical differences reflect both cooling and electrical load management and cannot be attributed exclusively to cooling. The water-film configuration showed a larger temperature reduction under its test conditions, but the active and passive results were obtained on different days and do not establish a comparison under matched environmental conditions.
papers.summary: This study experimentally evaluated front-surface water-film cooling and rear-mounted aluminum heat sinks for polycrystalline photovoltaic modules under outdoor conditions. The investigated module operated with maximum power point tracking, while the reference used a fixed resistive load. The water-film configuration showed a larger temperature reduction under its test conditions, but the active and passive results were obtained on different days and do not establish a comparison under matched environmental conditions.

papers.title: Rhodococcus–norovirus interactions: a hypothesis of affinity-driven viral release from bacterial exopolysaccharides
papers.abstract: Recent findings have revealed that Rhodococcus species bind human norovirus (NoV) particles in clinical stool samples collected from pediatric gastroenteritis cases. This recurring association across independent samples suggests a potentially relevant biological interaction. The binding appears to be mediated by exopolysaccharides (EPSs), which are typically rich in fucose, galactose, and glucuronic acid residues and may structurally mimic histo-blood group antigens (HBGAs), the known cellular receptors for NoV. We propose that these EPSs may function as transient viral carriers capable of stabilizing virions while maintaining reversible interactions with the viral capsid. We further hypothesize an affinity-driven release mechanism, whereby authentic HBGAs on host epithelial cells, possessing higher binding affinity, displace virions from bacterial EPSs, thereby facilitating timely infection. This interaction may serve a dual function: Environmental stabilization of the virus and its controlled release upon encountering host cells. If validated, this model would support the concept that bacterial glycans act as dynamic, reversible docking platforms that influence NoV ecology, transmission, and infectivity.

papers.title: Vitrimerization Routes for Waste PET Upcycling
papers.abstract: The accumulation of massive post-consumer poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) waste poses severe ecological hazards. Conventional mechanical recycling induces irreversible chain scission and severe property depreciation, while chemical depolymerization consumes excessive energy and toxic solvents, creating a performance-cost downcycling bottleneck limiting high-value PET reuse. This comprehensive critical review highlights vitrimer chemistry based on associative dynamic exchange as a transformative upcycling solution. The field is organized around two fabrication routes—depolymerization-reconstruction and in-situ/direct network construction while preserving the PET backbone—together with a cross-cutting transesterification catalytic dimension covering externally catalyzed, self-catalytic, and metal-free, no-added-catalyst (including residual-catalyst-assisted), and fully catalyst-free designs. Solvolysis-derived oligomers afford vitrimers with tunable glass transition temperature (Tg) (38~240 °C) and tensile strength up to 117 MPa; solvent-free extrusion fits continuous industrial lines, and metal-free designs may reduce heavy-metal contamination. Several optimized systems retain over 80% mechanical performance after cyclic reprocessing, although significant variations exist; for example, the bis(2-hydroxyethyl) terephthalate (BHET)/pyromellitic dianhydride (PMDA)/trimethylolpropane (TMP) vitrimer decreases from approximately 30 MPa to 16 MPa after two compression-molding cycles. These technologies show potential for closed-loop recycling and reprocessability, may reduce virgin resin demand, and may reduce carbon footprints, pending full life-cycle assessment. Major industrial barriers include insufficient creep resistance, incomplete monomer recovery, and non-uniform testing standards. This work delivers integrated theoretical and engineering guidance for scalable PET vitrimer circular-material development.
papers.summary: The accumulation of massive post-consumer poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) waste poses severe ecological hazards. These technologies show potential for closed-loop recycling and reprocessability, may reduce virgin resin demand, and may reduce carbon footprints, pending full life-cycle assessment. This work delivers integrated theoretical and engineering guidance for scalable PET vitrimer circular-material development.

papers.title: Evolution of Near-Surface Structure, Oxidation State, and Electrochemistry of Li + /H + -Exchanged and Heat-Treated Li- and Mn-Rich NCM
papers.abstract: Anionic redox in Li- and Mn-rich (LMR) NCMs (Li 1+ δ [TM] 1− δ O 2 , 0.1 ⩽ δ ⩽ 0.2) enables high reversible specific capacities (≈250 mAh g −1 ), but voltage and capacity fading compromise cycle life. Acid washing can mitigate these effects, through partial Li + /H + exchange, subsequently released during heat treatment, leading to an O-depleted near-surface structure. Here, Li 1.14 [Ni 0.26 Co 0.14 Mn 0.60 ] 0.86 O 2 was washed in a phosphate buffer to avoid transition-metal (TM) dissolution and heat-treated at 120–650 °C. Thermogravimetric analysis coupled with mass spectrometry allows to quantify the H + content. Model materials (≈30 at% H + ) were used to track the near-surface structure and TM oxidation states. At 120 °C, X-ray diffraction detects a protonated phase, while X-ray absorption near edge structure reveals a partial shift to spinel coordination (near-surface ½ MO 2 + ½ M 3 O 4 ) at 180–240 °C. At 300 °C, O 2 is released, and further spinel M 3 O 4 is formed, converting to rock-salt MO from 450 °C. Electrochemical tests on 8.7 at% Li + /H + -exchanged samples after 120 °C show a first-charge overpotential due to H + . Only the 450 °C sample exhibits significantly higher impedance across the entire potential range. Despite lower initial capacities, samples heated to 120 °C and 450 °C exhibit superior long-term full-cell C/2 capacity.
