papers.title: Surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy on the membranes for antimicrobial resistance testing
papers.abstract: Introduction Antimicrobial resistance is a major global health threat, causing millions of deaths every year. Traditional antibiotic susceptibility tests rely on the detection of bacterial growth in the presence of antimicrobial agents. These tests take over 1-2 days to complete, so empirical therapy schemes often begin before the test results are available. Rapid tests for antimicrobial resistance are needed to optimize treatment for bacterial infections. A combination of the MTT test and Raman spectroscopy can provide a 1.5-h test for antimicrobial susceptibility, requiring 10 6 –10 8 CFU/mL of bacteria. Here the novel rapid antibiotic susceptibility test for trace amounts of bacteria is described. Methods Surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) has been suggested to improve the sensitivity of the test. SERS spectra of MTT-treated bacteria can be acquired using membranes coated with silver nanoparticles. These membranes simultaneously concentrate the sample on the surface and generate SERS spectra under 532-nm or 638-nm laser irradiation. Results Both the spectra of individual bacteria and the large-area measurements provided information for antimicrobial resistance testing. The bacterial titer can be decreased down to 500 CFU/mL in the test. The overall analysis time was 1.5 h. Discussion This rapid sensitive test highly promising for point-of-care applications avoiding durable bacterial culturing.

papers.title: Two-layer micromagnetic modeling of ferrimagnets: Temperature-driven compensation and skyrmion dynamics
papers.abstract: Ferrimagnets host unique compensation phenomena that enable ultrafast dynamics and efficient current-driven manipulation, but their micromagnetic modeling remains challenging due to the need to resolve coupled sublattices. Here, we introduce an equivalent two-layer model implemented in the widely used MuMax3 framework that qualitatively reproduces the temperature-dependent magnetic and angular momentum compensation states of ferrimagnetic alloys, including thermally induced, sperimagnetic-like fanning of sublattice moments. By assigning different magnetic parameters and gyromagnetic ratios to the two layers, we demonstrate that the magnetic and angular momentum compensation temperatures can be separated. As a key application, we simulate current-induced skyrmion motion and find that, at the angular momentum compensation point, the skyrmion Hall effect vanishes while the longitudinal velocity reaches a maximum. Modeling distinct gyromagnetic ratios in the two layers requires a modified version of MuMax3 with region-dependent g-factors. Our approach provides an efficient framework for qualitative investigations of a broad range of ferrimagnetic phenomena, including composition-dependent compensation, domain-wall dynamics, and effects arising from nonuniform current or temperature distributions.

papers.title: Scattering crossover in the d -wave-like superconductor (TMTSF) 2 ClO 4 studied by specific heat measurements
papers.abstract: In the quasi-one-dimensional organic unconventional superconductor (TMTSF)2ClO4, the randomness of the non-centrosymmetric ClO4 anions can be experimentally controlled by adjusting the cooling rate through the anion-ordering temperature. This feature provides a unique opportunity to study disorder effects on unconventional superconductivity in great detail. We here report on measurements of the electronic specific heat of this system, performed under various cooling rates. The evolution of the residual density of states indicates that the ClO4 randomness works as Born-limit pair breakers, which, to our knowledge, has never been clearly identified in any unconventional superconductors. Furthermore, detailed analyses suggest a peculiar crossover from strong unitarity scattering due to molecular defects toward the Born-limit weak scattering due to borders of ordered regions. This work supports the nodal d-wave-like nature of pairing in (TMTSF)2ClO4 and intends to provide an experimental basis for further developments of pair-breaking theories of unconventional superconductors where multiple electron scattering mechanisms coexist.

papers.title: Multi-objective optimization of container loading: balancing space utilization, unloading obstacles, and cargo stability
papers.abstract: Abstract The Container Loading Problem (CLP) concerns the arrangement of rectangular boxes inside a container while satisfying practical requirements such as dimensional feasibility, weight capacity, stackability, delivery order, and cargo stability. In multi-drop delivery settings, additional operational challenges arise, including reducing unloading obstacles (ULOs) and maintaining load balance. This paper formulates a tri-objective CLP that simultaneously (i) maximizes space utilization, (ii) minimizes ULOs, and (iii) minimizes the loaded cargo’s center-of-gravity (CG) deviation from the container’s geometric center across all three spatial axes. The formulation integrates these operational and stability considerations within a unified mathematical framework. To address the resulting problem, a customized Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) is combined with an extreme-point placement decoder based on the deepest-bottom-left-fill strategy and balance-aware placement considerations. The framework also incorporates geometric feasibility, orientation restrictions, vertical support, stackability, payload limits, and delivery priorities. Computational experiments on modified Bischoff and Ratcliff benchmark instances show how volume utilization, unloading accessibility, and CG balance interact under different levels of instance heterogeneity and cargo-weight distributions. The resulting nondominated solution sets expose alternative compromises among packing efficiency, delivery accessibility, and load balance, providing a multi-objective evaluation framework for operational container loading.

papers.title: Highly conductive halide Na-ion conductor enabled by cost-effective aliovalent carbonate polyanion substitution for all-solid-state sodium batteries
papers.abstract: Halide-based Na-ion conductors have attracted intense attention due to their favorable (electro)chemical compatibility with oxide positive electrodes. Among these, zirconium (Zr)-based halide solid electrolytes (SEs) offer a cost advantage over halide SEs based on rare metals, but the relatively low ionic conductivity has limited their application in all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs). Here, we report employing soda ash (Na2CO3) as a low-cost precursor to introduce an aliovalent carbonate polyanion and produce a family of Na-Zr-Cl-CO3 conductors with nominal compositions of (2-x)NaCl-xNa2CO3-ZrCl4. This substitution increases structural disorder and amorphization, creating structural environments that facilitate Na+ transport. At the optimal composition, its ionic conductivity reaches 1.02 mS cm−1 at 25 °C. The optimized Na-Zr-Cl-CO3 SE also exhibits stable electrochemical behavior and favorable mechanical properties. When paired with NaCrO2 positive electrode, the assembled ASSBs deliver an initial discharge capacity of 117 mAh g−1 at 0.1 C and demonstrate a long-term cycling stability at 0.3 C for 850 cycles. This work highlights carbonate polyanion substitution as a practical strategy for improving low-cost Zr-based halide SEs, offering a promising route toward ASSBs with high performance. Zr-based halide solid electrolytes are promising for their lower cost but suffer from limited ionic conductivity. Here, authors introduce carbonate polyanion using cost-competitive soda ash to enhance structural disorder and Na+ transport, achieving 1.02 mS cm−1 ionic conductivity and stable all-solid-state battery cycling for 850 cycles.

papers.title: Optimal sizing and material choice for additively manufactured compact plate heat exchangers
papers.abstract: Axial wall conduction can limit the compactness of counterflow heat exchangers, making material selection dependent on both thermal conductivity and achievable wall thickness. This study investigates how additive manufacturing (AM) limits influence the optimal sizing and thermal power density of compact parallel-plate heat exchangers. A nondimensional analytical model accounting for lateral and axial wall conduction is coupled with geometric optimization for six materials: plastic, austenitic steel, aluminum oxide, aluminum nitride, aluminum and copper. Channel length and spacing are optimized at prescribed pressure drop and effectiveness, considering uniform or material-specific wall thicknesses and a minimum-spacing constraint. The effects of target effectiveness and improvements in thin-wall manufacturing are also examined. With a common wall thickness and minimum spacing, plastic and austenitic steel achieve similar calculated power densities. Under the selected material-specific thickness limits and minimum-spacing constraint, plastic reaches approximately 7.5 times the power density of copper. Its optimized design also achieves approximately 52% higher power density than the corresponding fixed-spacing reference with the same wall thickness. High-conductivity materials require larger channel dimensions to limit axial conduction losses, particularly at high effectiveness. Reducing wall thickness provides the greatest improvement for copper over the investigated thickness ranges, while thinner austenitic steel becomes competitive with plastic at lower effectiveness targets. These findings demonstrate the importance of jointly selecting material, wall thickness and channel geometry, and identify how improvements in AM thin-wall capability can influence achievable heat exchanger compactness.

These findings demonstrate the importance of jointly selecting material, wall thickness and channel geometry, and identify how improvements in AM thin-wall capability can influence achievable heat exchanger compactness.

papers.title: An adjustable-rate user-printable rain gauge calibrator
papers.journal: Geoscientific instrumentation, methods and data systems
papers.abstract: Accurate precipitation measurement is essential. However, calibration of field-deployed rain gauges remains a challenge. Many methods require laboratory conditions, costly commercial equipment, or instruments designed for specific rain gauges, which cannot accommodate smaller-diameter gauges. We introduce the Adjustable-Rate 3D Printed Rain Gauge Calibrator (AR3D) , a low-cost, open-source device designed for in situ calibration of rain gauges. The AR3D introduces three innovations: (1) an adjustable screw valve, enabling flow rate tuning from 0.15–16 mL min −1 (equivalent rainfall rates 1.3–141.2 mm h −1 , for a 9.3 cm diameter gauge), accommodating the lower flow rates needed for smaller rain gauges and allowing for validation across a wide range of rainfall rates; (2) a compact and durable design developed with low-volume reservoirs and elimination of degradable parts; and (3) an integrated pyranometer cover to generate automatic calibration event signals. We evaluated the AR3D using gravimetric tests, constant-rate stability tests, device-to-device equivalence tests, and field comparisons. Laboratory gravimetric tests of the AR3D demonstrate its ability to deliver volumes of water accurately with an average error of 0.11 % (comparable to ISO Class B tolerances for plastic volumetric flasks) at flow rates within ±5 % equivalence across independent devices, with a coefficient of variation (CV) below 5 %. The AR3D has been successfully deployed to weather stations in Kenya and the United States. Field validation of the AR3D with a single setting resulted in a flow rate CV of 8.7 %. The AR3D enabled the identification of properly functioning rain gauges, as well as an under-reporting station. The total cost of material and labor to build an AR3D is approximately USD 12.

papers.title: Supercritical snapping and controlled launching via dual-latch gels
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
papers.abstract: Natural organisms have evolved integrated Latch-Mediated Spring Actuation systems (LaMSA) that consist of multiple latches and springs to enhance power output and adapt to diverse environmental conditions. Similar designs are appealing yet largely unexplored in engineered materials due to the complexity of integrating multiple components into a single material platform. Here, we report a dual-latch magneto-elastic shell device capable of selectively activating the latches to regulate snapping pathways and energy output based on specific actuation requirements. Differential deswelling across the thickness acts as the “motor” to load the elastic energy into the shell, which is then released via the snap-through instability once the loading reaches the critical threshold, constituting an intrinsic mechanical latch. Activation of the external magnetic latch delays snapping onset beyond the threshold of the intrinsic latch, leading to a power-amplified supercritical snap-through instability as well as a bifurcation instability. The combined function of both latches allows for flexible control over energy storage and release. Additionally, this integrated LaMSA system possesses an untethered anchoring mechanism, enabling the device to launch in arbitrary directions from the substrate, driven by the energy released during snapping. We envision that the design principles of dual-latch LaMSA systems will create opportunities for power-dense actuation in engineered materials and robotic devices.

papers.title: Sustainability in Jordan’s municipal solid waste management system: reduction of methane emissions and benefits to public health
papers.journal: Journal of Material Cycles and Waste Management
papers.abstract: Abstract Municipal solid waste management (MSWM) in Jordan faces significant challenges. Jordan's primary waste management strategy relies heavily on final disposal, with up to 80% of all generated solid waste ultimately being landfilled. These unsustainable practices lead to environmental degradation and public health risks. Increased methane emissions have harmed air quality: methane can lead to the formation of ground-level ozone, which in turn causes respiratory problems including asthma and pneumonia. The main objective of this study is to evaluate the impact of improved solid waste management strategies on methane emissions in the period from 2020 to 2050. The Low Emissions Analysis Platform (LEAP) is used for the analysis, and current methane emissions from municipal solid waste are estimated using data obtained from the Ministry of Local Administration, the Greater Amman Municipality, the Department of Statistics, and the World Health Organization. These datasets, which include information on waste quantities and landfill boundaries, are integrated into the LEAP software to facilitate estimation of methane emissions. Our analysis finds that, without intervention, methane emissions will rise from 4.3 million metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent in 2020 to 7.8 million tons by 2050 due to increasing population and economic expansion. In addition to the serious environmental consequences, we estimate public health damages of $41 billion per year by 2050, linked to excess mortality. In the short-term, methane emissions can be mitigated by following a “circular economy” strategy of reuse and recycling. This could reduce methane emissions by 12% by 2030. Medium-term strategies, including the establishment of sanitary landfills and recycling facilities, combined with the short-term projects can reduce methane emissions 34% below baseline by 2040. Adding long-term strategies, including composting and additional reuse, leads to reductions of 55% by 2050. More dramatic individual changes to the system also have large effects: shifting to incineration instead of landfills reduces methane emissions by 52%. Advanced recycling facilities can reduce emissions by 35%. These results highlight the impact of improved integrated waste management approaches on reducing emissions and thus enhancing public health and global climate goals. The paper underscores the importance of technical advancement in solid waste management in Jordan. We show that large environmental and economic gains are possible with aggressive governmental actions and collaboration among stakeholders.

These results highlight the impact of improved integrated waste management approaches on reducing emissions and thus enhancing public health and global climate goals. We show that large environmental and economic gains are possible with aggressive governmental actions and collaboration among stakeholders.

papers.title: Development of commingled hoop-wound composites-reinforced O-rings (CRO) for aeronautical application
papers.abstract: Abstract Traditional elastomeric O-rings, although widely employed in aerospace sealing applications, are often limited by its inadequate chemical resistance, thermal stability, mechanical resistance and durability under extreme operating conditions. This article proposes the development of high-performance composites for O-ring reinforcement using carbon fiber/polyether ether ketone and glass fiber/polyamide commingled technologies engineered to address current limitations by integrating elastomeric materials with continuous reinforcements tailored for the demanding environments of aerospace systems. A novel pre-compaction device (machine head) for commingled tows was designed and developed for using at filament winding technique, which was used to manufacture the reinforcement inner section of the O-rings. Final compaction level of commingled composites was carried out using compression molding to meet aeronautical requirements. The materials were characterized by SEM and thermal analysis as DSC. O-ring reinforcements made from 3D-printed carbon fiber/Onyx and glass fiber/Onyx by Markforged® printer were also manufactured and tested, indicating the improvement of O-rings performance when used commingled technology. Using 3D-printing resources, a hermetic mold was created to combine the composites reinforcement with the silicon-based elastomeric covering. Finally, composites reinforced O-rings were submitted to tensile testing, based on ASTM D2290 procedures, and a comparison of the resulting mechanical properties revealed superior performance of the commingled reinforcements.

papers.title: Feeding a microencapsulated blend of essential oils and capsaicin affects growth performance, carcass traits, and beef quality of feedlot-finished Nellore bulls
papers.abstract: Abstract This study was conducted to evaluate the effects of a microencapsulated blend of essential oils and capsaicin (BEO) on the performance, carcass traits, and meat quality of feedlot-finished cattle. Forty-seven Nellore bulls (360 ± 15 kg; ~19 months old) were assigned to two treatments: a control diet without EO ( n = 24) or a diet supplemented with 150 mg/kg DM of BEO ( n = 23). All diets contained sodium monensin. Animal performance was assessed during the 94-day finishing period, and carcass and meat quality traits were evaluated after slaughter. Cattle fed BEO tended to have greater average daily gain (+ 130 g/day; P = 0.077), resulting in increased final body weight (+ 9.2 kg; P = 0.014) and carcass weight (+ 5.0 kg; P = 0.014). Subcutaneous fat thickness was also increased (+ 1.0 mm; P = 0.036), whereas dry matter intake, feed efficiency, dressing percentage, and loin muscle area were not affected. Meat from BEO-fed bulls had lower cooking loss (− 1.6% points; P = 0.005) and improved tenderness (− 3.2 N in shear force; P = 0.050), whereas pH, sarcomere length, and lipid content were unchanged. During retail display, BEO feeding was associated with lower meat lightness (L*) and yellowness (b*). No clear overall effect of BEO feeding was supported for lipid oxidation or any of the microbial groups evaluated, whereas microbial counts increased progressively during postmortem storage. In conclusion, dietary supplementation with a microencapsulated BEO combined with monensin, improved selected performance, carcass, and meat quality traits but did not provide clear evidence of improved microbial stability during retail display.

papers.title: Mapping the impact of imide-type anions on morphology and ion transport properties in PEO-based polymer electrolytes for potassium batteries
papers.abstract: The transition from liquid electrolytes to solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs) is a promising approach to improve the safety and stability of potassium metal batteries (PMBs). While Poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO) is widely used in SPEs, the effect of potassium salts on structure and performance of SPEs in PMBs have not been systematically studied. In this work, three salts, namely potassium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (KFSI), potassium bis(nonafluorobutanesulfonyl)imide (KNFBSI), and potassium hexafluoropropane-1,3-disulfonimide (KHFPSI), were studied over a wide compositional range. Thermal and structural characterization using DSC and XRD reveals that all systems exhibit a decrease in crystallinity with increasing salt content, while KHFPSI enables nearly complete amorphization of PEO at high salt loadings. Ionic conductivities on the order of 10 −3 S cm −1 were achieved at elevated temperatures (60-70 °C) for all systems, yet significant differences were observed at lower temperatures. The SPEs containing KNFBSI exhibit strongly suppressed conductivity, which is attributed to the formation of additional crystalline phases. 19 F NMR measurements confirm the presence of immobile ionic species in KNFBSI-containing systems, which are attributed to these secondary crystalline phases and lead to reduced ion transport. In contrast, KFSI-based SPEs exhibit the highest ionic conductivity due to the small size and high mobility of the anion.

papers.title: Liquid crystal elastomers by photopolymerization: from chemistry and alignment strategies to 4D printing
papers.abstract: Liquid crystal elastomers (LCEs) are materials that combine the anisotropy of liquid crystal molecules with the elasticity of lightly crosslinked polymer networks, making them promising for soft actuators. Photopolymerization has emerged as a key route for the design and implementation of LCEs, thanks to its broad chemical versatility and its compatibility with additive manufacturing, a field that had developed rapidly in recent years. However, this approach has not yet been comprehensively addressed, despite its central role in enabling LCE-based actuators and 4D-printed devices. This review aims to provide a comparative framework showing how chemical design governs material properties and defines compatible alignment strategies. Furthermore, it examines how the coupling between chemical structure and alignment can be integrated within additive manufacturing processes. By linking photopolymerization mechanisms, alignment strategies, and 4D printing processes, this review establishes guidelines for selecting suitable light-based chemistries, and for designing LCE networks with tailored properties.

papers.title: Starting material syntheses for non-aqueous molecular uranium chemistry
papers.abstract: Starting materials for non-aqueous uranium chemistry usually must be synthesised in-house, as they are rarely available commercially. Various routes to uranium precursors in oxidation states +III to +VI have been reported and developed further according to the availability of uranium compounds. This tutorial review discusses wet-chemical and selected solid-state routes to anhydrous uranium halide, amide and borohydride starting materials in oxidation states +III to +VI suitable for research laboratories. Oxidative, reductive, as well as halide interconversion routes are discussed to give a comprehensive overview on synthetically established routes and promising directions for future development.

papers.title: Development and Optimization of an HPMC/TPGS-Based Apixaban Amorphous Solid Dispersion for Enhanced Supersaturation and Oral Absorption
papers.abstract: An apixaban (APX) amorphous solid dispersion (ASD) containing hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HPMC) and D-α-tocopheryl polyethylene glycol 1000 succinate (TPGS) was prepared by spray drying to improve solubility and oral exposure. Screening identified HPMC for supersaturation maintenance and TPGS for apparent solubilization. A central composite design optimized their ratios using five responses: supersaturation solubility, 30-min kinetic solubility, kinetic solubility area under the curve (AUC), particle size, and polydispersity index (PDI). The optimized APX/HPMC/TPGS ratio was 1:3.93:0.85 (w/w/w), with a composite desirability of 0.8491 (on a scale from 0 to 1). Compared with crystalline APX, the optimized ASD increased supersaturation solubility, 30-min kinetic solubility, and kinetic solubility AUC 4.04-, 5.47-, and 8.10-fold, respectively. The dispersed formulation exhibited a particle size of 203.4 ± 17.3 nm and PDI of 0.246 ± 0.018. PXRD and DSC supported predominantly amorphous APX, while electron microscopy and DLS supported nanosized colloidal particle formation. The optimized ASD also maintained higher kinetic solubility in fasted-state simulated intestinal fluid than crystalline and amorphous APX. In rats, Cmax, AUC0–24, and AUC0–inf increased by 2.46-, 3.04-, and 2.80-fold, respectively, versus crystalline APX.

In rats, Cmax, AUC0–24, and AUC0–inf increased by 2.46-, 3.04-, and 2.80-fold, respectively, versus crystalline APX.

papers.title: The nonlinear mechanics of single electrospun polyurethane fibers under wet and dry conditions
papers.abstract: Polyurethanes (PU) are widely used polymers with numerous applications. These include electrospun biomaterials that are frequently exposed to aqueous environments. While the mechanical behavior of electrospun fiber networks has been extensively studied, the mechanics of single electrospun PU fibers and the influence of hydration on their behavior remain poorly understood. Thus, our goal is to characterize the mechanical response of single electrospun PU fibers under different hydration states and incorporate these findings into a constitutive framework suitable for predictive modeling. To this end, single fibers were tested under three conditions: dry, submerged in water, and soaked for four days. Across all hydration states, PU fibers exhibited hysteresis, strain stiffening, and damage. Notably, soaked fibers showed evidence of water-induced plasticization, whereas dry and submerged fibers displayed nearly identical mechanical responses. Additionally, the experimental data were fit with a quasilinear visco-hyperelastic damage model that accurately captured the mechanical behavior across all hydration states. Our combined experimental and modeling work provides new insight into the fiber-level mechanics of electrospun PU materials and enables multiscale modeling of electrospun PU fiber networks.
papers.summary: Polyurethanes (PU) are widely used polymers with numerous applications. Notably, soaked fibers showed evidence of water-induced plasticization, whereas dry and submerged fibers displayed nearly identical mechanical responses. Our combined experimental and modeling work provides new insight into the fiber-level mechanics of electrospun PU materials and enables multiscale modeling of electrospun PU fiber networks.

papers.title: Deubiquitinase USP14 restrains autophagy via LARS/mTORC1 axis to accelerate apoptosis in intervertebral disc degeneration
papers.abstract: Abstract Nutrient deficiency is a key contributor to the pathogenesis of intervertebral disc degeneration (IDD), exacerbating nucleus pulposus (NP) cell apoptosis and extracellular matrix (ECM) degradation. Here, we identified ubiquitin-specific protease 14 (USP14) as a critical stress-responsive regulator that is amplified in human and rat degenerative NP tissues. USP14 upregulation exacerbates nutrient deprivation–induced apoptosis and ECM degradation by inhibiting protective autophagy. Mechanistically, USP14 directly interacts with leucyl-tRNA synthetase (LARS) via its C-terminal catalytic domain, catalyzing the removal of K48-linked polyubiquitin chains to prevent proteasomal degradation of LARS. LARS stabilization hyperactivates the mTORC1 pathway, leading to autophagy suppression. The essential role of autophagy inhibition in USP14-mediated pathology was confirmed when pharmacological (chloroquine) or genetic (ATG5 siRNA) blockade of autophagy abolished the protective effects of USP14 knockdown. Both genetic targeting (siRNA, catalytic mutant C114A) and pharmacological inhibition (IU-1) of USP14 suppressed LARS/mTORC1 overactivation, restored autophagic flux, and mitigated NP cell damage, whereas LARS silencing or mTORC1 inhibition (rapamycin) alleviated USP14-driven pathological effects. Notably, intradiscal IU-1 delivery in a rat model of IDD attenuated disc degeneration, decreased apoptosis, and enhanced autophagic activity. Thus, we identified the USP14/LARS/mTORC1 axis as a ubiquitination-controlled mechanism regulating the autophagy-apoptosis equilibrium in nutrient-stressed NP cells, establishing USP14 as a promising therapeutic target for IDD.
papers.summary: Abstract Nutrient deficiency is a key contributor to the pathogenesis of intervertebral disc degeneration (IDD), exacerbating nucleus pulposus (NP) cell apoptosis and extracellular matrix (ECM) degradation. Notably, intradiscal IU-1 delivery in a rat model of IDD attenuated disc degeneration, decreased apoptosis, and enhanced autophagic activity. Thus, we identified the USP14/LARS/mTORC1 axis as a ubiquitination-controlled mechanism regulating the autophagy-apoptosis equilibrium in nutrient-stressed NP cells, establishing USP14 as a promising therapeutic target for IDD.

papers.title: Seafood intake and urinary total mercury in children: dose–response in three national samples and a paired urine–blood comparison in adolescents
papers.abstract: Urinary mercury is read as a marker of inorganic exposure, and urinary elimination of dietary methylmercury is treated as negligible. Whether urine carries a measurable seafood signal in children is unresolved, and national programs rarely draw blood from young children. The Korean National Environmental Health Survey (Cycle 5, 2021–2023) provided three probability samples: preschoolers ( n = 648), schoolchildren ( n = 780), and adolescents ( n = 901). We fitted survey-weighted log-linear models of habitual seafood intake with a Rao–Wu bootstrap. Each doubling of animal seafood intake was associated with 13.5%, 11.8%, and 15.0% higher creatinine-corrected total mercury in spot urine, pooling to 13.2% (95% CI 11.0, 15.5) with no detectable heterogeneity. Seaweed, the internal negative control, showed no positive association. In 812 adolescents, dietary slopes did not differ detectably between urine and blood (ratio 0.99; 0.72, 1.28), category profiles were similar, and adjustment for blood total mercury halved the urinary dietary slope. Agreement within individuals ( n = 872) stayed moderate (weighted Spearman ρ = 0.50, κ = 0.33). Spot urinary total mercury tracks seafood-related mercury exposure at population scale; without speciation, the signal cannot be assigned to methylmercury or inorganic mercury. It cannot stand in for blood mercury in one child.
papers.summary: Urinary mercury is read as a marker of inorganic exposure, and urinary elimination of dietary methylmercury is treated as negligible. Seaweed, the internal negative control, showed no positive association. It cannot stand in for blood mercury in one child.

papers.title: Lifelong vehicle re-identification via ResNet50 with depthwise spatial attention
papers.abstract: The core task of vehicle re-identification is to recognize vehicles with the same identity across different scenes. Existing methods, relying on fixed-dataset training, struggle to cope with continuously updating multi-domain vehicle data in real-world scenarios, and thus suffer significant performance degradation under data distribution shifts. While lifelong learning techniques can gradually accumulate multi-domain knowledge, they suffer from catastrophic forgetting of historical discriminative features and adapt inefficiently to new domains, particularly in preserving cross-domain spatial cues (e.g., component structure, contour details). To address this, this paper proposes a lifelong vehicle ReID model based on ResNet50, which embeds the depthwise spatial attention module. By leveraging depthwise separable convolution to dynamically focus on cross-domain invariant spatial regions such as the grille, headlights and vehicle contours, the model enhances local discriminative features to mitigate feature drift. The model couples two mechanisms: the depthwise spatial attention module preserves historical discriminative spatial features and curbs catastrophic forgetting, while the feature alignment loss maintains consistent multi-domain representations and balances old and new knowledge. Extensive experiments on VeRi-776, VRIC, and VehicleID show that, among the lifelong methods compared under a common protocol, the proposed method attains the highest accuracy—77.0% mAP and 78.7% R1 on average—while storing no historical images and requiring the lowest peak training memory of 7.2 GB.
papers.summary: The core task of vehicle re-identification is to recognize vehicles with the same identity across different scenes. Existing methods, relying on fixed-dataset training, struggle to cope with continuously updating multi-domain vehicle data in real-world scenarios, and thus suffer significant performance degradation under data distribution shifts. Extensive experiments on VeRi-776, VRIC, and VehicleID show that, among the lifelong methods compared under a common protocol, the proposed method attains the highest accuracy—77.0% mAP and 78.7% R1 on average—while storing no historical images and requiring the lowest peak training memory of 7.2 GB.

papers.title: Trauma-Informed Care for Perinatal Psychological Trauma: Application Progress and Public Health Strategies
papers.journal: Journal of Public Health and Preventive Medicine
papers.abstract: Perinatal psychological trauma has emerged as a critical public health concern with profound implications for maternal and child health as well as intergenerational trauma transmission. Trauma-Informed Care (TIC), operating as a universal prevention-oriented healthcare management framework, shows significant promise in restoring a sense of safety, mitigating perinatal post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), and advancing health equity. This narrative review synthesizes current research progress on the multidimensional characteristics and population-level burden of perinatal trauma, analyzes the core concepts and implementation frameworks of TIC, summarizes validated screening and assessment instruments, and thoroughly examines practical bottlenecks—including primary healthcare workforce shortages, socio-cultural stigma, and cross-sectoral referral fragmentation—along with corresponding coping strategies. Ultimately, this review aims to clarify the conceptual boundaries and theoretical foundations of TIC, providing an evidence-based framework to accelerate the translation of TIC principles from micro-level clinical operations into standardized, integrated public health systems.

papers.title: A supercapacitor-assisted cyclic battery recharging method for solar and wind power systems
papers.abstract: The efficient use of solar and wind electricity in stand-alone power systems for remote facilities is limited during periods of reduced generation, when the source voltage may fall below the activation threshold of the charge controller. Under such conditions, direct battery recharging becomes impossible despite the availability of residual energy from the renewable source. This paper investigates a cyclic battery recharging method based on preliminary energy accumulation in supercapacitor modules and their subsequent discharge into the battery. The proposed approach was evaluated using a MATLAB/Simulink simulation model and a physical experimental setup with 166 F and 500 F supercapacitor modules and lead-acid batteries. The results show that preliminary energy storage in supercapacitor modules followed by controlled discharge enables additional battery recharging when the source voltage is insufficient for direct charging through the controller. For the 166 F modules, the duration of the complete first cycle was approximately 8.3 min, while for the 500 F modules it was approximately 28.5 min. Repeated cycles started from the residual voltage of the supercapacitor modules, which reduced the duration of the subsequent charging stages. The deviation between the simulated and experimental voltage characteristics did not exceed 3.5% in the most important operating regions and remained below 7.4% in the other regions. The proposed method is based on voltage-threshold switching logic; in the physical setup, switching was performed manually, while automated implementation is considered as a direction for future research.
papers.summary: This paper investigates a cyclic battery recharging method based on preliminary energy accumulation in supercapacitor modules and their subsequent discharge into the battery. The proposed approach was evaluated using a MATLAB/Simulink simulation model and a physical experimental setup with 166 F and 500 F supercapacitor modules and lead-acid batteries. The results show that preliminary energy storage in supercapacitor modules followed by controlled discharge enables additional battery recharging when the source voltage is insufficient for direct charging through the controller.

papers.title: Digital enablement and employee performance in society 5.0: a dual-path model of motivation and exhaustion
papers.abstract: Introduction Society 5.0 integrates advanced digital technologies with human-centered work systems, yet its implications for sustainable employee performance remain underexplored. Drawing on Job Demands–Resources Theory and Self-Determination Theory, this study examines the relationship between Society 5.0 enablement intensity (S5EI) and sustainable human performance through autonomous motivation and emotional exhaustion, considering human-centric governance capability as a moderator. Methods The study employed partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) to analyse data collected from 519 employees working in digitally intensive sectors in India. Results The findings indicate that S5EI is positively associated with sustainable human performance, primarily through autonomous motivation. Emotional exhaustion partially offsets this positive effect through competitive mediation. Human-centric governance capability strengthens the relationship between autonomous motivation and sustainable human performance but does not significantly buffer the negative effect of emotional exhaustion. Discussion The findings conceptualize digital enablement as a dual-valence work condition that simultaneously strengthens autonomy-based motivation and increases digital demands, integrating Job Demands–Resources Theory and Self-Determination Theory. The study highlights the importance of participatory digital governance, workload management, and employee recovery measures for supporting sustainable human performance.
papers.summary: Introduction Society 5.0 integrates advanced digital technologies with human-centered work systems, yet its implications for sustainable employee performance remain underexplored. Results The findings indicate that S5EI is positively associated with sustainable human performance, primarily through autonomous motivation. The study highlights the importance of participatory digital governance, workload management, and employee recovery measures for supporting sustainable human performance.

papers.title: Context-aware tooth instance segmentation and missing-tooth localization in panoramic radiographs
papers.abstract: Reliable localization and segmentation of individual teeth are fundamental for automated dental diagnostics and computer-aided treatment planning. However, panoramic radiographs pose persistent challenges due to anatomical variability, overlapping structures, and inconsistent image quality, thereby keeping clinical workflows heavily dependent on manual interpretation. This study introduces DentAll, a framework that integrates tooth instance segmentation with contextual estimation of anatomically expected missing-tooth locations. The proposed segmentation with Contextual Spatial Attention Blocks (S-CSAB) integrates dilated convolutions and ROI-based positional encoding to enhance fine-grained boundary delineation while maintaining anatomical coherence across adjacent teeth. Building upon these contextual features, the Missing-Tooth Localization Predictor (MTLP) estimates missing-tooth locations via patient-conditioned coordinate regression, using the target tooth’s identity together with the geometry of its nearest same-arch neighboring teeth, without requiring explicit missing-tooth annotations. DentAll was evaluated on 1,325 panoramic radiographs using instance-level segmentation metrics, COCO-style mask average precision, comparative baselines, and controlled pseudo-missing localization experiments. Under an all-ground-truth evaluation protocol, the framework achieved a DSC of 88.21% (92.74% among successfully matched instances), AP50 of 97.34%, AP75 of 87.20%, and mAP50:95 of 68.58%, while contextual MTLP localization improved the IoU ≥ 0.5 rate from 25.20% (index-only formulation) to 72.58%. These findings demonstrate that integrating instance segmentation with patient-specific anatomical context provides an effective and computationally practical framework for structured analysis of panoramic dental radiographs under anatomical variability.
papers.summary: Reliable localization and segmentation of individual teeth are fundamental for automated dental diagnostics and computer-aided treatment planning. DentAll was evaluated on 1,325 panoramic radiographs using instance-level segmentation metrics, COCO-style mask average precision, comparative baselines, and controlled pseudo-missing localization experiments. These findings demonstrate that integrating instance segmentation with patient-specific anatomical context provides an effective and computationally practical framework for structured analysis of panoramic dental radiographs under anatomical variability.

papers.title: Brain tumor classification from contrast-enhanced T1 MRI, a patient-wise deep learning study
papers.abstract: Accurate classification of intracranial tumors on contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI (CE-T1) is challenged by heterogeneous enhancement patterns and strong correlations among multiple slices from the same patient. We propose a compact CE-T1 MRI analysis framework that standardizes image intensities, enhances local CLAHE (contrast using contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization), and applies a lightweight convolutional classifier whose slice-level probabilities are aggregated to obtain a single patient-level prediction. An independent optional U-Net-based pathway provides binary tumor segmentation when spatial delineation is required. Evaluation was performed using a strictly patient-wise, leakage-controlled protocol with stratified five-fold cross-validation on 233 subjects (3,064 slices) comprising glioma, meningioma, and pituitary adenoma. The classifier achieved 99.4% patient-level accuracy, with macro-averaged sensitivity and specificity of 99.3% and 99.0%, respectively. The optional segmentation pathway achieved a mean Dice similarity coefficient of 97.3%. Post-hoc temperature scaling reduced the patient-level expected calibration error from 3.0% to approximately 1.2%, although larger independent cohorts are required to determine the stability of this estimate. The classifier contains 7.8 million parameters and requires approximately 15.9 GFLOPs per $$256\times 256$$ slice, with an end-to-end inference latency of approximately 0.41 s per slice under the evaluated hardware configuration. These findings demonstrate strong patient-level performance within the evaluated retrospective cohort. The framework is intended as a research-stage approach for reproducible evaluation rather than a clinically validated diagnostic system for routine radiology practice. However, no independent quantitative external validation was performed; therefore, multi-centre evaluation across different scanners, acquisition protocols, institutions, and patient populations is required before generalizability or clinical applicability can be established.

papers.title: Changes in the suitable habitat of Ectropis grisescens (Warren, 1894) (Lepidoptera: Geometridae) in China under climate change
papers.abstract: Introduction Ectropis grisescens is a major pest species infesting tea plants ( Camellia sinensis ). In this study, we developed an ensemble species distribution model using the Biomod2 framework to predict the potential suitable habitat of E. grisescens and identify the key environmental factors limiting its distribution, thereby providing a theoretical basis for effective prevention and control strategies. Methods A total of 149 geographic occurrence records and 12 environmental predictors were used to simulate the current potential distribution of E. grisescens and to analyze the dominant driving variables. Future changes in suitable habitat were also projected under three climate scenarios (SSP126, SSP245, and SSP585) for the 2050s and 2070s. Results The Biomod2 ensemble model demonstrated high predictive accuracy and reliability (AUC = 0.973, TSS = 0.845). Among the 12 selected environmental predictors, bio1, bio2, elevation, and bio17 were identified as the key factors, with contribution rates of 32.46%, 26.01%, 18.78%, and 15.71%, respectively. Under current climate conditions, the suitable habitat of E. grisescens is mainly distributed in southeastern China (Sichuan, Shaanxi, Chongqing, Guizhou, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Guangxi, and Guangdong provinces), covering an area of 169.33 × 10⁴ km². Under future climate scenarios, the suitable habitat area decreased in all cases, declining to 168.83 × 10⁴ km² under SSP126 in the 2070s and to 100.28 × 10⁴ km² under SSP585 in the 2070s. Under future climate scenarios, the centroid of the suitable habitat of E. grisescens shifted northward in all cases, with the greatest cumulative displacement of 171.56 km (SSP585) and the smallest cumulative displacement of 86.05 km (SSP126). Discussion These findings provide important scientific evidence for the future management and monitoring of E. grisescens .

In this study, we developed an ensemble species distribution model using the Biomod2 framework to predict the potential suitable habitat of E. Results The Biomod2 ensemble model demonstrated high predictive accuracy and reliability (AUC = 0.973, TSS = 0.845).

papers.title: Structural modification and toxicity reduction of coal tar pitch via alkylation with long-chain alkenes
papers.abstract: Coal tar pitch (CTP) contains a high content of toxic polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), posing potential risks to human health and ecological environment, limiting its sustainable utilization. In this study, long-chain alkene alkylation was developed to reduce the toxic PAHs risks associated with CTP. Single-factor experiments were first conducted using phenanthrene, anthracene, fluoranthene, and pyrene as model compounds, and the optimized conditions were subsequently applied to CTP to produce modified CTP (MCTP). Changes in the chemical structure and carbon skeleton were characterized, while environmental risks were evaluated based on a multidimensional comprehensive toxicity assessment. The content of the 16 U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) priority parent PAHs decreased from 132.92 mg/g to 78.20 mg/g, corresponding to a 41.17% reduction, while 16 priority parent PAHs in the collected fumes decreased by 40.30%. Structural analyses indicated that long-chain alkyl groups were introduced at the edges of aromatic structures, accompanied by increased structural disorder. MCTP also exhibited lower TEQs and cytotoxicity, and decreased phytotoxicity toward the roots and shoots of mung beans. These findings demonstrated that long-chain alkene alkylation can reduce the chemical and biological risks of CTP while altering its carbon structure, providing an effective approach for cleaner CTP utilization and environmental risk management.

These findings demonstrated that long-chain alkene alkylation can reduce the chemical and biological risks of CTP while altering its carbon structure, providing an effective approach for cleaner CTP utilization and environmental risk management.

papers.title: Genome-wide identification and expression profiling of the 14-3–3 gene family in woodland strawberry (Fragaria vesca) under abiotic stresses and hormone treatments
papers.abstract: 14-3-3 proteins constitute a highly conserved regulatory protein family in eukaryotes, playing indispensable roles in plant growth, development, and stress responses. Although the 14-3–3 gene family has been characterized in many plant species, its identification and involvement in stress responses remain unexplored in Fragaria vesca . In this study, We identified 14-3–3 genes in three Rosaceae genomes, with 8, 9, and 9 members in Fragaria vesca , Rubus occidentalis , and Prunus davidiana , respectively. Subsequently, we conducted a comprehensive analysis of the strawberry gene family, covering their physicochemical properties, phylogeny, chromosomal locations, exon–intron structures, and expression patterns. Multiple sequence alignments and secondary structure predictions of Fv14-3–3 proteins indicated all the members contained nine conserved antiparallel α-helices. Phylogenetic analysis showed that they were categorized into ϵ and non-ϵ groups with four members, respectively. The Fv14-3–3 gene family members were unevenly distributed across the chromosomes, most proteins within each group shared similar conserved motifs, and gene structure analysis showed that gene length and intron number varied greatly among the members within the ϵ group, with FvGF14c having a single-exon structure. Promoter sequence analysis showed that the Fv14-3–3 gene promoters contained more cis-acting elements related to abiotic stress tolerance and phytohormone responses. RNA-seq data showed that Fv14–3–3 genes were expressed in all tissues of strawberry but that their expression patterns were different. Quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) showed that almost all Fv14-3–3 genes responded to drought, salt, cold, and heat stresses, as well as to SA and ABA, albeit with distinct expression patterns. FvGF14g may be involved in the regulation of fruit ripening through the ABA signaling pathway. Our results provide a systematic characterization of the Fv14-3–3 gene family and their expression patterns under abiotic stress and phytohormone treatments, establishing a preliminary basis for the functional validation of Fv14-3–3 genes in these processes.

papers.title: Retrospective prediction of registration-derived pesticide mixture restriction associations: evaluating knowledge graph and graph-free models
papers.abstract: Pesticide tank mixing is widely used to improve the efficiency and flexibility of crop protection. However, mixture performance depends not only on the molecular structures and physicochemical properties of the constituent pesticides but also on practical application contexts, including formulation types, target crops, target organisms, application methods, and technical requirements. These context-dependent factors make potentially incompatible or antagonistic combinations difficult to identify from molecular structures and physicochemical properties alone; in registration texts the corresponding constraints appear as documentary mixture-restriction evidence rather than as experimentally measured outcomes. Although pesticide registration documents contain authoritative information on practical use conditions, most of this information remains embedded in unstructured text and is rarely incorporated into computational analysis of registration-derived mixture restrictions. This study addresses binary prediction of registration-derived restriction associations for pesticide pairs. Positive labels are derived from mixture-restriction evidence recorded in pesticide registration texts, which primarily reflect antagonistic interactions. The model outputs a relative association score for registration-derived restriction evidence and is not intended to represent other risk types such as physical incompatibility, chemical instability, or phytotoxicity, nor does it provide experimentally verified incompatibility conclusions. This study developed FMPIP as a computational framework for predicting pesticide-pair associations with restriction evidence derived from pesticide registration information. The current study was designed as a retrospective computational evaluation rather than a prospective validation of physical, chemical, or biological mixture incompatibility. To address this limitation, we propose a structured knowledge-driven framework integrating registration-text structuring, multi-source knowledge graph construction, and graph-based registration-derived restriction association prediction. First, a previously validated single-stage entity–relation extraction method is adapted as the knowledge-generation component to transform pesticide registration descriptions into structured usage-context knowledge. Direct statements indicating mixture restrictions are excluded from predictive inputs and are used only to generate registration-evidence-derived supervision labels, thereby separating label-generating evidence from model features. Second, non-label registration-derived contexts are integrated with molecular information and physicochemical attributes to construct a multi-source pesticide knowledge graph. Third, FMPIP is developed to estimate relative restriction-association scores for registration-derived restriction evidence by combining graph-based random neighborhood sampling with attention-based aggregation. FMPIP provides a relative association score for registration-derived restriction evidence. Within the retrospective benchmark, the score ranks pesticide pairs by their association with registration-derived restriction evidence; however, ranking-oriented metrics and practical baselines are not evaluated in this study, so practical prioritization capability is not demonstrated. The model output should not be interpreted as a direct prediction of physical, chemical, or biological mixture compatibility under specific application conditions. The knowledge-generation module achieved an F1-score of 96.6% on the pesticide registration dataset. For the downstream restriction-association prediction task, FMPIP achieved an AUC of 90.4%, an AUPR of 84.8%, and an F1-score of 84.4% on PID, outperforming all graph-based baselines re-evaluated under the same deduplicated, pair-disjoint protocol (AUC 85.5-85.9%, AUPR 72.3-75.3%, F1-score 71.9-76.3%). Ablation analysis showed that, after deduplication, removing any single information source did not reduce performance, suggesting that the contribution of registration context observed in the earlier, non-deduplicated evaluation. An order-invariant evaluation, in which pair scores do not depend on the storage orientation of a pair and the classification threshold is selected on validation data, obtained an AUC of 90.8% (SD 0.5), an AUPR of 82.5% (SD 1.0), and an F1-score of 85.0% (SD 0.5) on PID, confirming that this comparison is not an artifact of pair storage. The resulting scores should be interpreted as retrospective recovery of held-out restriction labels within the benchmark rather than as evidence of experimentally verified incompatibility or of practical prioritization capability. Independent regulatory or experimental validation is required before these predictions can be interpreted as evidence supporting prospective practical mixture decisions. These findings illustrate how regulatory pesticide-use text can be converted into structured contextual knowledge for retrospective mixture-restriction analysis.

Ablation analysis showed that, after deduplication, removing any single information source did not reduce performance, suggesting that the contribution of registration context observed in the earlier, non-deduplicated evaluation.

papers.title: Ultrasound-Assisted Cascade Valorisation of Olive Leaves for Sequential Recovery of Phenolic Antioxidants and Chlorophyll-Rich Pigments from Residual Biomass
papers.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
papers.abstract: Abstract An ultrasound-assisted cascade strategy valorized olive leaves through sequential recovery of phenolic antioxidants and chlorophyll-rich pigments. Sonotrode-assisted hydroethanolic extraction was optimized using a Box–Behnken design and compared with ultrasonic bath, reciprocating shaking and vortex-assisted extraction. The optimized extract contained 211 ± 12 mg gallic acid equivalents g–1 phenolics, 252 ± 13 mg rutin equivalents g–1 flavonoids, and 7000 ± 200 mg kg–1 oleuropein, its major compound. Sonotrode-assisted extraction achieved higher antioxidant recovery than the other extraction techniques, with CVs of approximately 3–9%. Subsequent extraction of residual biomass yielded 900 ± 40 mg chlorophyll kg–1 dry leaves, approximately 29% more than direct extraction of untreated leaves. The pigment-rich extract showed concentration-dependent antimicrobial activity, achieving 99.993 ± 0.008% inhibition against Escherichia coli and 99.9 ± 0.2% against total aerobic microorganisms at 10% extract concentration. Thus, phenolic extraction also preconditioned biomass for enhanced pigment recovery, supporting integrated olive leaf valorization.

papers.title: Regional variation in database-derived soil organic carbon and its associations with vegetation and the environment in the coniferous forests of the Greater and Lesser Khingan Mountains
papers.journal: Frontiers in Forests and Global Change
papers.abstract: Introduction Northeastern China’s conifer forests constitute important components of the world’s carbon cycle. However, whether soil organic carbon (SOC) is associated with the same environmental and biotic pathways across the Greater Khingan Mountains (GKM) and Lesser Khingan Mountains (LKM) remains unclear. Methods Using data from 282 plots in GKM and 334 plots in LKM, together with soil carbon data from CSDLv2, we conducted regional comparisons, Spearman correlations, and structural equation modelling to identify the environmental and biotic factors associated with SOC in GKM and LKM. Results We found that aboveground tree carbon stock (AGTC) was higher in LKM than in GKM (71.76 versus 55.81 Mg C ha −1 , but this difference was not significant ( p > 0.05). By contrast, SOC concentration was higher in GKM than in LKM (5.9 vs. 4.98 g/100 g; p < 0.05). The Spearman test showed that ectomycorrhizal trees (EcM_T) were positively correlated with SOC in both regions (LKM: r = 0.48; GKM: r = 0.46, p < 0.05). MAT had positive correlations in the LKM ( r = 0.3, p < 0.05) but negative correlations in the GKM ( r = −0.62, respectively, p < 0.05). Structural equation models further identified the positive total effects of EcM_T on SOC between GKM and LKM. MAT had the biggest total effect (−0.52, 37%) on SOC in GKM, while MAP had the strongest positive effect (0.28, 36%) in GKM. EcM_T (14%) contributed more than TR (0.7%) to SOC in LKM, while TR (18%) had a bigger effect than EcM_T (7%) GKM. Discussion These findings show that SOC patterns in northeastern China’s coniferous forests are region-dependent. Climate factor, soil properties, and EcM tree communities are important factors that affect conifer forest SOC in temperate forests.

papers.title: Extracellular matrix remodeling associated with air pollution and spaceflight
papers.abstract: Air pollution remains one of the most pervasive environmental threats to human health. While the biological effects of particulate matter, ozone, volatile organic compounds, and metal-rich aerosols are widely documented, their interactions with the extracellular matrix (ECM) remain insufficiently explored. This narrative review synthesizes mechanisms by which air pollutants induce ECM injury, with emphasis on metal-catalyzed oxidative modification of collagen and elastin, aldehyde adduct formation, matrix metalloproteinase (MMP) activation, and maladaptive fibrotic repair. Building on this evidence, we present the ECM convergence hypothesis as a hypothesis-generating framework, proposing that spaceflight stressors, including microgravity and ionizing radiation, may produce partially overlapping patterns of ECM remodeling through oxidative modification, altered mechanotransduction, and proteolytic imbalance. We assess the strength of evidence separately for each stressor and explicitly distinguish established findings from conceptual extrapolation, because direct head-to-head comparative studies are currently lacking. Finally, we critically evaluate emerging ECM-directed interventions, including redox and electrophile-control approaches, mechanotherapy, and ECM-targeted pharmacology, while examining ECM-derived biomarkers as potential tools for monitoring environmental tissue injury. We discuss the predominantly preclinical evidence base and the translational barriers relevant to both terrestrial environmental health and space medicine.

We discuss the predominantly preclinical evidence base and the translational barriers relevant to both terrestrial environmental health and space medicine.

papers.title: Bacterial Meningitis: A Review of Clinical and Public Health Testing
papers.abstract: Purpose of the Review This review provides an overview on the causative agents of bacterial meningitis, Neisseria meningitidis, Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, and Streptococcus agalactiae, along with rarer causes. Available test methods, surveillance activities, current challenges and limitations are included as well as a discussion on testing for bacterial meningitis that is performed clinically and at public health laboratories. Recent Findings Although clinical laboratories can provide rapid Gram staining and FDA approved PCR testing to detect bacterial meningitis pathogens, culture can be unsuccessful with the initiation of antibiotic therapy at the onset of meningitis symptoms. Public Health laboratories can provide additional molecular testing on primary specimens using laboratory developed tests (LDTs) to detect these pathogens, determine a molecular serotype, and assess antimicrobial resistance. When isolates are available, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, serogroup/serotype determination, and whole genome sequencing can be utilized for support surveillance and outbreak investigations, improve vaccine development, and ultimately reduce the burden of disease. Summary This review discusses causes of bacterial meningitis and the role that public health laboratories can play in clinical, surveillance and investigation testing to further characterize isolates or specimens, determine if transmission has occurred in investigations, and continue to provide comprehensive data to inform and improve vaccines.

papers.title: Coupled Time–Temperature–Moisture Superposition of PA 6: Temperature Regime‐Dependent Shift Behavior
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The viscoelastic response of hygroscopic polymers is strongly influenced by both temperature and moisture, challenging the application of classical time‐temperature superposition concepts. In this work, the thermoviscoelastic behavior of polyamide 6 (PA 6) under different conditioning states is investigated using dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA). Dry‐as‐molded (DAM), standard atmosphere conditioned (ATM), and soaked samples were analyzed in terms of storage modulus, loss factor, master curves, and temperature‐dependent shift factors. The results show that comparatively smooth storage modulus master curves can be constructed for the individual conditioning states, whereas the corresponding shift behavior differs significantly between the investigated moisture states. In particular, pronounced deviations are observed in the transition region, indicating moisture‐dependent changes in the underlying relaxation behavior. To account for these effects, an empirical coupled time–temperature–moisture shift formulation was applied using separate local fits for different temperature regimes. While the coupled approach improves the joint representation of the investigated conditioning states within the individual regimes, no single smooth global master curve can be obtained over the complete temperature and moisture range investigated. The results highlight the coupled and temperature regime‐dependent characteristics of the viscoelastic response of PA 6 under coupled temperature‐moisture conditions.

The results show that comparatively smooth storage modulus master curves can be constructed for the individual conditioning states, whereas the corresponding shift behavior differs significantly between the investigated moisture states.

papers.title: Real-time embedded control and performance evaluation of BLDC motors for electric vehicle applications
papers.abstract: Abstract Brushless DC (BLDC) motors are central to modern electric vehicle (EV) drivetrains, yet achieving high efficiency and stable torque under dynamic conditions remains a significant engineering challenge. This study presents the design and real-time embedded implementation of a motor control system realised on the STM32F103C8T6 microcontroller, together with a hardware-parameterised performance characterisation used to evaluate and cross-validate its behaviour. Two established control strategies—Trapezoidal Commutation and Field-Oriented Control (FOC)—were implemented independently on the same hardware platform under identical load conditions to enable a direct, unbiased comparison. The system incorporates Hall-effect sensor-based rotor position detection, closed-loop PI control (speed for Trapezoidal, d/q current for FOC), Direct Memory Access (DMA) for high-speed data acquisition, and a Controller Area Network (CAN) / Universal Asynchronous Receiver-Transmitter (UART) framework for real-time parameter transmission to a driver-facing display. Characterised performance results, derived from the implemented hardware's own rated parameters, show that FOC achieves a peak efficiency of 92% versus 86% under Trapezoidal Control, with torque ripple reduced by approximately 40% and peak current lowered from 50 to 44 A. The characterised thermal behaviour indicates that FOC maintains motor temperatures below 70 °C at full load, whereas Trapezoidal Control approaches critical thresholds under equivalent conditions. The modular architecture supports scalability across microcontroller tiers and EV configurations, providing a validated and deployable reference for energy-efficient BLDC drive systems.

papers.title: A novel role of NOX2 in enhancing HBV replication through ROS‑mediated autophagy activation
papers.abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) is a serious global public health issue. Mounting evidence suggests that NADPH oxidase 2 (NOX2) plays critical roles in various physiological and pathological processes. However, the underlying mechanisms by which NOX2 affects HBV infection remain to be elucidated. In the present study, the potential role of NOX2 in HBV replication was investigated in cell models. First, it was demonstrated that NOX2 is highly expressed in transiently and stably HBV‑infected cells. Second, by employing inhibitor, RNA interference technique and plasmid overexpression, it was revealed that NOX2 plays an essential role in promoting HBV replication. Furthermore, the underlying mechanism of how NOX2 affects HBV replication was illustrated. It was found that NOX2‑mediated ROS induce an increase of intracellular autophagy levels, which result in facilitating HBV replication. These results suggested a previously unrecognized role of NOX2 in HBV replication. Taken together, NOX2 may serve as a novel target for developing treatment strategies against HBV‑related disorders.

papers.title: Hierarchical active learning for annotation-efficient 3D object detection in construction-scene LiDAR sensing
papers.journal: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
papers.abstract: 3D object detection in construction-scene LiDAR sensing remains challenging because sparse returns, irregular layouts, heavy occlusion, and diverse machinery make object representation and localization difficult. Dense manual annotation in such scenes is also inefficient and costly, creating a strong need for annotation-efficient learning. Existing active-learning methods often struggle in this setting because they tend to favor uncertain but redundant samples while overlooking representative scene coverage. To address this problem, we propose Hierarchical Clustering-enhanced Active Learning (HCAL), an active-learning framework for LiDAR-based 3D object detection in construction and roadwork environments. HCAL improves sample selection under limited labeling budgets by identifying informative candidate keyframes, suppressing redundant uncertain samples, and preserving representative coverage through entropy filtering, gradient-space clustering, and density-consistency selection. To support field-relevant evaluation, we further establish ConVeh3D as a construction-scene LiDAR benchmark for annotation-efficient 3D detection and unknown-category-aware evaluation in a controlled category-withheld setting. Experiments on ConVeh3D, with KITTI as secondary supporting evidence, show that HCAL achieves the best average detection accuracy across most tested labeling budgets. The results indicate that HCAL provides an effective framework for improving sample efficiency in construction-scene LiDAR-based 3D object detection under limited labeling budgets. The dataset and code will be made available at https://github.com/zxk688/ConVeh3D .

papers.title: Formulation and Evaluation of Bilayer Tablet of Atorvastain Calcium (Immediate Release) and Nifedipine (Sustained Release)
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, with hypertension and dyslipidemia frequently occurring together and significantly increasing cardiovascular risk. Long-term management of these conditions often requires multiple medications, leading to increased pill burden and reduced patient compliance. The present study aimed to formulate and evaluate a bilayer tablet comprising an immediaterelease (IR) layer of Atorvastatin Calcium and a sustained-release (SR) layer of Nifedipine to provide combined therapeutic benefits in a single dosage form. Preformulation studies, including organoleptic evaluation, solubility studies, calibration curve preparation, and drug–excipient compatibility studies using FTIR and DSC, were performed. The immediate-release layer of Atorvastatin Calcium was formulated using suitable superdisintegrants to achieve rapid drug release, whereas the sustained-release layer of Nifedipine was developed using HPMC K100M as a release-retarding polymer to prolong drug release. Bilayer tablets were prepared by the direct compression technique and evaluated for pre-compression parameters such as angle of repose, bulk density, tapped density, Carr’s index, and Hausner ratio. Post-compression evaluation included hardness, thickness, weight variation, friability, drug content uniformity, and in vitro dissolution studies. The prepared formulations exhibited satisfactory flow properties and acceptable physicochemical characteristics. The immediate-release layer demonstrated rapid drug release, while the sustained-release layer provided prolonged release of Nifedipine over the desired period. Drug release kinetics indicated diffusion-controlled release from the sustained-release matrix. The optimized formulation showed satisfactory tablet integrity and performance characteristics. The study demonstrates that bilayer tablet technology can successfully combine immediate and sustained drug release profiles within a single dosage form. Such a formulation has the potential to improve patient compliance, reduce dosing frequency, and provide effective management of patients suffering from concurrent hypertension and dyslipidemia.

papers.title: Experimental and numerical investigation of backstreaming positive ions in an RF-driven negative ion source
papers.abstract: Abstract Backstreaming positive ions are an unavoidable byproduct in high-power negative ion-based neutral beam injection systems, posing a critical challenge to the long-pulse operational stability of ion sources due to the significant heat loads and material erosion they induce. This paper presents a comprehensive experimental and numerical investigation into the generation, spatial distribution, and thermal effects of BSPIs in the dual-RF-driver negative ion source at the HONOR test facility of CRAFT. Using a water-flow calorimetry diagnostic system, the dependence of the Backstreaming positive ion power fraction (PBSPI/Pbeam) on key operational parameters was systematically studied. The results show that the PBSPI/Pbeam ratio increases monotonically with the source filling pressure, rising from ~2.05% at 0.3 Pa to ~3.15% at 0.57 Pa. A non-monotonic dependence on beam energy is observed, with the ratio peaking at ~2.65% at 161 keV. This trend is attributed to the competition between the improved geometric transmission efficiency of BSPIs—resulting from reduced beam divergence at moderate energies—and the intrinsic decrease in collision cross-sections at higher energies. Furthermore, the ratio is found to decrease with increasing extracted beam current, which is explained by the space-charge-induced beam divergence that reduces the geometric transmission efficiency through the acceleration grids. Distinct BSPI bombardment traces on the backplate exhibit an array pattern corresponding to the plasma grid apertures. Coupled thermal-fluid-solid simulations, incorporating the measured heat loads, indicate that under typical high-power conditions (190 kV, 16.2 A), the maximum backplate temperature remains well below the material safety limit. This work clarifies the key mechanisms governing BSPI generation and validates the thermal reliability of the backplate design, providing a solid basis for the development of high-power NNBI systems.

papers.title: Magnetization of a branched polyaminoacid chain: properties investigation, Cr(VI) removal, and CO2 adsorption-desorption potential
papers.abstract: A novel magnetic branched polyamino acid adsorbent (S6) was synthesized through covalent grafting of a polyamino acid chain onto a Fe3O4@SiO2 core. The material displayed a CO2 capture capacity of 275 mg/g at 75 °C, with only 5.6% loss in performance after seven adsorption-desorption cycles. For Cr(VI) removal from aqueous solutions, the adsorbent achieved a maximum uptake of 64.98 mg/g under optimal conditions (pH 3.5, initial concentration 80 mg/L, temperature 65 °C). Thermodynamic analysis revealed the Cr(VI) adsorption process was spontaneous (negative ΔG values across 298–348 K) and endothermic (ΔH = + 78.04 kJ/mol), with increased disorder at the solid-liquid interface (ΔS = + 255.18 J/mol·K). The material maintained over 95% Cr(VI) removal efficiency after eleven regeneration cycles. The thermogravimetric analysis-differential thermal analysis (TGA-DTA) confirmed an organic-to-inorganic ratio exceeding 5:1, while VSM analysis showed saturation magnetization of 19.58 emu/g, enabling magnetic separation. The strip-shaped morphology and mesoporous structure (surface area 62.14 m²/g, pore diameter 6.99 nm) contributed to its dual functionality for gas capture and heavy metal remediation. Polyamino acid was branched and grafted to Fe3O4@SiO2 by a facile method. The sample exhibits good adsorption capacity (275 mg/g) for carbon dioxide and has good recycling performance. After successful synthesis, the sample was characterized by FT-IR, XRD, and EDS techniques. The sample has a good potential Cr (VI) ion adsorption and achieved a remarkable maximum absorption capacity of 64.98 mg/g at pH=3.5.

papers.title: Development and Characterization of a Sustainable Form-Stabilized Phase Change Materials incorporating industrial waste for Battery Thermal Management Applications
papers.abstract: The need for reliable thermal management strategies has intensified with the rapid growth of lithium-ion batteries used in electric vehicles especially in hot climates where high ambient temperatures accelerate degradation, reduce efficiency and raise safety risks. Owing to their high latent heat storage and ability to maintain stable temperatures, phase change materials (PCMs) appear to be promising candidates for passive cooling. However, the leakage issues as well as lower thermal conductivity of PCM limits its practical application in battery thermal management. This study presents a sustainable form-stabilized PCM (FS-PCM) which is developed using paraffin RT42 mixed with Oil Ash (OA), an industrial waste material under a controlled environment. The composite prepared via vacuum impregnation at 45 wt% RT42 and 55 wt% OA, demonstrated structural stability with no chemical interaction as confirmed by X-ray diffraction. Thermal analysis showed a melting temperature of 33.8°C and latent heat of 81.5 J/g suitable for battery thermal regulation. The PCM was encapsulated within the porous OA matrix and showed uniform elemental distribution as revealed in microstructural characterization. Application of FS-PCM significantly enhanced the battery thermal management by decreasing the elevated temperature up to 7.25°C at the 4C discharge rates and maintaining temperature uniformity within safe limits (<5°C) when FS-PCM thickness is 7 mm. Overall, the developed FS-PCM offers a cost-effective, sustainable, and efficient solution for passive battery cooling in high-temperature environments.
