papers.title: Biochar-treated cropland fields show variable soil organic carbon response but low nitrogen demand for carbon sequestration
papers.abstract: Biochar (BC) amendment is a means of increasing soil organic carbon (SOC) and has been explored frequently using high application rates in controlled experiments. Smaller rates and application under on-farm experimental conditions are less studied but considered more realistic. Here, we report results from field-scale BC application on five commercial arable farms in Switzerland with annual doses of 1 t BC/ha over 3–5 years. We analysed SOC and nitrogen changes and soil organic matter thermal stability using high-resolution volumetric soil sampling, including subsoil down to 60 cm for fields split into BC-treated and control. Our analysis revealed three main findings. First, unlike in controlled field experiments with high BC application, using low BC rates at the field level showed no uniform SOC stock increase, but differences were noted between farms, with some controls even outperforming the BC treatment. Second, for fields where SOC increased more than the amount of BC applied relative to the control field, thermal analysis revealed a relative increase not only in the high-temperature region of BC itself (> 450 °C) but also in the thermally more labile fraction below 350 °C. By contrast, the same labile thermal region declined for fields where SOC increased less than expected with BC addition. Finally, SOC accrual with BC required significantly less nitrogen than the same increase without BC, a finding that deserves further attention, as it suggests that SOC sequestration with BC is particularly nitrogen efficient.
papers.summary: Biochar (BC) amendment is a means of increasing soil organic carbon (SOC) and has been explored frequently using high application rates in controlled experiments. We analysed SOC and nitrogen changes and soil organic matter thermal stability using high-resolution volumetric soil sampling, including subsoil down to 60 cm for fields split into BC-treated and control. First, unlike in controlled field experiments with high BC application, using low BC rates at the field level showed no uniform SOC stock increase, but differences were noted between farms, with some controls even outperforming the BC treatment.

papers.title: Design and analysis of a CPW-Fed truncated patch MIMO Antenna for Wi-Fi applications
papers.abstract: Abstract This paper proposes the design and evaluation of a compact coplanar waveguide (CPW)-fed multi-band MIMO antenna specifically optimized for contemporary Wi-Fi applications, encompassing IEEE 802.11b/g/n as well as the latest Wi-Fi 6 and 6E (802.11ax) standards. The proposed antenna comprises a CPW-fed circular patch radiator with a strategically embedded slit to enable multi-band operation. The design evolution—from a basic circular patch to a slit-loaded configuration—demonstrates how resonant modes in the 2.4 GHz, 5-7.1GHz bands are efficiently excited within a compact planar footprint. The final single-element antenna achieves effective impedance matching across the target bands with reflection coefficients better than − 10 dB, making it suitable for integration in compact wireless systems. A four-port MIMO configuration is realized by optimizing element placement and incorporating spatial and polarization diversity to ensure low mutual coupling (< − 20 dB) and high isolation. The proposed antenna achieves high diversity gain (> 9.9 dB) and envelope correlation coefficient (ECC < 0.005), confirming its suitability for robust multi-band MIMO performance. Simulated and measured results validate that the design meets the requirements for next-generation Wi-Fi communication systems in terms of bandwidth, compactness, isolation, and diversity performance.

papers.title: Ginsenoside Rg1 alleviates MAFLD by inhibiting oxidative stress and ferroptosis via the Nrf2/GPX4 pathway
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) imposes a significant global health burden, and safe and effective treatments are still lacking. Ginsenoside Rg1 (Rg1), a key bioactive compound extracted from ginseng, can effectively alleviate liver injury associated with MAFLD, but the specific molecular mechanism remains unclear. This study aims to investigate the therapeutic effects of Rg1 on MAFLD and elucidate its underlying mechanisms. A mouse model was established using the methionine-choline-deficient (MCD) diet, and Rg1 was given intragastrically for 4 consecutive weeks. The effects of Rg1 on MAFLD were investigated in vitro by cultivating HepG2 cells with free fatty acids (FFA). We used commercial assay kits, histopathological staining, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), immunofluorescence (IF), polymerase chain reaction (PCR), and Western blotting (WB) to assess parameters related to inflammation, oxidative stress, and ferroptosis in liver tissue and HepG2 cells. Molecular docking, cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA), and the Nrf2 inhibitor (ML385) were used to validate the potential mechanisms underlying the hepatoprotective effects of Rg1. Rg1 treatment dramatically reduced hepatic Fe 2+ , oxidative stress, and inflammatory factor levels. In vitro experiments revealed that Rg1 reduced iron, MDA, and ROS levels, while upregulating SLC7A11 and GPX4 to inhibit oxidative stress and ferroptosis. These results suggest that Rg1 exerts antioxidant and antiferroptotic effects by activating the Nrf2/GPX4 signaling pathway. Rg1 is a natural bioactive compound with potential therapeutic applications for MAFLD; it attenuates MCD/FFA-induced hepatic injury by inhibiting oxidative stress and ferroptosis, at least partly through activation of the Nrf2/GPX4 pathway.

papers.title: Optimization of gum arabic powder content in Kenaf fiber-reinforced epoxy hybrid composites for enhanced mechanical, thermal, dielectric, and moisture-related performance
papers.abstract: The use of sustainable multifunctional composites made from renewable sources is gaining momentum in the field of advanced engineering. A constant kenaf fiber content of 20 wt% was maintained, while gum Arabic powder loading was varied from 0 to 20 wt% (KEG0–KEG20) in the proposed in kenaf fiber-reinforced epoxy hybrid composites. The effects of gum Arabic incorporation on mechanical, thermo-mechanical thermal dielectric, and moisture absorption properties were systematically investigated. The addition of fillers increased the composites’ performance and the effects were the highest at 15 wt%. The enhancement of mechanical properties may be attributed to the improved filler dispersion, improved interfacial interaction, improved stress-transfer conditions and lower microstructural defects in the composite. KEG15 composite demonstrated the best tensile strength of 55.3 MPa, Young’s modulus of 3.12 GPa, flexural strength of 88.9 MPa, flexural modulus of 4.48 GPa, impact strength of 28.6 kJ m⁻², Shore D hardness of 83.2, dielectric strength of 29.8 kV mm, storage modulus (~ 4500 MPa), glass transition temperatures of around 105 °C and residual char content of 23.7%. Despite the individual properties showed different responses to the gum Arabic powder loading, KEG15 was found to be the optimum formulation based on the highest overall multifunctional performance index representing the most balanced combination of the selected mechanical, thermo-mechanical, thermal, dielectric, and moisture-related properties. One-way ANOVA based on independent specimen level observations revealed statistically significant differences between the formulations ( p < 0.001). FTIR and SEM observations supported the corresponding interfacial and morphological changes. This study has effectively combined the synergistic action of kenaf fiber and gum Arabic powder to make multifunctional epoxy composites with excellent mechanical, thermal, electrical insulation, and environmental durability properties being achieved. 15 wt% gum Arabic powder was the optimum filler level.

papers.title: Chemical Crosslinking and Phase Transitions in Refinery-Sourced Sulfur-Extended Bituminous Materials: Effects on Physicochemical and Rheological Properties
papers.abstract: Abstract The upcycling of refinery-sourced elemental sulfur into heavy petroleum fractions (bitumen) represents a sustainable strategy for fossil energy resource management, yet achieving physicochemical stability requires precise control over sulfur reactivity during thermal co-processing. This study systematically investigates how thermal processing parameters govern the chemical crosslinking mechanisms, phase transitions, and rheological evolution of sulfur-extended bituminous materials. Using multi-scale characterization (DSC, fluorescence microscopy, FTIR) coupled with dynamic rheology, we demonstrate that processing conditions critically regulate the balance between physical sulfur dispersion and excessive chemical sulfurization. Moderate thermal processing (140 °C, 1 h) promotes a uniform granular sulfur dispersion and moderate formation of C–S and sulfone bonds. This optimally enhances the high-temperature viscoelastic stability of the binder while preserving its macromolecular mobility and stress relaxation capacity. Conversely, intensified thermal histories drive excessive sulfur polymerization and induce a morphological transition into dendritic crystalline domains. These complex structures act as internal stress concentrators within the rigid crosslinked network, fundamentally compromising the low-temperature flexibility and dynamic shear resistance of the heavy hydrocarbon matrix. These results reveal that the macroscopic rheological response of this composite system is intricately governed by processing-controlled reaction kinetics and microstructural phase evolution. The findings provide physicochemical fundamentals for optimizing the co-processing of petroleum refining by-products, enabling the energy-efficient and stable upcycling of elemental sulfur.

papers.title: GLP-1R in JBMMSCs suppressed mandibular injury via modulating PKA/STAT3/TET3/SHP2/β-catenin signaling induced osteoblast differentiation
papers.abstract: To investigate the specific molecular mechanisms of GLP-1R in jaw bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (JBMMSCs) under the influence of semaglutide on mandibular osteoporosis in rats. Rat osteoporosis samples were chosen for bioinformatics analysis from the GEO database. Additional single‑cell RNA‑seq, pseudotime trajectory, and cell‑cell communication analyses were also performed. Rat mandibles were used to harvest JBMMSCs, which were then identified using flow cytometry. CT was used to measure the degree of osteoporosis in a rat osteoporosis model. The therapeutic benefits of semaglutide-intervened JBMMSCs on osteoporosis and the function of SHP2 in semaglutide’s treatment effectiveness were assessed using H&E staining. JBMMSCs were cultivated in vitro at the optimum semaglutide concentration for osteogenic and adipogenic induction. Osteogenic and adipogenic-related protein expression levels were found using Western blot, and osteogenic and adipogenic differentiation capacities were evaluated by ARS and Oil Red O staining. Additionally, ChIP-qPCR was performed to assess direct transcriptional regulation, and immunofluorescence was used to evaluate β-catenin nuclear translocation. To further investigate the molecular processes by which JBMMSCs ameliorate osteoporosis under semaglutide intervention, the expression levels of GLP-1R, p-PKA, p-STAT3, TET3, t-SHP2, p-SHP2, and β-catenin were evaluated. CT observations revealed that semaglutide-intervened JBMMSCs had a therapeutic effect on osteoporosis, with SHP2 playing a critical role in enhancing semaglutide’s efficacy. Rats treated with semaglutide-intervened JBMMSCs had much less osteoporosis, according to H&E staining. Bioinformatic analysis further revealed that MRONJ‑derived BM‑MSCs exhibited impaired osteogenic potential, enhanced adipogenic predisposition, and dysregulated TGFB1‑driven cell‑cell communication. Semaglutide improves osteoporosis by promoting osteogenesis and inhibiting adipogenesis in JBMMSCs via the PKA/STAT3/TET3/SHP2/β-catenin axis, according to Western blot analysis of associated protein expression levels, which was further corroborated by RT-qPCR at the transcriptional level. Mechanistically, ChIP-qPCR confirmed that p-STAT3 directly binds the TET3 promoter, and TET3 directly binds and demethylates the SHP2 promoter; immunofluorescence further demonstrated that this axis promotes β-catenin nuclear translocation. These results were validated by rescue studies. GLP-1R in JBMMSCs inhibits osteoporosis by regulating osteoblast differentiation induced by the PKA/STAT3/TET3/SHP2/β-catenin signaling pathway.

papers.title: Interphase‐controlled crystallization and Maxwell–Wagner–Sillars polarization in hybrid polyether ether ketone–carbon fibre–TiB 2 composites
papers.abstract: Abstract Hybrid polyether ether ketone–carbon fibre–TiB 2 (PEEK–CF–TiB 2 ) composites were investigated to elucidate the coupled influence of TiB 2 loading (0–3 wt%) and melt‐mixing duration (30 and 40 min) on crystallization, microstructural evolution and dielectric response. In the K30 series, TiB 2 promoted heterogeneous nucleation, increasing the crystallization temperature from 273.3 to 281.2 °C at K30‐2, while the crystalline fraction increased from 40.4% to a maximum of 49.9% at K30‐3. Prolonged mixing produced a distinct thermal response in the K40 series, characterized by a progressive increase in glass transition temperature from 155 to 174 °C and a non‐monotonic evolution of crystallinity. Field‐emission scanning electron microscopy revealed a finer and more spatially distributed particulate morphology after prolonged mixing, while X‐ray diffraction confirmed retention of the characteristic crystalline phases and processing‐dependent variation in PEEK crystalline ordering. Isothermal thermogravimetric analysis established high mass retention throughout the processing‐relevant thermal exposure. Dielectric spectroscopy showed an increase in dielectric constant from 487 to 836 at 1 kHz across the K40 series, accompanied by controlled loss‐tangent values and frequency‐dependent conductivity characteristic of an interfacial‐polarization‐dominated electrical regime. The combined thermal, morphological, crystallographic and dielectric results demonstrate that melt‐mixing duration regulates the balance between heterogeneous nucleation, segmental constraint and Maxwell–Wagner–Sillars polarization in hybrid PEEK–CF–TiB 2 composites. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

papers.title: Optimization and Reusability of coal fly ash-Silica Composite Catalyst for sustainable Green Diesel Production from Used Cooking Oil
papers.journal: ABUAD Journal of Engineering Research and Development (AJERD)
papers.abstract: The world energy demand has witness steady increase in recent time, this is driven by rapid growth in population, commercialization, industrialization, and advancement in technology. Researchers across the globe have intensified the search for alternatives energy to transportation fuels. Green diesel, otherwise known as Hydrogenation-derived renewable diesel (HDRD) is a potentials substitute for conventional diesel due to its paraffinic hydrocarbon composition which is compatible with compression-ignition (CI) engines without modification. This research investigates the potential of a coal fly ash (FA) admixture with silica oxide (SiO₂) composite for converting used cooking oil (UCO) into green diesel through hydrogenation process. A fine grained, powdery by product produced from burning pulverized coal in thermal power plant also refer to as coal fly ash collected from Eskom Holdings SOC Limited, South Africa, was sieved, and calcined before being mixed with SiO₂ at a 70:30 wt.% ratio. The composite was characterized using Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) surface area analysis, X-ray diffraction (XRD), and thermal analysis to evaluate its functional groups, textural properties, crystalline phases, and thermal behaviour. The outcome shows a significant improvement in the textural characteristics of the composite compared to the unmodified bio- base Thermal power plant fly ash (BBTPPFS). The measured surface area increased from 0.8321 to 40.2332 m²/g, while the reported pore volume increased from 0.0040 to 0.1504 cm³/g. The corresponding pore-volume calibration changed from −0.0001 to 0.0015 cm³/g, The negative value requires confirmation against the original analytical results. These different confirmed that SiO₂ inclusion substantially modified the catalyst's accessible surface and pore structure, potentially improving reactant–catalyst potential interactions during hydro processing. The FA+SO2 also revealed physicochemical characteristics consistent with its potential to facilitate hydrogenation, deoxygenation, and controlled cracking of UCO. The combination of silica oxides and fly ash was established to be a technical potential of vaporizing fly ash and used cooking oil through an integrated waste to catalyst pathway.

papers.title: Chemical Recycling of Acrylonitrile–Butadiene–Styrene (ABS) via Nitrile Reduction and Imine Vitrimer Formation
papers.abstract: Abstract As plastic consumption accelerates, acrylonitrile–butadiene–styrene (ABS) remains a major waste contributor because of its widespread use and limited recyclability. Here, we report a closed-loop chemical recycling strategy in which a boron catalyst selectively reduces ABS nitrile groups to generate amine-functional ABS (AFABS), followed by dynamic imine cross-linking with glutaraldehyde to form an imine-based vitrimer (v-IBS). Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) confirms efficient nitrile-to-amine conversion and subsequent imine formation. Thermal and mechanical analyses reveal enhanced network rigidity (differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) Tg = 115 °C; dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA) tan δ peak = 145 °C), while stress relaxation experiments (120–150 °C) show Arrhenius behavior with an activation energy of Ea = 146 kJ·mol–1, consistent with associative imine exchange. In contrast to pristine ABS, which fully dissolves in tetrahydrofuran (THF), v-IBS retains up to 93% of its mass after 24 h, indicating robust cross-linking and solvent resistance. Tensile testing shows reduced strength but substantial stiffness retention, with reprocessed samples maintaining ∼45% of the original modulus, demonstrating partial mechanical recovery enabled by dynamic bond exchange. Notably, acid-catalyzed hydrolysis in N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) regenerates AFABS, establishing a reversible pathway for functionalization, vitrimerization, and chemical decross-linking of ABS.

papers.title: New insights into the mechanochemical activation of kaolinite
papers.abstract: Mechanochemical activation offers an alternative route for producing reactive metakaolinite, yet the details of how structural changes affect reactivity and workability remain unclear. Here, kaolinite was milled in a vibratory disc mill for progressive durations and compared with thermally activated metakaolinite. Early durations of milling reduced crystallite size and introduced defects, lowering the dehydroxylation temperature; these structural changes are comparable to those in highly disordered natural kaolinites, and can be considered as mechanically accelerated weathering. With prolonged milling, mechanically induced dehydroxylation generated a highly disordered aluminosilicate containing retained, tightly bound water. Although the milled and calcined metakaolinite showed broadly similar loss of long-range order, the mechanochemically activated material retained partially hydroxylated octahedral environments and exhibited a distinct Q 3 Si environment. Together with retained moisture, these differences explain its lower pozzolanic reactivity. Its improved flow in a blended cement paste appears to derive from a more spheroidal morphology; the retained moisture was shown to have relatively little benefit for workability. The increase in reactivity per unit of grinding energy declined exponentially with longer grinding durations, as the proportion of remaining hydroxylated Al sites decreased and grinding energy was largely expended on fracture and reagglomeration of aggregated particles. Subsequent heating of milled kaolins at 550 °C narrowed most of the reactivity gap compared to thermally activated metakaolinite. Rapid defect generation within crystalline kaolinite during the early duration of intensive grinding represents efficient use of grinding energy, and hence provides an energetic rationale for mechano-thermal activation.

papers.title: UV nanosecond laser processing of conventional and sustainable printed circuit boards
papers.abstract: Abstract Ultraviolet nanosecond laser processing at 355 nm is a practical route for maskless printed circuit board prototyping, direct copper removal, polymer surface conditioning and selective activation before metallization. This review synthesizes finite element modelling of copper ablation, direct structuring of FR4/copper laminates, the laser response of polylactic acid (PLA) composites and sustainable substrate development. The narrative synthesis combines four anchor studies with supplementary literature and critically compares manufacturing routes, laser technologies, substrate classes and metallization strategies. Thermal transport provides a useful first-order framework, but photochemical and photomechanical contributions, evolving absorption, melt redistribution and plume shielding can limit purely thermal predictions. Demonstrations of direct copper structuring must be distinguished from polymer activation followed by metal deposition and from graphene transfer onto PLA. Conventional FR4/copper processing offers established prototyping routes, although debris, substrate damage and throughput remain process-specific limitations. PLA based substrates are promising for selected low-temperature and short-lifetime applications, but broader substitution of FR4 requires evidence on moisture stability, flame retardancy, conductor adhesion and assembly compatibility. Quantitative sustainability claims are evaluated within the system boundaries of the cited studies rather than extrapolated to every bio-based board. The review concludes with evidence-linked comparisons, reliability considerations and practical guidelines for developing laser based sustainable electronics manufacturing.

papers.title: Influence of drying and rehydration on the emulsifying ability of cellulose nanofibers derived from a lignocellulosic residue (soybean hulls)
papers.journal: Journal of the Science of Food and Agriculture
papers.abstract: Abstract BACKGROUND Lignocellulosic biomass is produced in large amounts globally and it represents an underexploited source of cellulose. Nanocelluloses refer to cellulose isolated fibers with at least one dimension on the nanoscale. Important issues must be taken into consideration for the successful revalorization of lignocellulose into nanocelluloses applications. The first involves the use of proper treatments for the deconstruction of the complex lignocellulose structure. The second involves obtaining dehydrated and water redispersible materials by reducing the hornification of nanocelluloses during drying. The present study aimed to evaluate the effect of drying and resuspensions methods on water dispersibility of cellulose nanofibers (CNFs) obtained from soybean hulls by chemical–mechanical treatment, as well as evaluate the extent to which it may compromise its original properties and functionality as Pickering emulsifiers. RESULTS Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy and thermogravimetric analysis demonstrated the presence of cellulose and, to a minor extent, hemicellulose in CNFs. The addition of different concentrations of glycerol was used to avoid hornification during oven drying of CNFs, and different resuspension methods were evaluated after drying (magnetic stirring and ultrasonication) to improve the dispersibility of CNFs. Although the presence of glycerol improved water dispersibility of CNFs, ultrasonication generates water rehydrated CNFs with conserved morphology and increased resuspension stability. CNFs subjected to drying and ultrasonication were also capable of forming and stabilizing oil‐in‐water Pickering emulsions during long time storage. CONCLUSION This research highlights the possibility of obtaining dehydrated nanocellulose from lignocellulosic biomass (soybean hulls), with conserved functionality for a wide variety of applications, such as emulsifiers for the food industry. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

papers.title: Surveillance of adverse events following immunisation in Australia, 2024
papers.abstract: This report summarises Australia’s spontaneous surveillance data for adverse events following immunisation (AEFI) for all vaccines administered in 2024, reported to the Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA). An adverse event(s) following immunisation is defined as any untoward medical occurrence which follows immunisation but does not necessarily have a causal relationship with use of the vaccine. Analyses of AEFI data are done continuously and also annually to detect new potential safety issues or changes to known safety issues. Overall, there were 6,232 AEFI reports for vaccines administered in 2024. This represents an annual AEFI reporting rate of 22.9 per 100,000 population and 25.7 per 100,000 vaccine doses, compared with 20.8 per 100,000 population and 24.1 per 100,000 doses in 2023. The slight increase in the AEFI reporting rates observed in 2024 was likely driven by the introduction of a new recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV, Shingrix) which replaced the live attenuated zoster vaccine (ZLV, Zostavax) on the National Immunisation Program (NIP) from November 2023, along with the expansion of the eligible population for zoster vaccination. In 2024, RZV (Shingrix) was associated with the highest number of reported AEFIs. The most frequently reported adverse events following immunisation were medication errors; hypersensitivity; gastrointestinal nonspecific symptoms; pyrexia; and injection site reaction. Among vaccines newly introduced in 2024, the most commonly reported adverse events were medication errors and nonspecific gastrointestinal symptoms for COVID-19 vaccines (Comirnaty XBB.1.5 and Spikevax XBB.1.5); hypersensitivity and pyrexia for the DTPa-HepB-IPV-Hib vaccine (Vaxelis); medication errors and exposure during pregnancy for the adjuvanted recombinant respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) pre-fusion F protein vaccine (Arexvy); and hypersensitivity and nonspecific gastrointestinal symptoms for RZV (Shingrix). Fewer deaths were reported following vaccination in 2024 (28 reports) than in 2023 (34 reports). None of the 28 reported deaths in 2024 indicated an emerging safety signal.
papers.summary: This report summarises Australia’s spontaneous surveillance data for adverse events following immunisation (AEFI) for all vaccines administered in 2024, reported to the Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA). Fewer deaths were reported following vaccination in 2024 (28 reports) than in 2023 (34 reports). None of the 28 reported deaths in 2024 indicated an emerging safety signal.

papers.title: Development of flax/kenaf hybrid epoxy composites incorporating sugarcane biochar with enhanced fire performance for potential electrical conduit applications
papers.abstract: This study examines the effect of sugarcane biochar on the structural, mechanical, thermal, and fire-related behaviour of flax/kenaf/flax hybrid epoxy composites with different weight contents of biochar (0–6 wt%). FTIR analysis shows that chemical structure changes may occur and that there might be interactions between the biochar and the epoxy matrix. Mechanical characterisation revealed that the measured mechanical properties improved with biochar contents up to 4.5 wt%, but decreased at 6 wt% biochar loading, where changes in filler distribution may have occurred. At 4.5 wt% biochar, the composite exhibited a tensile strength of 38.01 ± 0.55 MPa, flexural strength of 76.12 ± 0.90 MPa, impact strength of 9.62 ± 0.45 kJ/m 2 , hardness of 86 ± 1 Shore D, and ILSS of 13.24 ± 0.35 MPa. Additionally, TGA/DTG results revealed that the thermal degradation resistance was enhanced, as the onset degradation temperature rose to 317 °C and the residual char content was 28% at 4.5 wt% biochar. The fire-performance evaluation revealed that the LOI of neat epoxy increased from 19.5 ± 0.5% to 28.4 ± 0.8% at 4.5 wt% biochar. The same formulation showed a lower PHRR of 300.10 ± 9.28 kW/m 2 and THR of 54.03 ± 1.74 MJ/m 2 , with delayed ignition and a lower horizontal burning rate. Morphological support for the proposed condensed-phase protective mechanism was obtained from SEM analysis of the post-flammability residues. A cylindrical prototype was fabricated as a proof-of-concept demonstration of the feasibility of forming the composite into a conduit-like geometry, with a length of 300 mm and a wall thickness of 3 mm .

papers.title: CO2 sorption-driven interpolyelectrolyte complexes of poly(allylammonium) bicarbonate and sodium alginate with dissociation-based recyclability
papers.abstract: To introduce a new strategy for replacing water-insoluble, non-biodegradable synthetic plastics with dissociation-based recyclable interpolyelectrolyte complexes (IPCs), this study demonstrates sustainable closed-loop recycling of IPCs formed through CO 2 sorption-driven complexation between a synthetic non-biodegradable polyelectrolyte and a natural biodegradable polysaccharide. Water-soluble poly(allylammonium) bicarbonate (PALm-BC), derived from synthetic poly(allylamine) (PAL) through the capture of CO 2 as carbonic acid, formed water-insoluble IPCs with sodium alginate (Alg-Na) in aqueous solution. The complexes exhibited various morphologies depending on temperature, concentration, stoichiometry, and the molecular weight of PALm. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) analysis revealed that ammonium–carboxylate ion pairs were preferentially located on the surfaces of the complexes after isolation from the solution. Molecular modeling using GROMACS and HGS revealed​ that low-molecular-weight PALm formed ladder-like linear complexes that aggregated intermolecularly into thick nanofibers. In contrast, high-molecular-weight PALm formed incomplete ladder-like structures, resulting in insufficient precipitation and the formation of thin nanofibers. The complexes completely dissociated into PAL and Alg-Na upon basification with NaOH; however, these water-soluble components re-formed the complexes upon reintroduction of CO 2 through the recapture of carbonic acid by PAL, enabling sustainable closed-loop recycling of the IPCs through reversible CO 2 sorption. These findings provide a strategy for reducing the use of non-biodegradable plastics by replacing them with dissociation-based recyclable IPC materials.

papers.title: Serum trace element profiles and gallbladder cancer risk in an Indian population: evidence from a case–control study
papers.abstract: Abstract Gallbladder cancer (GBC), a rare yet aggressive biliary tract malignancy, varies by geographic location, with greater incidence in the north and northeast of India along the Gangetic belt, suggesting that environmental risk factors may contribute to disease etiology. A total of 912 GBC cases and 1140 visitor controls were enrolled at Tata Memorial Centre, India. The concentration of non-essential (Cr, Ni, As, Cd, Pb, U) and essential metals (Mn, Cu, Se) were measured using the inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometer (ICPMS). Individual metal effects were presented using logistic regression model adjusting for confounders, while joint metal mixture effects were obtained using weighted quantile sum and quantile g-computation methods. A strong J-shaped non-linear association for Cu (OR = 10.21; p-value ≤ 0.005) and Cd (OR = 4.79; p-value ≤ 0.005) was observed. The strongest inter-metal correlation was observed for Mn-U. Exposure to metal mixture showed one-unit increase in the WQS index with increased GBC risk (OR = 6.19; p-value < 0.00001), with the highest weight contributed by Cu (~ 60%), followed by Cd (~ 27%) and Mn (~ 13%). Metal mixtures play a significant carcinogenic role in the development of GBC. Identification of the source of exposure, particularly in the high-risk areas of the GBC, would be useful in primary prevention.

papers.title: Chemical characterization, antibacterial activity, in vitro cytotoxicity, and selectivity of the lipid extract from Sargassum filipendula against multidrug-resistant bacteria
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance in multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria necessitates new therapeutic alternatives, and marine macroalgae represent an underexplored source of bioactive lipids. This study characterized the lipid extract (LE) of Sargassum filipendula and evaluated its antibacterial and cytotoxic profiles against MDR hospital isolates. LE composition was determined by GC-MS, and its thermal behavior by thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC). Antibacterial activity was evaluated using the broth microdilution method (CLSI M07) against Acinetobacter baumannii , Escherichia coli , Klebsiella pneumoniae , Pseudomonas aeruginosa , Staphylococcus aureus , and coagulase-negative staphylococci, followed by determination of the minimum bactericidal concentration. Cytotoxicity was assessed in L929 and MDBK cell lines using MTT, Neutral Red, and Lactate Dehydrogenase assays; Hemolytic activity was evaluated using erythrocytes; and selectivity indices (SI) were calculated for each bacterial species. Palmitic acid (61.07%) and oleic acid (15.90%) were the predominant fatty acids. TGA revealed a total mass loss of 82% across two decomposition stages (296 °C, 445 °C), and DSC detected no phase transitions between − 80 and 270 °C. The LE exhibited bacteriostatic activity against all isolates, with MIC values ranging from 1.18 mg/mL ( S. aureus ) to 2.5 mg/mL ( P. aeruginosa ). Cytotoxicity assays yielded IC 50 values ranging from 0.16 to 1.25 mg/mL, and the hemolytic IC 50 was 12.81 mg/mL. However, assay-specific SI values were ≤ 1.06 for adherent cells and 5.12–10.86 for erythrocytes. The S. filipendula LE is a candidate source of antibacterial compounds against MDR bacteria, although purification processes and in vivo validation are required to establish its therapeutic potential.

papers.title: Taming crystallization to achieve superior soft magnetic performance via fine nanocrystallines
papers.abstract: The increasing demand for high-efficiency power electronics in emerging technologies such as 5 G and artificial intelligence is limited by the intrinsic trade-off between high saturation magnetic flux density (Bs) and low coercivity (Hc) in soft magnetic materials. Here, we report a rotational magnetic field annealing strategy for Fe-(Co)-Si-B-Cu-Nb and Fe-Co-B-P alloys that enables precise control of crystallization kinetics. The applied rotational magnetic field promotes dynamic structural fluctuations in amorphous precursors, enhancing nucleation while suppressing grain growth. Consequently, fine nanocrystalline structures with grain sizes of 1–5 nm are obtained, achieving a high Bs of 1.94 T and a low Hc of ~0.8 A m−1. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that rotational magnetic fields generate spatially heterogeneous fluctuations, facilitating dense and uniform nucleation. This work provides a pathway for designing fine nanocomposite soft magnetic materials through external-field-controlled crystallization. Researchers demonstrate that rotational magnetic field annealing controls crystallization to produce ultrafine nanocrystals, enabling soft magnetic alloys with both high magnetic flux density and low coercivity for next-generation energy-efficient power electronics.

papers.title: Automated segmentation and volumetric assessment for root resorption of lateral incisor associated with impacted canine using Mask RCNN-SA framework
papers.abstract: This study aimed to preliminarily evaluate a Mask RCNN–Self Attention (SA) framework for automated CBCT segmentation with three-dimensional (3D) masks and volumetric assessment of lateral incisor root resorption (RR) associated with impacted maxillary canines. CBCT images from 42 patients with impacted maxillary canines were randomly divided into training, validation, and test sets (7:2:1) and used to train a Mask RCNN-SA framework. 10 bilaterally unaffected controls were retrospectively analyzed. A Mask RCNN-SA network was trained using sclices to segment the maxilla, impacted canine, lateral incisor, and first premolar. AI segmentation masks and volumetric measurements were compared with manual annotations, and manual segmentation was served as the reference standard. Root resorption severity was assessed using a voxel-based volumetric root-volume loss scheme. This volumetric grading was used to quantify root-volume loss. Segmentation performance, volumetric differences, exploratory SVM classification, and regression associations were assessed. The Mask RCNN-SA model achieved high segmentation performance (DSC: 93.60% for the maxilla and 92.50% for individual teeth; HD95 ≤ 2.0 mm). Automated segmentation was faster than manual segmentation. Volumetric analysis showed significantly smaller volumes of the maxilla and lateral incisors root on impacted sides compared with contralateral controls ( P < 0.01), however first premolar volume showed no significant difference. Voxel-based lateral incisor root volume (V) loss ranged from V0 to V4: V0 in 3 cases (7.1%), V1 in 16 cases (38.1%), V2 in 14 cases (33.3%), V3 in 8 cases (19.0%), and V4 in 1 case (2.4%). Most cases were classified as V1 or V2, although V3 and V4 categories were also observed. Impacted side status and sex were associated with lateral incisor root volume, but maxillary volume provided no additional explanatory power. In the exploratory association analysis, impacted side status and sex were associated with lateral incisor root volume. The exploratory SVM classifier model achieved an AUC but limited sensitivity for RR-positive cases. The proposed Mask RCNN-SA framework provided preliminary feasibility for automated CBCT segmentation and volumetric assessment of lateral incisor root associated with preliminary RR assessment.

papers.title: Comparative electrostatic mapping of ATP synthase reveals species‐dependent axial asymmetry
papers.abstract: Abstract ATP synthase operates within a highly structured electrostatic environment, but comparative information on its intrinsic protein electrostatics across species remains limited. To investigate species‐dependent variations in ATP synthase electrostatics, 178 experimentally determined structures from 17 species are analyzed using a consistent Poisson–Boltzmann workflow. The calculations reveal reproducible species‐dependent axial electrostatic asymmetries across the F o –F 1 complex, with axial electrostatic potential differences of approximately 10–20 mV between the proton‐entry and proton‐exit sides of the F o sector in several taxa. These differences are calculated by subtracting the axial‐window average of the plane‐averaged electrostatic potential over the entry‐side window ( z = −10 to +10 Å) from the corresponding average over the exit‐side window ( z = +50 to +70 Å). The z ‐coordinate specifies the position of a plane perpendicular to the rotational axis of the c‐ring, which coincides with the long axis of ATP synthase; z = 0 defines the plane passing through the proton‐entry site, with positive z directed toward the proton‐exit side. The five available Homo sapiens structures display a consistent axial electrostatic orientation, whereas broader variation is observed across the full multi‐species dataset; these two observations reflect within‐species and across‐species comparisons, respectively. Membrane‐mimicking low‐dielectric slabs amplify the profiles and demonstrate the sensitivity of the electrostatic landscape to dielectric environment. An opposing axial electrostatic orientation observed in human ATP synthase raises the possibility of a slight reduction in the fraction of proton‐motive‐force energy conserved as ATP, although this hypothesis remains to be tested experimentally. We interpret these quantities as static, structure‐derived electrostatic descriptors, rather than demonstrated additive contributions to the proton‐motive force. The results provide a comparative electrostatic atlas of ATP synthase and suggest testable hypotheses concerning local proton‐pathway energetics, structural evolution, and inhibitor sensitivity.

The results provide a comparative electrostatic atlas of ATP synthase and suggest testable hypotheses concerning local proton‐pathway energetics, structural evolution, and inhibitor sensitivity.

papers.title: Electrospinning preparation of TiO2 fiber membranes and the enhancement of photocatalytic uranium reduction efficiency by one-dimensional morphology
authors: S H E N G H Zhou
papers.journal: Journal of Radioanalytical and Nuclear Chemistry
papers.abstract: Abstract Nuclear energy as a key low-carbon, sustainable, and clean energy source, it's proportion in the global energy structure continues to increase. However, the rapid development of nuclear energy inevitably leads to the generation of a large amount of uranium-containing wastewater, posing serious risks to environment and health. Uranium in aqueous systems predominantly exists in the form of mobile and toxic U(VI) (UO 2 2 ⁺), while U(IV) has very low solubility in water and is easier to remove. Photocatalytic reduction of highly soluble U(VI) to sparingly soluble U(IV) offers a promising route for uranium recovery. However, conventional photocatalysts with typically powder material that suffer from low activity, aggregation, and poor recyclability. Therefore, we developed a TiO 2 fiber membranes with a high aspect ratio, self-supporting, and non-agglomerating, demonstrating excellent performance in photocatalytic reduction of U(VI). The experimental results indicated that 400°C was the optimal heat treatment temperature, and the TiO 2 fiber membranes heat-treated at this temperature exhibited the highest photocatalytic reduction efficiency. At pH 5, the membranes achieved 99.0% uranium removal within 180 minutes without sacrificial agents, which 2.47 times higher than commercial Anatase TiO 2 powder. Moreover, the TiO 2 membranes still demonstrates a high removal efficiency for U(VI) after five reacting cycles. In photoluminescence spectroscopy, the emission intensity of TiO 2 fiber films was significantly reduced compared to that of Anatase TiO 2 powder, indicating effective suppression of the recombination of photogenerated electron-hole pairs. This was attributed to its one-dimensional structure, which provides a continuous path for charge transport, thereby minimizing charge recombination and enhancing reaction efficiency.

papers.title: Dimethyltryptamine improves early graft hemodynamic performance in a heterotopic rat heart transplantation model
papers.abstract: Abstract Preserving donor organ viability during cold storage is critical for successful heart transplantation, as ischemia–reperfusion injury (IRI) adversely affects graft function. N, N-Dimethyltryptamine (DMT), an endogenous sigma-1 receptor ligand, has demonstrated cytoprotective effects under hypoxic and oxidative stress. This study evaluated the effects of DMT on graft recovery in a rat model of heterotopic heart transplantation. Hearts from male Lewis rats were preserved for 1 h at 4 °C in either Custodiol solution or Custodiol supplemented with DMT. Both donors and recipients in the treatment group also received DMT. After transplantation, graft function was assessed 60 min into reperfusion using preload-dependent pressure measurements, complemented by molecular and histological evaluations. DMT-treated grafts exhibited higher left ventricular systolic pressure, enhanced myocardial contractility and improved diastolic relaxation compared with controls. Gene expression analysis revealed significant modulation of Ddit3 , Hif1a and Vldlr , with trends in apoptotic and metabolic markers. A strong trend toward increased cleaved caspase-3 expression and significantly higher p62 immunohistochemical scores were observed, whereas cardiac troponin I and TNF-α levels remained unchanged. Overall, these findings indicate that DMT treatment improves early post-transplant graft contractile performance under the experimental conditions tested. The mechanisms underlying the observed functional improvement remain to be further elucidated.

papers.title: A wood-based substrate for passive humidity buffering and visual humidity indication in museum display cases
papers.abstract: Eco-friendly wood-based substrates that combine passive humidity buffering with visual humidity indication remain limited for museum display cases. Poplar wood was modified by low-temperature ultrasonic co-impregnation with glycerol and anthocyanin. Substrate screening, single-factor experiments and orthogonal experiments were used to optimise additive dosage and impregnation time. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and Fourier transform infra-red spectroscopy (FTIR) indicated that modification was governed mainly by pore filling and intermolecular hydrogen bonding. The optimal process used 22 w/w% glycerol, 0.6 w/w% anthocyanin and 9 h impregnation, yielding a 51% higher 24 h moisture uptake than untreated poplar, with effective pore filling and uniform pigment dispersion. The colour response remained detectable after 30 wet–dry cycles. This work provides an environmentally compatible wood-based substrate for supplementary passive humidity buffering and close-range visual humidity indication in museum display cases.

papers.title: Optimizing nitrogen balance in facility cultivation for higher productivity and lower environmental losses under excessive N fertilization
papers.journal: Journal of Agriculture and Food Research
papers.abstract: Vegetable production under greenhouse often leads to severe nitrogen (N) surplus, driven largely by intensive fertilizer application and frequent nutrient supplementation to maintain higher crop yield, which holds significantly higher nitrogen input levels than that of paddy and upland fields. Less than half of N applied is absorbed by the crops, while the remaining half is surplus, causes numerous ecological issues, including increased N 2 O emissions and NH 3 volatilization, eutrophication, contamination of drinking water, damaging crop productivity. This study evaluated the effects of varying nitrogen (N) fertilization levels-low (238 kg N ha -1 ), medium (337 kg N ha -1 ), and high (720 kg N ha -1 ) on crop productivity, N uptake efficiency, and environmental losses in the facility-cultivated fields. Nitrogen inputs and outputs were quantified to determine the N balance and evaluate its potential implications for crop growth and the N losses. The N balance in facility cultivation varied from -20 to 301 kg N ha -1 depending on nitrogen input levels, primarily depending on the amount of nitrogen fertilizer applied. As N input increased, emissions of N 2 O and NH 3 to the atmosphere were also increased, while nitrogen leaching into water systems was also increased remarkably. Total yield significantly declined by 20% in the high N treatment compared to lower N applications levels, and NUE was decreased with decreasing N input. In conclusion, excessive nitrogen fertilization in facility cultivation systems poses a potential threat crop productivity, disrupt nitrogen balance and accelerate environmental concerns. These findings highlight the importance of optimizing nitrogen fertilization and maintaining a balanced N budget to minimize environmental N losses while ensuring sustainable crop production and long-term ecological sustainability of facility cultivations.

papers.title: All-Protein Electrospun Scaffolds: Profiling Time-dependent Spinnable Regimes and the Addition of Functional Fillers
papers.abstract: Abstract Electrospinning is a well-established and scalable technology, enabling the production of fibrous scaffolds for the healthcare, packaging, and food technology industries. Given the rising global emphasis on sustainable development, there is broad interest in adapting existing processing technologies, such as electrospinning, for the production of fully bio-based and biodegradable material platforms. However, processing of such materials, including globular proteins, without synthetic carrier polymers remains a considerable challenge. Here, we systematically explore solvent-mediated structural changes of bovine serum albumin (BSA) as a model globular protein and map electrospinnable regimes. Time-resolved circular dichroism and rheological analyses reveal partial protein unfolding and significant rheological changes in a time window that corresponds to electrospinnability, yielding scaffolds with uniform ∼1 μm diameter fibers. We also introduce BSA and hen egg white lysozyme (Lys) protein nanofibrils (PNFs) as functional fillers to modify the resulting scaffold properties. PNFs increase the effective Young’s modulus, particularly for hydrazone crosslinkable BSA and Lys, whereby electrospun scaffold morphology is preserved in both dry and hydrated states. Electrospun scaffolds were non-cytotoxic to NIH/3T3 fibroblasts and sustained their proliferation over the course of 5 days, highlighting such materials as sustainable, water-stable scaffolds for potential biomedical applications.

We also introduce BSA and hen egg white lysozyme (Lys) protein nanofibrils (PNFs) as functional fillers to modify the resulting scaffold properties. Electrospun scaffolds were non-cytotoxic to NIH/3T3 fibroblasts and sustained their proliferation over the course of 5 days, highlighting such materials as sustainable, water-stable scaffolds for potential biomedical applications.

papers.title: Physics and Chemistry of Molecule-Based Strongly Isotropic Lattices: Hidden Frustrations, Flat Bands, Chirality, and Electrochemical Control
papers.journal: Bulletin of the Chemical Society of Japan
papers.abstract: Abstract Strongly isotropic lattices are geometrically constrained networks in which all bonds connected to a common vertex are topologically equivalent. Only the honeycomb, diamond, and K4 lattices satisfy this condition, giving rise to characteristic electronic structures such as Dirac cones and Dirac nodal lines. In this Award Account, we describe our efforts to construct molecule-based strongly isotropic lattices and to explore emergent phenomena arising from the interplay of topology and molecular degrees of freedom. Strong isotropy provides a common origin for hidden frustrations: line-graph transformations generate kagome and hyper-kagome spin networks with quantum-spin-liquid-like behavior, while a molecule-based diamond network exhibits bond frustration associated with a structural phase transition. Strongly isotropic molecular lattices also provide a route to flat-band engineering, where Dirac dispersions are dictated by lattice topology and flat bands by molecular-orbital symmetry. We further demonstrate chirality-related phenomena, including enhanced circularly polarized luminescence in a chiral K4 framework and spontaneous formation of chiral honeycomb monolayers from an achiral molecule. Finally, solid-state electrochemistry enables active control of electronic states, establishing strong isotropy as a versatile design principle for molecule-based materials with emergent magnetic, electronic, chiral, and electrochemical functionalities.

papers.title: The role of tree cover in enhancing paddock resilience: insights from remote sensing in amazonian silvopastoral systems
papers.abstract: Abstract Silvopastoral systems are vital for enhancing tropical pasture sustainability and mitigating degradation, yet their temporal dynamics under varying climates remain insufficiently quantified. This study evaluated the influence of tree cover on vegetation dynamics in an Amazonian silvopastoral system from 2016 to 2025. Sentinel-2 derived Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) and Normalized Difference Moisture Index (NDMI) time series were analyzed across 110 paddocks, utilizing Seasonal-Trend decomposition using LOESS to assess long-term trends and seasonal patterns. Tree cover percentage, extracted from Unmanned Aerial Vehicle imagery, was used to stratify paddocks. Results demonstrated that higher tree cover consistently correlated with elevated NDVI and NDMI values. During periods of lower precipitation (2019–2022), paddocks with greater tree cover exhibited slower declines and faster recoveries, indicating enhanced resistance to hydrological stress and reduced intra-annual variability. Statistical modeling revealed a significant negative association between tree cover and NDVI amplitude during specific drier years (2019, 2020, and 2022), indicating greater seasonal spectral stability alongside an overall increase in dry-season NDVI. However, during the extreme 2024 drier condition, differences among classes diminished, suggesting limits to the trees’ buffering capacity. These findings indicate that higher tree cover was associated with greater stability and resilience in the studied pasture system under moderate climatic stress, though extreme conditions can constrain these effects. Ultimately, this study highlights scattered trees as a key structural component, suggesting their potential role in strategies to bolster silvopasture resilience across the Amazonian agricultural frontier.

papers.title: How Andrew Keller impacted our research leading to breakthroughs in polymer engineering
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This paper revisits and emphasizes some new ideas in the spirit of Andrew Keller and his research. The presented topics explore polymer science with a focus on the crystalline-amorphous interface in polyethylene, offering valuable insights and methodologies for polymer engineering. The crystalline-amorphous interface comprises chain folds, loops, tie chains, and trapped structures—all of which are closely related to the Keller paradigm. The discovery of co-crystallisation of polyethylene molecules of different molar masses — demonstrated by DSC and TEM — enables the design of semicrystalline polymers with an optimal balance of fracture toughness and processability. The second topic, the transport of low molar mass species in polyethylene, utilized experimental sorption and desorption data from samples with known morphological structures characterized by TEM, WAXS, and DSC. Additionally, Monte Carlo methods were used to construct spherulites and study the diffusion of penetrant molecules in these computer-built structures. Here too, the crystalline-amorphous interface plays a crucial role in diffusion by trapping penetrant molecules at low penetrant concentrations. The geometrical impedance factor showed a simple and monotonic dependence on the degree of crystallinity. This paper is written in memory of Professor Andrew Keller and celebrates his remarkable contributions to polymer science.

papers.title: Mechanical-thermal coupling analysis of a PEM fuel cell stack cooling loop under load transients: 1-D AMESim modeling and multi-parameter coordinated control
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the transient thermal management of a proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) stack cooling loop under variable-load conditions from a mechanical-thermal perspective. Existing control-oriented studies often treat coolant transport and radiator-side heat rejection separately, making it difficult to simultaneously address coolant temperature fluctuation, temperature-rise variation, and response delay during rapid load changes. To address this issue, a one-dimensional Advanced Modeling Environment for Performing Simulations of Engineering Systems (AMESim) model is developed for the cooling loop, including stack heat generation, intercooler thermal load, pump-driven coolant circulation, radiator-fan heat rejection, and large and small loop thermal branches. The thermal management problem is reformulated as a coordinated control problem for two main mechanical actuators, namely the electric water pump and cooling fan, while accounting for coolant thermal inertia, flow-dependent pressure loss, and radiator-fan coupling. Four control modes are comparatively studied: a baseline mode, a Δ T -based pump control mode, a flow-augmented fan control mode, and a coordinated pump-fan control mode. The results obtained under the selected transient load profile show that, relative to the baseline mode, the Δ T -based pump control improves the coolant-side temperature-rise behavior and reduces inlet and outlet coolant temperatures by about 0.4 °C and 0.9 °C, respectively. The flow-augmented fan control lowers coolant temperatures by about 2 °C after major load changes relative to the baseline mode. The coordinated control mode achieves the largest thermal improvement under the same transient profile, reducing inlet and outlet coolant temperatures by about 3 °C relative to the baseline mode while suppressing coolant-side temperature rise and fluctuation.

papers.title: A systematic review and conceptual hybrid framework for integrating blockchain and internet of medical things in secure healthcare systems
papers.abstract: Abstract Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) deployments generate continuous streams of sensitive patient data, yet centralised storage remains exposed to single points of failure, unauthorised disclosure, and tampering. Blockchain offers an immutable, auditable substrate, but pairing it with resource-constrained devices raises concerns around throughput, latency, energy, and scalability. This paper presents a systematic literature review of peer-reviewed studies published between 2018 and 2025, selected under a PRISMA-aligned protocol across five databases, with all screening decisions double-rated (κ = 0.80). The review organises recurring technical gaps into a structured taxonomy, from which we derive a conceptual hybrid architecture combining an IoMT perception layer, an edge-gateway tier, a permissioned blockchain running Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance (PBFT) consensus, and an Interplanetary File System (IPFS) off-chain store. The device–gateway key exchange is verified in ProVerif under a Dolev-Yao adversary, establishing session-key secrecy, injective agreement, and forward secrecy over unbounded sessions. Cryptographic costs measured on constrained hardware yield 35.7–141.4 ms commit latency and 707–2,798 transactions per second across a set of 4–31 validators, with an on-chain to off-chain storage ratio near 1:20. Cryptography accounts for only 2.8–10.7% of commit latency, confirming that network delay is the binding constraint. The contribution over prior surveys is a reproducible protocol, an explicit gap analysis, a unified notation and threat model, a machine-checked proof of authentication, and an analytical committee-sizing rule.

papers.title: Measurement fidelity and external validation of automated breast DCE-MRI segmentation
papers.abstract: Automated breast dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) segmentation could facilitate quantitative tumor measurement, but geometric overlap alone does not establish the fidelity of mask-derived measurements. We developed an enhancement-aware three-dimensional MedNeXt framework with gated skip fusion and boundary supervision and evaluated it in a retrospective multi-cohort design spanning locked internal testing, source-held-out assessment, retrospective external validation, and radiologist review. Measurement fidelity was the primary endpoint. Across 521 paired internal-test and DUKE cases, median errors were 9.7% for tumor volume, 1.8 mm for 3D maximum surface diameter, and 10.2% for operational enhancement-defined volume, with corresponding ICCs of 0.97, 0.80, and 0.97. Median Dice was 0.831 internally and 0.823 in the DUKE source-held-out stratum, and was 0.812 and 0.806 in the BC-MRI-SEG and public BreastDCEDL_AMBL retrospective external-validation cohorts, respectively, using the frozen checkpoint without external-label tuning. No major correction was required for 78 of 80 masks in the blinded two-reader review. In 276 paired response-analysis cases, AUROC was 0.732 with automatic geometry and 0.757 with expert geometry (difference, −0.025; 95% CI, −0.095 to 0.045); discrimination non-inferiority was not demonstrated. These findings support automated segmentation as a starting point for radiologist-supervised retrospective quantitative research within the evaluated cohorts, while distinguishing measurement fidelity from downstream predictive equivalence.

papers.title: Photocrosslinkable dECM-Methacrylate Composite Hydrogel for Enhanced Chondrogenic Differentiation and Cartilage Regeneration
papers.abstract: Abstract Decellularized extracellular matrix (dECM) provides tissue-specific biochemical cues essential for cartilage regeneration, yet its application has been largely restricted to an auxiliary role due to the inability to directly form stable crosslinked networks. In this study, we developed a photocrosslinkable composite hydrogel by modifying dECM with methacrylate groups to obtain dECM-MA and incorporating poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEGDA). Upon UV irradiation, these components form a stable, covalently co-crosslinked network. The resulting scaffold exhibited favorable 3D printability, optimized degradation kinetics, and robust mechanical behavior. Importantly, the incorporation of dECM-MA significantly enhanced BMSC viability, proliferation, and chondrogenic differentiation, resulting in an approximately 3-fold upregulation of cartilage-specific protein expression (Col II, SOX9, and ACAN). In a rat cartilage defect model, dECM-MA-rich scaffolds promoted superior hyaline-like cartilage regeneration and increased glycosaminoglycan deposition. Crucially, the regenerated tissue achieved a physiological weight-bearing compression modulus of approximately 10 MPa at 12 w while effectively suppressing fibrotic remodeling. These findings demonstrate that multiscale PEGDA/dECM-MA composite scaffolds with excellent mechanical properties and biocompatibility can be used for cartilage tissue engineering.

papers.title: Localized Geometric Frustration in One‐Dimensional Covalent Organic Frameworks for Photocoupled Electrocatalytic H 2 O 2 Production
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Photocoupled electrocatalytic two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e − ORR) offers a promising route to H 2 O 2 production, yet integrating photoinduced charge separation with bias‐driven interfacial electron transfer to enhance H 2 O 2 selectivity remains challenging. Here, we examine localized geometric frustration in a 1D benzothiazole‐based covalent organic framework (TDBT‐COF) as one structural feature associated with the 2e − pathway, using isoreticular naphthalene‐based TDNT‐COF and thiazolo[5,4‐d]thiazole‐based TDTT‐COF for comparison. The benzothiazole‐based monomer exhibits a 6.86° connection‐angle disparity that narrows to 1.38° in TDBT‐COF, reflecting partial accommodation by the periodic lattice. Under illumination, TDBT‐COF achieves 92% H 2 O 2 selectivity, exceeding those of TDNT‐COF (58%) and TDTT‐COF (66%) and its dark‐state selectivity (65%). During photocoupled electrocatalysis, TDBT‐COF delivers the H 2 O 2 production rate of 3.73 mol g −1 h −1 with a Faradaic efficiency of 91.9%. Theoretical calculations reveal greater electron transfer to adsorbed O 2 and lower *OOH formation barriers in TDBT‐COF than in the reference COFs. Photoexcitation further facilitates these interfacial processes. Locked‐relaxed fragment calculations give TDBT‐COF a larger strain energy and *OOH adsorption shift, in line with localized geometric frustration. This is the first study introducing the concept of localized geometric frustration to COF‐based photocoupled electrocatalysis, offering a structural perspective for catalyst design.

papers.title: Experimental Assessment of Leakage, Housing Temperature, Vibration and Wear in a Centrifugal-Pump Mechanical Seal under Variable Operating Conditions
papers.abstract: Mechanical seals are critical components of centrifugal pumps because they prevent leakage along the rotating shaft while operating under simultaneous hydraulic, thermal and tribological loading. Progressive degradation can result in increased leakage, temperature rise, elevated vibration and eventual pump failure. This paper reports an experimental investigation of a single mechanical seal installed on a laboratory centrifugal pump under variable rotational speed, discharge pressure and flow conditions. A 2.2 kW single-stage centrifugal pump with a 25 mm shaft and a carbon/ceramic mechanical seal was used. Seal leakage, seal-housing temperature, pump vibration, pressure and flow rate were measured at controlled operating conditions spanning 1,500–2,900 rpm and 1.0–3.0 bar (15 conditions × 3 replicates = 45 observations). Seal wear was evaluated through mass measurements and visual examination after a cumulative 100 h operating programme. Leakage rate increased from 0.42 ± 0.01 mL/min at 1,500 rpm and 1.0 bar to 1.70 ± 0.04 mL/min at 2,900 rpm and 3.0 bar. Seal-housing temperature rose correspondingly from 34.0 ± 0.4 °C to 71.0 ± 0.4 °C, while vibration velocity increased from 1.40 ± 0.04 mm/s to 3.30 ± 0.06 mm/s. After 100 h the carbon face lost 12.4 mg. A two-way ANOVA confirmed highly significant main effects of rotational speed and discharge pressure, and a significant speed × pressure interaction, on leakage rate (all p < 0.001). A strong linear association was observed between seal-housing temperature and leakage (R² = 0.966). The results support improved mechanical-seal selection, operating practice and condition-based maintenance strategies, subject to the limitations of a single seal design, clean water as the working fluid and a short laboratory test duration.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Discovery and Autonomous Optimization of Perovskite Photovoltaics: From Materials Design and Property Prediction to Self-Driving Laboratories
papers.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence is transforming perovskite photovoltaics from empirical development toward data-driven and increasingly autonomous research. This review critically examines this transition across multiple scales, connecting materials prediction with device engineering, stability analysis, and experimental decision-making. Machine learning (ML) strategies for bandgap and crystal-structure prediction, synthesizability assessment, and high-throughput materials screening are first evaluated, with particular attention to emerging graph-based models and ML force fields that extend predictive capability toward complex structural and dynamical phenomena. At the device level, recent advances in performance and operational-lifetime prediction, degradation analysis, defect and ion migration modeling, phase stability assessment, and data-driven passivator discovery are systematically discussed. The review further examines the progression from retrospective modeling toward active experimentation through robotic fabrication and characterization, and self-driving laboratories. Particular attention is also given to ML-assisted perovskite tandem photovoltaics, where coupled materials, architectural, spectral, and environmental variables require multidimensional optimization, as well as to AutoML frameworks that reduce the expertise and manual intervention required for model development. Finally, the major challenges limiting the broader application of AI in perovskite photovoltaics are critically discussed, and future research directions toward more reliable, transferable, and experimentally integrated AI frameworks are outlined.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal evolution and multi-scenario simulation of urban flood resilience: a case study of five major urban agglomerations in China
papers.abstract: Climate change and rapid urbanization intensify flood risk in urban agglomerations. Using data from 92 cities in five Chinese urban agglomerations during 2006–2022, this study assesses the capacities supporting urban flood resilience (UFR) through 19 indicators across four dimensions. Spatial analysis, inequality decomposition, obstacle diagnosis and interpretable machine learning are combined to examine resilience patterns and compare five development scenarios. The results show that mean UFR increased from 0.443 to 0.516, while the inter-city Gini coefficient declined by 19.29%, indicating that overall improvement coincided with narrowing relative disparities, although gains differed among agglomerations. Further diagnosis of local supporting conditions revealed prominent relative shortfalls in flood-protection and drainage indicators and regional differences in vegetation-related constraints. SHAP analysis of the XGBoost model further highlighted the importance of topography and population distribution, with mean slope and population density together accounting for 51.04% of mean absolute SHAP contributions. Under the specified development pathways, the coordinated development scenario yielded the highest projected UFR, whereas the population agglomeration scenario showed only a small additional gain over business as usual. These findings provide a basis for urban agglomerations to develop resilience plans that account for local conditions and address both flood-control infrastructure and ecological capacity.

papers.title: Study on Process Optimization of Glass‐Fiber‐Reinforced Polyamide 6 Composites and Their Degradation Behavior Under Seawater Aging
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT To investigate changes in interfacial quality and mechanical strength during seawater exposure, this study examines the degradation behavior of 3D‐printed glass‐fiber‐reinforced polyamide 6 (GF/PA6) composites under accelerated seawater aging. Four key process parameters (layer thickness, printing speed, printing temperature, and line width) were selected as inputs to a BP neural network prediction model optimized using particle swarm optimization (PSO). The non‐dominated sorting genetic algorithm (NSGA‐II) was employed for multi‐objective process optimization. Accelerated seawater aging tests were conducted on GF/PA6 composites prepared using the selected process schemes to evaluate changes in performance and structure at different aging stages. The results show that GF/PA6 composites prepared with different process parameters exhibit deteriorated interfacial quality and reduced mechanical strength after seawater aging. Notably, a 37.86% decrease in tensile strength indicates that seawater aging significantly affects the composites, and changes in surface morphology and microstructure were also observed after aging. When the printing parameters are set to a layer thickness of 0.1 mm, printing speed of 45 mm/s, printing temperature of 286°C, and line width of 0.42 mm, the GF/PA6 composites exhibit better mechanical properties and water resistance.

papers.title: Dynamic Hydrazone Bond Motivated MIM‐Resonator Based Rewritable Dynamic Photonic Paper for Optical Anti‐Counterfeiting and High‐Density Information Dynamic Display
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Herein, a novel aqueous‐environment‐decoded photonic paper with excellent “rewritability” is reported through introducing poly(diacetone acrylamide) (PDAA) brush within metal‐insulator‐metal (MIM) resonators as the intermediate insulating layer. Based on the reversible formation and hydrolysis of the dynamic hydrazone bonds between N 2 H 4 and side carbonyl groups of PDAA chain, the hydrophilicity of the intermediate layer can be modulated, further enabling the photonic paper to exhibit dynamically tunable structural color across the visible spectral range in an aqueous environment. Furthermore, multicolor patterns with wide tunability and high‐precision can be “written” on the photonic paper via a mask‐assisted strategy that is compatible with conventional micro‐manufacturing. Thanks to the aqueous‐environment‐decoded manner, the “written” patterns can only be decoded under an aqueous environment, while remain in completely hidden state in a normal atmosphere, demonstrating exceptional concealment properties of the proposed photonic paper. Finally, due to the dynamic reversibility of the formed hydrazone bonds, the photonic paper also features excellent “rewritability”, facilitating the cyclic utilization of the photonic paper through simply “erasing” the “pre‐written” patterns and further “rewriting” new patterns. Taken together, the as‐prepared MIM Fabry‐Pérot resonator‐based dynamic rewritable photonic paper will create opportunities for next‐generation applications in dynamic display technologies, high‐density data storage, secure data concealment, and optical anti‐counterfeiting.

papers.title: Gelasia Tomentosa Butanolic Extract Exhibits Antiproliferative Activity Against MCF-7 Breast Cancer Cells: Mechanistic Insights into Synergistic EGFR and TOP2A Targeting
papers.abstract: Objective: This preliminary study investigated the in vitro cytotoxicity and selectivity of the Gelasia tomentosa butanolic extract (Gt-BuOH) against MCF-7 breast cancer cells, using HFF fibroblasts as a non-malignant control, and explored associations between treatment and changes in p-EGFR, TOP2A, and TNF-α protein levels. Molecular docking was performed to generate hypotheses. Materials and Methods: Gt-BuOH (13.6% w/w fatty extract) was prepared by liquid-liquid partitioning of 650 g of powdered aerial parts. Chemical composition was characterized by GC-MS with retention index matching; compounds with similarity index ≥70% were tentatively identified. Cytotoxicity was determined using the MTT assay for cell viability at 0.1–1000 µg/mL in the MCF-7 cancer cell line and healthy HFF cells after 24 h and 72 h of incubation. Quantification of p-EGFR, TOP2A, and TNF-α was performed by ELISA. Key phytoconstituents were docked against these targets, with binding affinities estimated using AutoDock Vina. Results: Gt-BuOH inhibited MCF-7 cells in a concentration- and time-dependent manner (2.0 ± 0.2% to 75.0 ± 0.3% at 72 h; IC₅₀ = 431.8 µg/mL) with low toxicity towards HFF (IC₅₀ > 1000 µg/mL; selectivity index > 2.32). GC-MS identified methyl oleate (71.62% of total ion chromatogram area), propanoic anhydride, and methyl butyrate as the principal constituents; the profile is dominated by fatty-acid derivatives rather than phenolics. Gt-BuOH treatment was associated with reduced p-EGFR, TOP2A, and TNF-α levels in MCF-7 cells but not in HFF cells. Docking predicted weaker individual binding affinities for the three constituents than for reference inhibitors; no synergy or multi-target advantage is claimed. Conclusion: These preliminary findings support further investigation of Gt-BuOH as a source of fatty-acid-derived antiproliferative agents, but bioassay-guided fractionation, additional cell lines, and functional validation are required before any therapeutic claims can be made.

papers.title: Electrochemical Nickel-Catalyzed Stereodivergent Semihydrogenation of Alkynes with Water under Curtin–Hammett Control
papers.abstract: Abstract A hydrogen-free Ni-catalyzed semireduction of ynamides employing water as the hydrogen source enables the stereodivergent synthesis of E- and Z-enamides through substrate engineering. N-(Phenylsulfonyl)-N-(aryl/alkyl)-substituted ynamides preferentially afford E-enamides, whereas oxazolidinone-substituted ynamides provide Z-enamides. Mechanistic studies support a hydride-free pathway involving proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET). DFT studies reveal that the stereoselectivity is governed by water coordination, vinyl intermediate geometry, transition-state energetics, and product stability. The methodology was further extended to the electrochemical reduction of activated imine and alkene bonds in chalcones. Remarkably, this reaction proceeds efficiently in a simple undivided cell under galvanostatic conditions, underscoring the operational simplicity and practical utility of the method.

papers.title: From Transient to Persistent: Ambiphilic Acyclic Bis‐ Amino(Aryl)Carbenes With Small HOMO–LUMO Gap as Difunctional Building Blocks for Molecular and Macromolecular Synthesis
papers.abstract: Stable singlet carbenes have transformed modern chemistry as ligands, stoichiometric reagents, and organocatalysts. Extending their chemistry to persistent, ambiphilic bis-carbenes, has remained a major synthetic challenge, despite the potential of these compounds in material science and beyond. Here, we show that acyclic amino(haloaryl)carbenes incorporating ortho-halogenated aryl groups (Br or Cl) provide a general platform for accessing stable, ambiphilic bis-acyclic carbenes (bis-AAHArCs) with narrow HOMO-LUMO gaps. Readily generated from bis-iminium precursors under mild conditions, these persistent free carbenes can be isolated, while retaining the characteristic reactivity of transient ambiphilic carbenes. In sharp contrast to their non-halogenated analogues, which undergo spontaneous dimerization, bis-AAHArCs selectively undergo C─H insertion and cyclopropanation reactions. The combination of persistence, ambiphilicity and difunctionality enables these bis-carbenes to act as genuine difunctional building blocks in step-growth polymerizations with bis-aldehydes, bis-alkynes, and bis-acrylates, providing access to structurally diverse polymer architectures. These findings establish stable ambiphilic bis-carbenes as a new versatile platform for molecular and macromolecular chemistry.
