papers.title: Dual-Functional Halloysite Nanotube-Derived Cigarette Capsules for Hazard Reduction and Mold Prevention
papers.abstract: Abstract Currently, cigarette-filter modification has predominantly targeted reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging; however, beyond ROS, cigarette smoke contains other hazardous agents such as carbon monoxide (CO), tar, and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), the reduction of which remains largely neglected in current strategies. Herein, we report a novel cigarette-filter capsule, termed Cit-sHNT@Capsule, fabricated by loading the natural flavor citral (Cit) into sulfuric acid-etched halloysite nanotubes and further encapsulating the hybrid within alginate-based hydrogel beads. Incorporating Cit-sHNT@Capsule into cigarette filters moderately reduced CO and tar yields by 9.74% and 13.4%, respectively, while the •OH and •O2– probe assays indicated reductions of approximately 50% and 60%, and fluorescence-based calibration yielded an apparent 57.0% reduction in the PAH-associated measurement, without compromising the moisture and nicotine content during combustion. Thermogravimetric analysis indicated limited mass loss over 70–80 °C, and the capsules retained their structural integrity under the heating conditions, providing preliminary support for their incorporation into cigarette filters. Furthermore, the outstanding antifungal activity of Cit-sHNT@Capsule against Aspergillus niger (nearly 100% inhibition within 45 days) underscored the potential to extend tobacco storage duration and reduce fungal contamination. Collectively, this work highlights the potential of Cit-sHNT@Capsule as a dual-functional additive for cigarette filters, enabling simultaneous hazard reduction and mold prevention.

papers.title: Ordered Atomic Channels Enable Ultrafast Hydrogen Spillover for Hydrogen Evolution at Industrial Current Densities
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT In proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE), facilitating hydrogen spillover via alloy engineering is promising for boosting the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). However, the inhomogeneous electronic structures of conventional alloy electrocatalysts induce heterogeneous energy barriers across catalytic sites, with a subset of sites featuring inordinately high barriers that hamper hydrogen spillover kinetics. Herein, we, for the first time, propose that the ordered atomic channels in the proof‐of‐concept ordered L1 2 ‐Pt 3 Fe/TiO 2 intermetallic catalyst enable ultrafast hydrogen spillover by effectively reducing excessive hydrogen migration barriers, thereby delivering industrial‐level current density. Compared with conventional catalysts, the L1 2 ordered structure renders Pt's electronic environment more uniform, drastically suppressing unfavorable high‐barrier migration pathways and facilitating efficient hydrogen spillover, with the underlying mechanism fully verified by in situ Raman spectroscopy and theoretical simulations. When applied in a practical PEMWE cell, the catalyst prepared via our newly proposed strategy achieves an ultralow cell voltage of 1.63 V at 1.0 A cm −2 , with a record‐breaking stability of over 2000 h maintained at this current density. This work provides a novel design strategy for advanced acidic HER electrocatalysts and offers fundamental insights into atomic‐level regulation of hydrogen spillover processes.

papers.title: Through‐Space Hot‐Electron Transfer Between Gold Nanoclusters and MOF Boosting Photothermal Conversion
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The structural elucidation of metal nanocluster@MOF composites remains challenging due to their poor crystallinity, hindering the establishment of precise structure–property relationships. Here, we present a reverse templating strategy in which atomically precise gold nanoclusters (GNCs) to direct MOF crystallization, yielding highly crystalline GNC@MOF single crystals for single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction (SCXRD) analysis. Coarse‐grained molecular dynamics (CGMD) simulations reveal the adaptive growth of MOFs around spherical GNC template, accompanied by a complete topological transformation from rectangular to hexagonal symmetry. Combining transient absorption spectroscopy, density functional theory (DFT) calculations, and optoelectronic measurements, we reveals pronounced space interfacial electron coupling between GNCs and MOFs. This coupling facilitates directional transfer of photoexcited hot electrons from GNCs to MOFs, resulting in enhanced photothermal conversion performance. Upon 660 nm laser irradiation, Au 13 @Zn‐NDC‐MOF rapidly heats to 106.3°C within 6 s and reaches a maximum temperature of 182.0°C (∆ T = 158.1°C), outperforming discrete Au 13 clusters (∆ T = 126.3°C) under identical conditions. Au 13 @Zn‐NDC‐MOF also exhibits excellent photostability over multiple on‐off cycles. This work establishes a direct link among through‐space interfacial electron coupling, hot‐electron transfer, and enhanced photothermal behavior, providing a generalizable platform for the rational design of high‐performance MNC@MOF materials for solar energy conversion and photocatalysis.

papers.title: Sustainable toughening of epoxy resin with liquefied corn straw: insights into plasticization and compatibility
papers.journal: Journal of Adhesion Science and Technology
papers.abstract: In this study, polyethylene glycol 400 and ethylene glycol were used as the copolymerization liquidation agents, and concentrated sulfuric acid was used as the catalyst. The corn straw (CS) was liquefied at 160 °C under normal pressure. 2-methylimidazole was used as the curing agent to prepare the liquefaction product (LP)/E51 composite material. The structure of the liquefaction product was characterized by Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy and gas chromatography-mass spectrometry coupling, and the scanning electron microscope, differential scanning calorimetry, thermogravimetry and mechanical properties tests were conducted for different epoxy systems. The experimental results showed that adding different proportions of LP to E51 could improve its toughness and strength to varying degrees. When the LP addition amount was 20 wt%, the impact strength of E51 reached the maximum value of 11.14 kJ/m2, which was 499.1% higher than that of pure E51. When the LP addition amount was 15%, the tensile strength (44.61 MPa) was 300.81% higher than that of pure E51 (11.13 MPa), and the bending strength increased from 17.43 MPa (pure E51) to 98.95 MPa. The experimental results indicated that LP was a mixture of different chain-length molecules with terminal hydroxyl groups, which significantly reduced the activation energy required for the curing of the system. The toughness and mechanical strength of E51 were significantly enhanced. It is notable that the glass transition temperature (Tg) determined by DMA decreased from 174 °C to 80 °C, indicating an increase in flexibility; while the initial thermal decomposition temperature (Td5%) determined by TGA slightly decreased.

papers.title: Large-Tiny Spin-Stripe SDW Order in La 3 Ni 2 O 7 via 139 La-NQR Spectroscopy: Reconsideration Based on the Am 2 m Structure
papers.journal: Journal of the Physical Society of Japan
papers.abstract: The lower-symmetry Am2m structure was recently proposed as the intrinsic ambient-pressure phase of La 3 Ni 2 O 7 based on synchrotron x-ray diffraction, whereas earlier studies investigated its properties assuming the commonly accepted Amam structure. Here, we reexamine the crystal structure in La 3 Ni 2 O 7 and the spin configuration of spin-density-wave (SDW) state via 139 La nuclear quadrupole resonance (NQR). The observation of two distinct La(2) sites in the NQR spectra is naturally accounted for by the Am2m structure without any special assumptions, whereas it cannot be reconciled within the Amam framework. Within the Am2m framework, we reanalyze the spin configuration of the SDW phase and identify it as a large-tiny spin-stripe structure, arising naturally from two inequivalent Ni sites with large and tiny magnetic moments. These results establish the itinerant nature of the SDW order at ambient pressure in La 3 Ni 2 O 7 , providing a basis for understanding its relationship to the emergence of high-T c superconductivity under high pressure.

papers.title: The aging human brain exhibits reduced hemodynamic and cerebrospinal fluid flow waves during sleep
papers.abstract: Abstract Aging reduces the quality and quantity of sleep, and sleep disruption is predictive of neurodegeneration and cognitive decline. Sleep loss could affect brain health through disruption of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) circulation, which is important for brain homeostasis. In young adults, large CSF flow waves appear during non-rapid eye movement sleep; however, whether sleep-dependent brain fluid physiology changes in aging is not known. Here we imaged large-scale CSF flow and hemodynamics in young (18–39 years) and older (60–84 years) adults during nighttime sleep. Sleep-dependent CSF flow was reduced in older adults, and was linked to reduced EEG slow wave power, decreased global hemodynamic oscillations and gray matter atrophy. Using sensory and vasoactive stimuli to drive CSF flow, we found that both neural and cerebrovascular changes contributed to this disruption. These results demonstrate reduced CSF flow during sleep in human aging, before disease onset, and identify parallel neural and hemodynamic mechanisms contributing to this decline.

papers.title: Sublevel-selective electron spin hyperpolarization of triplet radical pairs in metal–organic frameworks
papers.abstract: Molecular spin systems are promising platforms for spin-based technologies because their electronic structures can be synthetically tailored and integrated into higher-order assemblies. Photogenerated radical pairs can exhibit spin hyperpolarization under ambient conditions, yet extending such spin dynamics from isolated molecules to structurally organized materials remains challenging. Here, we report a metal–organic framework that regulates the generation of spin-polarized radical pairs within locally well-defined donor–acceptor arrangements. N,N’-di(4-pyridyl)−1,4,5,8-naphthalenetetracarboxdiimide is introduced into a zinc tetrakis(4-carboxyphenyl)porphyrin-based framework. Dense donor–acceptor packing promotes efficient quenching of the porphyrin singlet excited state and selectively forms strongly coupled triplet radical pairs polarized in the zero-spin projection sublevel. These radical pairs exhibit narrow electron paramagnetic resonance signals and long spin-lattice relaxation times. Their spin-lattice relaxation dynamics persist in various guest solvents and vary with guest identity, demonstrating a route to chemically responsive spin materials based on porous, locally organized donor–acceptor frameworks. While molecular spin systems are promising platforms for spin-based technologies, previous studies have mainly focused on isolated molecular systems embedded in dense solid matrices. Here, the authors report a metal-organic framework approach for regulating the generation of spin-polarized radical pairs within a well-defined donor-acceptor arrangement.

papers.title: Late-Stage Fluorosulfurylation Using Sulfuryl Fluoride Bound within a Metal–Organic Framework
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract: Abstract Organic S(VI) fluorides have garnered substantial interest for covalent drug discovery and chemoproteomics due to their ambient stability and unique electrophilic reactivity. Sulfuryl fluoride (SO2F2) is the ideal reagent for the synthesis of various S(VI)–F moieties, yet it is a toxic greenhouse gas, often making it incompatible with laboratory settings. Developing a strategy for handling SO2F2 that is amenable to high-throughput reaction discovery would enhance its utility in the laboratory without necessitating specialized equipment or extensive safety measures. Herein, we report a strategy to safely store reactive SO2F2 within a metal–organic framework (MOF) for its facile application to the synthesis of electrophilic, bioactive molecules. The solid SO2F2–Mg2(dobdc) reagent can be stored for at least five months with minimal gas loss due to the strong yet reversible interaction between SO2F2 and Mg2+ centers in the MOF, as confirmed by single-crystal X-ray diffraction. Using this reagent, we prepare a range of drug-like arylfluorosulfates, primary and secondary acyclic sulfamoyl fluorides, saturated N-heterocyclic sulfamoyl fluorides, and N-heteroarene sulfamoyl fluorides, the last of which cannot be accessed using sulfonium salt alternatives to SO2F2 due to the requirement for strongly basic conditions. These findings represent the first experimental study of SO2F2 adsorption within a MOF and the first use of MOFs for late-stage fluorosulfurylation, paving the way toward a general approach to carefully handling dangerous, reactive gases as solid reagents.

papers.title: Rewiring dendritic cell function with CLEC9A and DEC205 CARs
papers.abstract: Abstract Dendritic cells (DCs) are central orchestrators of anti-tumor immunity, yet their therapeutic utility has been limited by dysfunction and insufficient activation within solid tumors. Here, we report chimeric antigen receptor-engineered DCs (CAR-DCs) that potently prime T cells and reprogram the tumor microenvironment. We identify the intracellular domains of CLEC9A or DEC205 as essential for functional CAR-DC activity, enabling enhanced antigen uptake, cross-presentation, and robust cytokine production that drive strong T cell expansion and effector differentiation. Mechanistically, CARs incorporating CLEC9A or DEC205 intracellular domains triggered SYK phosphorylation and downstream signaling pathways. In both murine and humanized models, CAR-DC therapy suppressed tumor growth and promoted expansion of tumor-reactive T cells. These findings establish CAR-DCs as a scalable and clinically translatable platform for next-generation solid tumor immunotherapy.

papers.title: Inverse Design of Inorganic Compounds with Generative AI
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract: Abstract Machine learning is revolutionizing chemistry. Beyond the value of predictive models accelerating virtual screening, generative AI aims at enabling inverse design, reversing the compound-to-property prediction paradigm into property-to-compound generation. Chemists now have access to a rich AI toolbox for organic chemistry, including drug discovery. However, the application of these methods to inorganic compounds remains limited by the challenges posed by their intrinsic nature. This perspective analyzes how these challenges have been addressed, considering widely diverse systems ranging from molecules to crystals, including transition metal complexes and microporous materials. The analysis focuses on how generative AI methods have evolved toward data-representation-model pipelines that address the full complexity of inorganic compounds, including their chemical composition, geometry, symmetry, and electronic structure. Future directions, like benchmark standardization and the development of synthesizability metrics, are also discussed.

papers.title: Extending reach while maintaining oversight: Clinicians' perspectives on digital mental health implementation in youth services
papers.abstract: Background Digital mental health interventions (DMHIs) offer a promising means of extending care for children and adolescents, yet their integration into routine clinical services remains inconsistent. The implementation conditions clinicians identify as prerequisites for adoption carry greater relevance given the emergence of AI tools now being used by young people. This study examined the perspectives of mental health professionals (MHPs) working with children and young people to identify key implementation considerations for the development and adoption of DMHIs. Methods Nineteen focus groups were conducted with 50 mental health clinicians from a range of service settings in Queensland, Australia between May 2020 and May 2021. Data were analyzed using a mixed deductive-inductive thematic approach informed by the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR). Results MHPs were cautiously optimistic about DMHIs, viewing them as most valuable when implemented as supplementary rather than replacement tools. Key perceived uses included waitlist support, screening and assessment, between-session engagement, and flexible treatment pathways. However, MHPs consistently emphasized the need to preserve clinical judgement and oversight across all stages of DMHI use. Risk management, duty of care, and privacy and confidentiality were identified as critical prerequisites for implementation. Conclusions Successful DMHI implementation in child and adolescent mental health services requires flexible, clinician-centered integration approaches, robust risk management protocols, and clear organizational frameworks delineating clinician responsibility. As AI tools are adopted by young people largely outside clinical oversight, these findings offer a grounded baseline for evaluating what needs to be in place before adoption decisions are made.

papers.title: Development of PEBA-PEMA blend membranes for the pervaporation separation of 1-butanol from aqueous solutions
papers.abstract: Using the Hansen’s solubility parameters (HSPs) approach, novel polyether block amide (PEBA)-polyethyl methacrylate (PEMA) polymer blend membranes were synthesized and applied for the pervaporation (PV) separation of 1-butanol. Blending with PEMA led to an increase in surface roughness and hydrophobicity. PV performance of the blend membranes for the recovery of 1-butanol from aqueous solution (20 g/L) at 40 °C showed an improvement in separation performance with the blending of PEMA; however, a higher blending ratio (≥ 8 wt%) significantly reduced PV performance due to phase separation. The membrane (PBPM-5) containing 5 wt% of PEMA achieved the best PV separation, yielding a flux of 0.19 kgm −2 h − 1 and a separation factor of 15.5, which is a 50% enhancement in flux and a twofold increase in the separation factor as compared to the pristine PEBA membrane. An increase in PV operation temperature and feed butanol content showed simultaneous enhancement in both the separation factor and flux for the PBPM-5 membrane. Separation of butanol from multicomponent mixture resulted in lower performance indicating the presence of strong coupling effect. This work shows the PV butanol separation capability of PEBA can be significantly enhanced through the judicious blending of small amount of PEMA polymer.

papers.title: Machine learning-based experimental access to photon-by-photon arrival times in scintillation detectors
papers.abstract: Abstract Objective . Scintillation detectors with excellent timing resolution enable more precise localization of radiation sources in positron emission tomography, leading to substantial improvements in diagnostic capability for diseases such as cancer and dementia. At the timing precision required for such applications at the picosecond scale, detector performance is governed by the dynamics of scintillation photons generated within the detector and their subsequent detection processes. However, detector signals have conventionally been treated only as collective responses of many photons due to structural constraints inherent to photodetectors. In this study, we overcome this fundamental limitation using deep learning framework. Approach . The proposed method estimates photon-by-photon arrival times directly from detector waveforms without requiring any modification to the detector structure; the method operates on an event-by-event basis without ground-truth labels by integrating an unsupervised learning framework with a physically informed detector-response model. Main results . Through comprehensive validation combining Monte Carlo simulation and experimental measurements across various detector configurations, we experimentally demonstrate improved timing resolution, visualized depth-of-interaction-dependent photon transport, and classified Cherenkov and scintillation photons based on the estimated photon-level timing information using a unified deep learning-based framework. Significance . papers.title: Ultrasonic cryoporometry: determining pore-size distributions from acoustic measurements
papers.abstract: Abstract The standard experimental approaches for determining pore size distribution (PSD) are gas adsorption (e.g., nitrogen porosimetry) and mercury intrusion porosimetry. While widely used, these methods have limitations: gas adsorption experiments often require high-temperature heating and are less sensitive in macropores, whereas mercury intrusion is destructive and involves hazardous materials. Therefore, there is always a demand for alternative methods for characterization of porous materials. Thermodynamics of fluids confined in nanopores depend on the pore size. In particular, both the capillary condensation pressure and the freezing/melting point are shifted relative to their bulk values due to confinement. Capillary condensation is the basis of gas adsorption porosimetry, while the melting/freezing temperature shift can also be used for PSD determination through the Gibbs—Thomson equation, which links the transition temperature to the pore radius. This is the main idea of thermoporometric methods such as differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) based thermoporometry, and nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) cryoporometry. Both techniques, however, typically require complex and costly instrumentation. Ultrasonic measurements provide an alternative route to probe phase transitions in porous materials. In ultrasonic pulse-transmission technique, speed of an ultrasonic wave depends on the density and elastic moduli of the composite system. When a fluid confined within nanopores freezes, the shear modulus of the composite increases, and the difference between the liquid-like and solid-like states reflects the contribution of the confined phase to the overall modulus. In this work, we analyze literature ultrasonic data for fluids (heptane, nonane, argon) confined in nanoporous media using a phenomenological model by Denoyel and Pellenq for phase transitions under confinement. We demonstrate that the temperature-dependent ultrasonic response provides information on the fraction of solidified fluid and, consequently, used to extract the pore size distribution. Our results suggest that ultrasonic data on porous materials can be used for determining PSD, providing an alternative to the methods based on NMR or DSC.

papers.title: Impact of repeated temperature cycling on the low-concentration CO2 adsorption capacity of grafted silica-amine
papers.abstract: Abstract The use of short-chain ethyleneimines (SCEI) and polyethyleneimines (PEI) as CO 2 sorbents has been extensively studied as a potential means of capturing carbon dioxide directly from the atmosphere. Previous work on such sorbents has focused on concentrated sources of CO 2 , such as found in combustion exhaust streams, as well as 400 µLL − 1 CO 2 concentrations more typical of the atmosphere. In this study, we examine changes in the adsorption properties and physical, chemical, and morphological changes induced in grafted SCEI, specifically diethyleneimine and triethyleneimine chains grafted onto two high surface- area silica supports, MCM-41 and SBA-15, when subjected to large numbers of thermal cycles in dry, CO 2 -free air. Emphasis is placed on the adsorption at 400 µLL − 1 CO 2 at 25 ◦C to study the potential suitability of similar grafted imine-containing systems for use as direct air capture (DAC) sorbents. For comparison, we also examine changes in the adsorption capacity at CO 2 concentrations of 5%, which are more typical of combustion exhaust. Notably, the low-concentration capacity is found to generally decrease faster than the capacity at the higher concentration with increased thermal cycling. All sorbents were found to decrease in adsorption capacity after a large number of cycles; however, DAS-derived sorbents were in general more robust. Moreover, the decrease in the CO 2 adsorption capacity at 25 ◦C before and after thermal cycling was found to vary significantly with the adsorptive concentration.

papers.title: Time-Reversal Invariant Topological Photonic Alloy
papers.abstract: Abstract Conventional approaches generate quantum spin Hall (QSH) and quantum valley Hall (QVH) effects by breaking spatial inversion symmetry across the entire photonic crystal. Modulating the bulk transmission gaps within such periodic frameworks has traditionally relied on the global modification of structural parameters throughout the lattice, which often presents substantial challenges for device reconfigurability and postfabrication adaptability. While recent advances have begun to explore localized tuning mechanisms to overcome these limitations, in this work, we demonstrate a fundamentally distinct mechanism for generating topology: the random, local breaking of crystalline spatial symmetries in a reciprocal photonic alloy. Using a photonic alloy platform based on random substitutional disorder in a parallel-plate metal waveguide, we show that disorder-driven local breaking of z-direction mirror and in-plane symmetries can open topological gaps to trigger QSH and QVH phase transitions, respectively. Importantly, this symmetry-engineered disorder manifests exclusively as diagonal perturbations, inherently suppressing backscattering in interspin/valley channels and thereby supporting robust helical edge states and valley kink states. Rigorous topological characterization via an improved, mode-mixing-free reflection-phase winding method reveals a striking size-dependent scaling behavior in both configurations, where the threshold doping concentration required to trigger the topological phase transition asymptotically vanishes in the thermodynamic limit. By enabling flexible, on-demand bulk gap engineering simply through random doping tuning─rather than relying on magnetic constituents or global structural reconfigurations─this photonic alloy platform not only deepens understanding of disorder-induced topological physics but also offers a scalable, highly efficient design strategy for integrated topological optical communications.

papers.title: Alchemy: Bounded Enumeration and Interactive Exploration of Small-Molecule Radical Reaction Networks
papers.journal: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abstract: Abstract Automated construction of chemical reaction networks is limited by the combinatorial growth of possible molecules, intermediates, and formal transformations. We present alchemy, an open-source Python workflow for systematic enumeration and interactive exploration of small-molecule radical reaction networks. Within an explicitly bounded graph space, alchemy generates connected, neutral C/N/H molecular graphs with single, double, or triple bonds and specified radical counts; RDKit sanitization and canonicalization then remove graph-invalid and duplicate records. Formal reaction candidates are constructed without learned reaction templates by combining bond-dissociation records into rearrangement and transfer stoichiometries. Parallel generation, persistent disk-backed storage, and Kuzu graph representation make the resulting formal network searchable. An independent brute-force control recovers exactly the same 416 neutral molecular graphs as alchemy in a three-heavy-atom C/N/H space. In a trimethylamine case study limited to at most five heavy atoms and one unpaired electron per reaction side, the workflow generated 41,735 unique molecular graphs and a seed-0 bounded sample of 60,035 first-generation reaction records. The reaction construction is not complete because high-frequency shared fragments are handled by a documented deterministic sampling cap. An optional PaiNN molecular-energy model is distributed with the software, but its closed-shell QM9 benchmark does not validate the open-shell species considered here, and its output is not used to rank, filter, or interpret the case-study records. Alchemy therefore, provides a reproducible route to bounded reaction-space construction and downstream graph inspection.

papers.title: Tailoring Gas Transport Properties in MOF-Based Mixed Matrix Membranes: The Role of Filler Morphology and Surface Functionalization
papers.abstract: Abstract The development of high-performance mixed-matrix membranes (MMMs) for gas separations relies on precise control of filler morphology and optimized polymer–filler interactions. In this study, we elucidate how crystal size, morphology, and surface functionalization of the perfluorinated metal–organic framework (MOF) F4_MIL-140A(Ce) influence the gas transport properties of MMMs based on Pebax 1657 and Matrimid 9725 matrices. Through systematic modulation of reaction conditions, we synthesized submicrometric F4_MIL-140A(Ce) particles with tailored size and aspect ratio, achieving improved dispersion and interfacial contact within the polymer phases. A postsynthetic grafting strategy using stearic acid further enhanced the compatibility of the MOF with the polymer matrix without altering crystallinity, pore accessibility, or CO2 adsorption behavior, as confirmed by powder X-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy, and sorption analyses. MMMs prepared with the surface-functionalized MOF displayed improved polymer–filler adhesion, minimized interfacial voids, and significantly enhanced gas transport properties. In particular, the Pebax 1657-based MMMs approached the 2008 Robeson upper bound for CO2/N2 separation, primarily driven by increased CO2 solubility, which increased the CO2 permeability by 62% (from 76 to 123 Barrer) and the CO2/N2 selectivity by 28% (from 58 to 74). In contrast, Matrimid 9725 MMMs exhibited substantial improvements in H2/N2 and O2/N2 selectivity (i.e., from 93 to 108 and from 6.6 to 7.7, respectively), because of enhanced diffusivity. The insights presented in this work provide a rational framework for engineering MOF–polymer interfaces and advancing membrane-based gas separation and CO2 capture technologies.

papers.title: Anion manipulation for breaking through 3.0 V of aluminium–graphite batteries
papers.abstract: Aluminium-graphite batteries offer low cost and intrinsic high safety. However, the voltage window mostly remains limited because conventional chloroaluminate ionic-liquid electrolytes with Lewis-acidic Al2Cl7−([AlCl3–AlCl4]−) anions are intrinsically moisture-sensitive and unstable beyond 2.5 V. To extend the voltage window, a polytetrafluoroethylene/AlF3 framework‑confined, fluorine-rich chloroaluminate ionic-liquid composite quasi-solid-state electrolyte cosolvated with 1,1,2,2-tetrafluoroethyl 2,2,2-trifluoroethyl ether is designed for constructing stable aluminium-graphite batteries with a cut-off voltage of 3.0 V. With the presence of AlF3, the Al2Cl7− is regulated through AlF3-associated chloroaluminate interactions, which reduces its activity and suppresses its electrochemical decomposition in the range of 2.5–3.0 V. Meanwhile, the fluorinated ether coordinates with the AlCl3 units in Al2Cl7− and promotes the formation of a fluorine-rich artificial interface on the graphite, essentially improving the electrochemical stability via alleviating electrochemical decomposition of AlCl4− up to 3.0 V. Furthermore, ion transport channels could be well maintained during large mechanical deformation induced by anion-intercalation/deintercalation of graphite interlayer. Therefore, the Al|electrolyte|graphite cells deliver discharge capacity beyond 137 mAh g−1 up to 3.0 V (specific current: 5.0 A g−1) (compared to 64 mAh g−1, charged up to 2.5 V at 5.0 A g−1) along with stable cycles beyond 35,000, demonstrating long-term high-voltage operation in rechargeable aluminium–graphite batteries. Aluminium–graphite batteries are limited by electrolyte decomposition above 2.5 V. Here, authors regulate chloroaluminate anions with a fluorine-rich, framework-confined quasi-solid-state electrolyte, enabling stable 3.0 V operation for Al | |Graphite cells.

papers.title: Integrated Reactive CO2 and NH3 Capture and Conversion to Ammonium Carbamate: Material Design toward Low-Concentration Sources
papers.abstract: Abstract Carbon dioxide (CO2) and ammonia (NH3) emissions are responsible for global warming and eutrophication, among other causes. Ionic liquids (ILs) stand out as versatile designer absorbent/catalyst materials that contribute to the capture and conversion of both gases. This work focuses on the efficient and innovative use of ILs in NH3 and CO2 integrated capture and conversion (ICC) to produce ammonium carbamate (AMC) using an efficient self-regenerating catalytic system operating at room temperature, with spontaneous product separation by precipitation. Experimental ICC tests were carried out using 10 ILs, with remarkable structural differences, and different NH3 and CO2 partial pressure and experimental times. Two different optimization routes were explored by tuning the IL material features through molecular design: (i) an NH3-driven mechanism using IL as the physical absorbent and (ii) a CO2-driven mechanism using IL as the reactive capture agent, selected to promote high CO2 chemical absorption and activation and easy IL regeneration and AMC removal. The use of an IL as a reactive capture agent strongly improves the process performance with fast ICC rates even at low NH3 and CO2 partial pressures, highlighting the CO2-driven approach as a versatile ICC technology capable of efficiently treating diluted NH3 and CO2 streams to produce value-added AMC products.

papers.title: Advanced biomedical materials and drug delivery systems for gastrointestinal applications: current understanding and future perspectives
papers.abstract: The gastrointestinal (GI) tract is a major site of ulcerative, inflammatory, and neoplastic diseases. It also functions as an important interface in systemic metabolic regulation. The effectiveness of current treatments is often limited by poor drug stability and short residence times in the GI tract, insufficient exposure at the target site, and unnecessary systemic exposure. These limitations are compounded by regional pH changes, digestive enzymes, mucus turnover, peristaltic clearance, immune surveillance, and microbial metabolism. Advanced biomedical materials, including mucoadhesive hydrogels, stimuli-responsive nanoplatforms, metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), and extracellular matrix (ECM)-derived scaffolds, are increasingly being developed to protect cargo, prolong mucosal residence, enable site-selective release, support tissue repair, and modulate immune or microbial processes. However, selecting a suitable material and delivery strategy for different GI diseases remains challenging. This review examines physiological barriers to drug delivery in the GI tract, classifies advanced biomaterials and delivery systems by therapeutic function and platform type, and evaluates their applications across GI diseases with attention to administration routes, target sites, therapeutic outcomes, and clinical translation. Finally, we discuss future priorities for route-specific material design, human-relevant evaluation, and the safe development of advanced delivery systems. This review aims to provide a practical reference for selecting appropriate biomaterials and delivery systems for GI disease treatment and for guiding their further development toward clinical use.

papers.title: Response Surface Optimization of Reduced‐ DMF Binary Solvents and Apparent Curing Kinetics of BMI /Epoxy/ DDS Resin Systems for Fiber‐Reinforced Composites
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT In the manufacture of fiber‐reinforced composites, bismaleimide (BMI)/epoxy resin (EP) systems are attractive matrix materials because they combine the heat resistance of BMI with the processability of EP, although their practical use is limited by reliance on highly polar amide solvents and complex curing behavior. In this work, a reduced‐DMF DMF/ethanol binary solvent system and the apparent curing kinetics of BMI/EP/DDS resin systems were investigated using Box–Behnken response surface methodology and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC). A DMF fraction of 88% was sufficient to maintain stable homogeneous solutions within the investigated composition range. Increasing EP content shifted the characteristic curing temperatures to higher values and broadened the curing‐temperature window from 40.1°C to 54.4°C, while the Kissinger activation energy increased from 91.96 to 97.76 kJ/mol. The Kissinger and Ozawa methods gave consistent apparent activation‐energy trends, indicating that the curing behavior could not be described as a simple superposition of independently curing BMI and EP components. Based on an apparent n th order kinetic model, isothermal curing windows were proposed for the three formulations. These results provide guidance for reduced‐DMF solution preparation and curing‐process design of BMI/EP/DDS resin systems for fiber‐reinforced composites.

papers.title: Waste-Derived Oil Palm Mesocarp Fiber in LLDPE Biocomposites: Low-Loading Mechanical and Moisture Response
papers.abstract: Waste-derived oil palm mesocarp fiber (OPMF) has potential as a lignocellulosic reinforcement for thermoplastic composites. The same trend in strength, stiffness, and moisture-related properties does not always hold at relatively low fiber loadings. This study examined these property changes in linear low-density polyethylene (LLDPE) biocomposites. Composites containing 0, 5, 10, and 15 wt% alkali-treated OPMF were produced by hot compression molding. Tensile and flexural properties, density, 24 h water absorption, and water contact angle were evaluated, supported by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC). The 5 wt% composite showed the highest mean tensile and flexural strengths of 16.16 ± 1.14 MPa and 29.33 ± 3.57 MPa, while the highest apparent tensile modulus (521.25 ± 38.84 MPa) and flexural modulus (0.888 ± 0.122 GPa) occurred at 10 wt%. Water absorption increased from 0.06 ± 0.01% to 1.19 ± 0.12%, while the contact angle decreased from 97.78 ± 2.04° to 65.18 ± 5.21°. Strength, stiffness, and moisture response followed different loading-dependent trends, indicating a composition-dependent strength–stiffness–moisture trade-off within the investigated range.

papers.title: Mechanical Properties Evolution and Aging Mechanism of NBR Sealing Materials Under Multiple Environmental Factors in Ultra-High Voltage Converter Station
papers.abstract: Nitrile butadiene rubber (NBR) is commonly served as a sealing element for oil-tight seals in ultra-high voltage converter stations. Due to the harsh environmental conditions in these stations, NBR is frequently exposed to thermal oxidation, ultraviolet radiation, and low temperatures, as well as the effects of the sealed medium. This work focuses on evaluating the impacts of various environmental conditions on the mechanical characteristics of NBR and analyzes the underlying mechanisms. Stress distribution under the combined action of force, heat and hypothetical electric field is analyzed with the aid of ABAQUS simulation; the aging test only investigates single factors without verifying the multi-field coupling mechanism, and the conclusions are only for qualitative reference of the simulation. The service life of NBR is effectively predicted based on the compression set decay curve. Analysis of TGA measurements reveals the gradual loss of incorporated additives upon aging, accompanied by a reduction in the thermal stability of aged NBR. Results from crosslinking density tests, FTIR, and XPS analyses demonstrate that oxidation crosslinking progressively increases as thermal-oxidative aging proceeds, the rise in C–C and C–H content is associated with the degradation of C=C bonds, oxygen-containing functional groups (carboxyl, hydroxyl, and carbonyl) are generated during the thermal-oxidative aging of NBR, and the cleavage of C–S bonds leads to the formation of S=O species.

papers.title: Dual‐Component Phytic Acid/Gallic Acid System for Enhancing Flame Retardancy and Multifunctional Packaging Performance of Polyvinyl Alcohol Films
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Although polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) exhibits excellent film‐forming ability, transparency, and biodegradability, its inherent flammability limits its applications. In this study, phytic acid (PA) and gallic acid (GA) were employed as a synergistic flame‐retardant system to prepare flame‐retardant PVA composite films via solution blending. The flame‐retardant properties and underlying mechanisms of the films were systematically investigated and characterized via limiting oxygen index (LOI), UL‐94 vertical burning tests, thermogravimetric analysis (TG), cone calorimetry (FTT), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Raman spectroscopy, and related techniques. At a PA:GA mass ratio of 3:1, the composite film achieved a UL‐94 VTM‐0 rating at a total loading as low as 10 wt%. At the highest loading tested (20 wt%), the LOI reached 47%, the peak heat release rate decreased by 81.2% relative to neat PVA, and the char residue at 600°C increased to 28.8%. Mechanistically, PA and GA enable a spatially differentiated mechanism involving “condensed‐phase char formation” and “gas‐phase flame inhibition,” as well as a temporally coordinated sequence of “char formation followed by flame suppression,” thereby enhancing the flame retardancy of the composite films. The composite film also exhibited a transmittance of 94.9% at 550 nm, an elongation at break of 590.207%, and the PA/GA system showed antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli .

papers.title: Vertical Microbial Stratification in a Three-Layer Biotrickling Filter Strengthens Simultaneous Anammox and Denitrification for Synergistic Decontamination of Trimethylamine and Nitric Oxide in Combustion Flue-Gas-Heated Sludge-Drying Off-Gas
papers.abstract: Abstract Co-treatments of trimethylamine (TMA) and nitric oxide (NO) in sludge drying off-gas receive little attention. Hitherto, TMA biofiltration shows limited nitrogen elimination; microbial collaboration in biofilters is conventionally attributed to horizontal biofilm stratification. This work elucidates vertical microbial stratification-driven simultaneous anammox-denitrification (SAD) in a three-layer biotrickling filter for decontamination of TMA and NO (loads: 44 gTMA m–3 h–1, 219 gNO m–3 h–1; 2–8% O2). Optimal removal efficiency of TMA and NO at 2% O2 attained 99% and 96%, respectively, equivalent to 71% and 29%, 25% and 38%, and 3% and 29% at the bottom, middle, and top layers. 91% of C and 99% of N were mineralized to CO2 and N2. From bottom to top, TMA declined but NO enhanced in performance, causing a C/N drop; dominant genera shifted from TMA-degrading denitrifiers to anammox bacteria; O2 mass transfer weakened; TMA removal pathway shifted from aerobic degradation to denitrifying degradation, while that of NO shifted from denitrification to anammox. These effects became more prominent at lower O2 levels. Along bed height, denitrification and anammox sequentially played leading roles in SAD: TMA was degraded to CO2 and NH3 with O2 then NO; NO was reduced to N2 with TMA then NH3. Vertical stratification gradually upgraded the removal progress toward thorough decontamination. This study provides new insights that vertical stratification can act as a driving force of functional synergy in biofiltration systems.
papers.summary: Abstract Co-treatments of trimethylamine (TMA) and nitric oxide (NO) in sludge drying off-gas receive little attention. Hitherto, TMA biofiltration shows limited nitrogen elimination; microbial collaboration in biofilters is conventionally attributed to horizontal biofilm stratification. From bottom to top, TMA declined but NO enhanced in performance, causing a C/N drop; dominant genera shifted from TMA-degrading denitrifiers to anammox bacteria; O2 mass transfer weakened; TMA removal pathway shifted from aerobic degradation to denitrifying degradation, while that of NO shifted from denitrification to anammox.

papers.title: Digital health interventions for promoting physical activity and improving anthropometric indicators in postpartum women: a systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.abstract: Background The postpartum period is often characterized by insufficient physical activity and unfavorable anthropometric changes, which may increase women's long-term health risks. Digital health interventions (DHIs) represent a flexible and accessible strategy for promoting healthy behaviors during this period. However, their effectiveness in improving physical activity and anthropometric outcomes among postpartum women remains uncertain. Methods PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were systematically searched from inception to March 25, 2026. Randomized controlled trials were eligible if they evaluated DHIs in postpartum women and reported at least one physical activity-related or anthropometric outcome. Random-effects meta-analyses were conducted, and pooled effect estimates were expressed as standardized mean differences (SMDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results Twenty-one trials involving 4,121 participants were included. DHIs were associated with a small increase in moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA; SMD = 0.21, 95% CI: 0.07 to 0.34) and reductions in body weight (SMD = −0.36, 95% CI: −0.55 to −0.17), body mass index (BMI; SMD = −0.45, 95% CI: −0.83 to −0.07), waist circumference (SMD = −0.34, 95% CI: −0.59 to −0.08), and waist-to-hip ratio (SMD = −0.59, 95% CI: −1.05 to −0.11). No statistically significant effects were observed for total physical activity (TPA; SMD = 0.14, 95% CI: −0.00 to 0.29) or physical activity self-efficacy (SMD = −0.04, 95% CI: −0.25 to 0.17), although evidence for these outcomes was limited. Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested potential improvements in MVPA and BMI with human-assisted interventions and reductions in weight-related outcomes with certain intervention types. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously. Conclusion DHIs may provide a flexible and accessible approach to increasing MVPA and improving selected anthropometric outcomes among postpartum women. However, the observed effects were generally modest, and the certainty of evidence varied across outcomes, with substantial heterogeneity in several analyses. Further high-quality RCTs with larger sample sizes and longer follow-up periods are needed to confirm these findings and determine the optimal intervention components and long-term effectiveness of DHIs. Systematic Review Registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261346240 , PROSPERO identifier CRD420261346240.

papers.title: Chromium pollution and its effects on soil health, microbial diversity, and sugarcane production in the Vellore sugarcane belt: a metagenomic and geochemical assessment
papers.journal: World Journal of Microbiology and Biotechnology
papers.abstract: Abstract Disposal of tannery effluent has elevated soil chromium (Cr) across the Vellore sugarcane belt of southern India, yet its integrated consequences for soil health, bacterial communities and sugarcane productivity remain poorly characterised. Nine composite soil samples from a recognised tannery-affected belt were pre-stratified into High, Low and Near-threshold Cr sites. Soils and irrigation water were geochemically characterised for total and speciated heavy metals and profiled by full length (V1-V9) 16​S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing on an Oxford Nanopore GridION. Soil total Cr increased from 29.10 ± 0.14 to 180.51 ± 2.95 mg kg − 1 , the alkaline-extractable Cr (VI) fraction rising from 2.92 ± 0.09 to 52.07 ± 0.11 mg kg⁻¹ and co-occurring Cd and Ni increasing across strata. Soil pH shifted alkaline (7.74 to 8.48), organic carbon declined by up to 31.7% and exchangeable Ca and Mg by up to 40.4%. Tissue Cr followed root > shoot > leaf but peaked at Near-threshold rather than High Cr sites, indicating bioavailability-driven uptake. Cane and stalk fresh weight declined 25.8–31.3% at High Cr sites, whereas sucrose, Brix, purity and fibre remained largely unchanged. Alpha diversity followed a threshold structured rather than linear dose response, with observed richness in High Cr levels reduced to 74–76% that in Low Cr levels alongside parallel declines in Shannon diversity and Pielou’s evenness. NMDS resolved three non-overlapping community clusters. A Cr-resilient core ( Sphingomonas panacis , Nitrospira lenta ) persisted alongside elevated prediction of azoR/acpD and chrA abundance, defining a chromium-tolerance signature in tannery-impacted sugarcane soils.

papers.title: Efficient and Reusable Polymer Supported Copper(II) and Vanadium(IV) Complexes of 4-(Furan-2-ylmethyleneamino)benzoic Acid as Catalysts for the Oxidation of Phenol
papers.abstract: This study reports the synthesis, characterization and catalytic evaluation of polymer supported Cu(II) and V(IV) complexes for the oxidation of phenol. The heterogeneous catalysts were prepared by covalently immobilizing 4-(furan-2-ylmethyleneamino)benzoic acid onto chloromethylated polystyrene followed by coordination with the respective metal ions. Elemental analysis, spectroscopic characterization and ligand-to-metal stoichiometry confirmed successful complex formation, with metal loadings of 1.40-1.41 mmol g–1. The vanadium complex exhibited square-pyramidal geometry with a V=O bond, while the copper complex having a square-planar geometry. The catalytic activity was evaluated using H2O2 and tert.-butyl hydroperoxide (TBHP) as oxidants under varying reaction conditions. The Cu(II) catalyst with TBHP achieved a maximum phenol conversion of 94.9% and catechol selectivity of 76.3% under optimized conditions. X-ray diffraction, BET analysis, and thermogravimetric analysis revealed a predominantly amorphous, mesoporous structure with a specific surface area of 54.05 m2 g–1 and thermal stability up to approximately 335 ºC. Spectroscopic analysis confirmed structural stability after repeated catalytic use, while atomic absorption spectroscopy revealed negligible metal leaching over five cycles. These results establish the potential of polymer-supported Cu(II) and V(IV) complexes as reusable heterogeneous catalysts for phenol oxidation.

papers.title: Management Control Optimization under Managerial Overconfidence: A Principal–Agent Model of Business Development Decisions
papers.journal: Journal of Decision Science and Optimization
papers.abstract: Business development decisions require resource commitments under uncertain opportunity quality, giving managerial judgment a central role in investment evaluation. This study develops an agency model to examine how managerial overconfidence shapes optimal incentive intensity and monitoring intensity. A behavioral parameter captures the manager's overestimation of opportunity value, while the board anticipates the investment response and selects both control instruments. Equilibrium analysis examines how biased beliefs, environmental uncertainty, effort costs, and monitoring costs influence control choices. Overconfidence raises perceived investment returns and increases managerial effort for given control choices. Comparative statics suggest that stronger bias reduces optimal incentive intensity and increases optimal monitoring intensity. Inflated expectations provide investment motivation and reduce the need for financial rewards. Monitoring reduces evaluation error losses outside the compensation measure. Numerical illustrations show lower optimal incentive shares and higher monitoring intensity as overconfidence increases. These findings connect managerial cognition with endogenous control design and clarify how behavioral and informational conditions shape business development decisions. The model distinguishes the motivational effects of overconfidence from evaluation losses outside compensation measures and characterizes the optimal control response to each effect.

papers.title: Nutritional, Structural, Thermal and Bioactive Characterization of Drynaria quercifolia (L.) J.Sm Rhizome
papers.journal: Asian Journal of Dairy and Food Research
papers.abstract: Background: Drynaria quercifolia (L.) J.Sm. (Polypodiaceae) is an ethnomedicinally significant pteridophyte traditionally associated with anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, anticancer and anti-rheumatic properties owing to its diverse bioactive constituents. Methods: This study comprehensively characterized Drynaria quercifolia Rhizome Powder (DQRP) by evaluating its nutritional composition, fatty acids, bioactive constituents, anti-nutritional factors, structural and thermal characteristics. Result: DQRP exhibited a favourable nutritional composition, with considerable protein, soluble and insoluble fibre and carbohydrate content, together with notable levels of vitamin C and vitamin E. Fatty acid analysis revealed palmitic acid and linoleic acid as the major fatty acid methyl esters. DQRP also exhibited appreciable flavonoid, phenolic and terpenoid content, while anti-nutritional factors were present at levels comparable to those reported for other plant-based foods. Structural analysis (FTIR) indicated bands characteristic of functional groups associated with alcohols, phenols, carboxylic acids and aromatic compounds, while thermal analysis showed moderate thermal stability. FESEM revealed an irregular, fibrous and layered morphology indicative of a porous structure that may be favourable for food applications. These findings represent a preliminary investigation of DQRP as a potential ingredient source for future functional food formulation studies.

papers.title: Thiazole-functionalized copolymer‑mediated interfacial engineering towards high‑performance SBR/Kaolin composites
papers.journal: Journal of Materials Science Materials in Engineering
papers.abstract: Abstract To address the pronounced particle agglomeration and poor interfacial compatibility of kaolin in elastomer systems, poly(isoprene- co -4-methyl-5-vinylthiazole) (PIPMVT) was synthesized via free-radical polymerization. Based on performance optimization, the copolymer with an MVT : IP feed molar ratio of 20 : 80 and an M n of 14 kDa was identified as optimal, and modified kaolin (PM-Kaolin) was prepared by spray-coating PIPMVT onto the kaolin surface. During the thermo-vulcanization process, the isoprene double bonds in the copolymer can graft onto the rubber backbone. Meanwhile, the thiazole units interact with the kaolin surface and act synergistically with the isoprene segments, thereby forming an interfacial mediator between kaolin and styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR). The effects of PIPMVT on the vulcanization characteristics, mechanical properties, filler dispersion, and viscoelastic behavior of SBR composites were systematically investigated. The results demonstrated that PIPMVT significantly improved the dispersion of kaolin and its interfacial compatibility within the SBR matrix, effectively suppressing filler agglomeration. At a loading of 50 phr, the tensile strength of the SBR/PM-Kaolin composite reached 11.50 MPa, representing a 51.3% increase over the unmodified system. Dynamic mechanical analysis further reveals that the modified composite exhibits improved viscoelastic stability. Significant improvements in stress relaxation were observed.

papers.title: Conformation-selective inhibition and destabilisation of MERS-CoV papain-like protease by the flavonol fisetin: an integrated in vitro and in silico study
papers.abstract: Background Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus (MERS-CoV) continues to cause sporadic zoonotic infections with a case-fatality rate of approximately 35%, with recent 2025 surveillance confirming ongoing activity internationally. No specific antivirals or vaccines have been approved. Viral papain-like protease (PLpro) is essential for polyprotein processing making it a high-priority biochemical lead. Fisetin has been tested in clinical trials for its senolytic and anti-inflammatory activity and has demonstrated inhibitory activity against other coronavirus enzymes. However, it has not been evaluated as inhibitor for MERS-CoV PLpro. This study investigates fisetin as a novel MERS-CoV PLpro inhibitor. Methods Recombinant MERS-CoV PLpro was expressed in E. coli BL21 (DE3) and purified by Ni-NTA chromatography. Fisetin’s inhibitory potency was quantified by fluorogenic protease assay (Z-RLRGG-AMC substrate) and thermal shift assay (TSA). The binding interface was characterised by 100 ns all-atom MD simulations from both closed and open PLpro conformations, and independently cross-validated by AI co-folding using Boltz-2. Results Fisetin inhibited MERS-CoV PLpro with an IC 50 of 40.58 µM. TSA revealed concentration-dependent destabilisation (ΔTm −7.66 to −20.09 °C), a signature distinct from our previously characterised inhibitors. Contact frequency analysis localised stable fisetin engagement to a catalytic-domain pocket (residues 164–209; frequency 0.71–1.00) enclosed, while open conformation showed only diffuse surface sampling. Boltz-2 independently placed fisetin at the same pocket, with five of six predicted contacts overlapping the MD set (Jaccard 0.545; Spearman ρ = 0.43, p < 10 −15 ). Conclusion Fisetin is a dietary-derived MERS-CoV PLpro inhibitor engaging a catalytic-domain pocket distinct from the binding regions identified for our previously characterised inhibitors. Available human safety and pharmacokinetic data support further investigation of fisetin, particularly through cellular antiviral validation, formulation optimization, and combination studies.

papers.title: Engineering Surface Reconstruction of Perovskite Oxides through Vanadium Doping and Alkalinity Regulation for Enhanced Oxygen Evolution
papers.abstract: Abstract Lattice oxygen participation in perovskite electrocatalysts can significantly enhance oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity, yet it often compromises long-term durability due to severe surface reconstruction and bulk degradation. Here, we deliberately engineer surface reconstruction to reconcile activity and stability by preconstructing a highly active and robust (oxy)hydroxide layer on a perovskite oxide. A vanadium-doped perovskite, SrFe0.25Co0.25Ni0.18V0.02Mo0.3O3 (SFCNM-V0.02), is rationally designed, in which V-doping facilitates rapid OH–-induced reconstruction. Preimmersion in concentrated KOH accelerates the formation of a dense and stable amorphous (oxy)hydroxide layer that suppresses bulk dissolution while serving as the dominant catalytic active phase. Consequently, SFCNM-V0.02 delivers a low overpotential of 265 mV at 10 mA cm–2 and exceptional operational stability exceeding 1100 h in 1 M KOH. Furthermore, by correlating the degree of surface reconstruction with catalytic activity, we analyzed the origin of the pH-dependent variation observed in this work, which provides useful implications for appropriately evaluating pH-dependent behaviors in electrocatalysis. This work demonstrates that controlled surface reconstruction fundamentally governs OER performance in perovskite oxides and provides practical design principles for durable, high-efficiency OER electrocatalysts.

papers.title: An in vitro study of cyclic fatigue resistance and bending performance of three heat-treated nickel-titanium endodontic systems at physiological temperature
papers.abstract: Objective. To evaluate and compare the cyclic fatigue resistance and bending resistance of three heat-treated nickel-titanium systems (2Shape, Reciproc Blue, and EdgeFile X7) at a physiological intracanal temperature (37°C). Methods. Eighty-four unused NiTi instruments were tested, with a total of 28 instruments allocated to each of the three systems. Fourteen independent instruments from each system – 2Shape (25/.06), Reciproc Blue (25/.08), and EdgeFile X7 (25/.06) – were used for each test. Bending resistance testing was conducted according to ISO 3630-1 using a universal testing machine (Instron, Canton, MA, USA) with a 45° deflection protocol at 37°C. Cyclic fatigue resistance was evaluated in a stainless-steel artificial canal with a 45° angle of curvature, a 3-mm radius of curvature, a 1.5 mm canal diameter, and a 3.5 mm curved segment. The canal was immersed in a thermally controlled water bath. Time to fracture was recorded for the reciprocating system, and NCF was calculated for the continuous-rotation systems. Data were analyzed using one-way ANOVA followed by post hoc tests (α = 0.05). Effect size was recorded. Results. Significant differences were observed among the tested groups (p < 0.05). EdgeFile X7 demonstrated the highest cyclic fatigue resistance, while Reciproc Blue showed the greatest bending resistance. Fragment length did not differ significantly among the groups (p > 0.05). Effect size analysis indicated a strong influence of instrument design and heat-treatment technology on mechanical behavior. Conclusion. The mechanical performance of the tested heat-treated NiTi instruments at 37°C is influenced by both metallurgical phase composition and geometric design. EdgeFile X7 demonstrated higher resistance to cyclic fatigue at simulated intracanal temperature, while Reciproc Blue exhibited higher bending resistance, likely associated with its greater taper and metal mass.

papers.title: Preparation of Ether-free Polycarbazole-Based Anion Exchange Membranes and Regulation of Cations on Membrane Properties and Fuel Cell Performance
papers.abstract: Abstract Quaternized ether-free aromatic polymers from superacid-catalyzed polycondensation are excellent candidates for high-performance anion exchange membranes (AEMs). Most current studies mainly focus on cation-modified carbon-aromatic AEMs. However, the structure–property relationship of cation-functionalized heteroaromatic polyarylene systems is still insufficiently understood. This work develops a series of carbazole-based ether-free AEMs with different side-chain quaternary ammonium (QA) cations, including conventional trimethylammonium, charge-delocalized imidazolium, and N-cyclic piperidinium and quinuclidinium. All membranes share the same polycarbazole backbone. Thus, the side-chain cation structure primarily determines membrane comprehensive performance. QPC-TMA with trimethylammonium groups exhibits the highest hydroxide conductivity at 80 °C, owing to its high ion exchange capacity and well-developed microphase separation. In comparison, QPC-QUI with bulky quinuclidinium groups shows outstanding alkaline and oxidative stability under harsh aging conditions. It shows least conductivity loss (2.65% loss for 1080 h) and weight loss (0.81% loss for 72 h).In fuel cell tests, the QPC-QUI-based AEM achieves a peak power density of 998 mW cm–2, which is higher than QPC-TMA (928 mW cm–2). This work proves that rational cation structural design of ether-free heteroaromatic polymers is a reliable strategy to prepare high-conductivity and durable AEMs for electrochemical energy applications.

papers.title: Molecular identification and spatial distribution of cutaneous leishmaniasis cases in Markazi Province, central Iran, using ITS1 PCR RFLP and GIS
papers.abstract: Abstract Cutaneous leishmaniasis (CL) remains a considerable public health concern in Iran. This study aimed to characterize Leishmania spp. among available diagnostic specimens and describe the spatial distribution of cases reported in the Markazi Province during 2021–2022. In this cross-sectional study, all 210 microscopically confirmed CL cases were analyzed using a total census sampling method. A subset of 42 cases with available diagnostic smears was evaluated by internal transcribed spacer 1-polymerase chain reaction-restriction fragment length polymorphism (ITS1-PCR-RFLP) for species identification, followed by sequencing of four representative amplicons. Spatial distribution of the 42 molecularly characterized cases was mapped using a Geographic Information System (GIS; ArcGIS 10) based on recorded coordinates. Among all 210 cases, CL was more frequent in males (57.1%) with the highest proportion in the 40–49-year age group (20.5%). Lesions were predominantly ulcerative with exudate and localized to the extremities. All 42 molecularly analyzed samples were identified as Leishmania major , though this convenient subset may not fully represent the overall species composition across the entire province. Phylogenetic analysis confirmed that the sequenced isolates clustered within the L. major clade. GIS-based descriptive mapping indicated that analyzed cases were localized primarily in Saveh and Mahallat counties. These findings provide an updated baseline for CL in Markazi Province; however, systematic molecular surveys and vector-reservoir investigations are needed to fully delineate species distribution and transmission dynamics across all counties.
papers.summary: Abstract Cutaneous leishmaniasis (CL) remains a considerable public health concern in Iran. In this cross-sectional study, all 210 microscopically confirmed CL cases were analyzed using a total census sampling method. GIS-based descriptive mapping indicated that analyzed cases were localized primarily in Saveh and Mahallat counties.

papers.title: High condition index and distinct biochemical profiles in triploid Crassostrea gigas cultured at a high-energy open-water site
papers.abstract: High-energy open-water (HEO) sites are increasingly being explored as alternatives to conventional coastal oyster farms, yet their suitability for triploid Pacific oysters remains poorly documented. This study compared the physiological condition and tissue biochemical composition of a single cohort of triploid Crassostrea gigas cultured for 7 months at three Korean grow-out environments: an independently moored HEO site located approximately 1.3 km from an operating offshore wind farm, a sheltered subtidal bay, and an intertidal flat exposed to regular emersion. Biometric observations were made on 30 oysters from three culture units per site and are reported descriptively. Biochemical analyses were based on three pooled composites per site, one from each culture unit. Oysters sampled from the HEO site showed smaller mean shell size and whole weight but greater mean soft tissue mass and the highest mean condition index (29.2%), compared with 13.9–15.0% at the coastal sites. Proximate composition differed among the three sites, with HEO oysters showing higher mean crude fat, ash, and carbohydrate fractions but a lower mean crude protein concentration. Within the diethyl ether extract, oleic acid and DHA showed their highest mean relative proportions at HEO, whereas EPA and ARA showed their highest mean relative proportions at the intertidal Gochang site. These findings provide initial site-specific evidence that independently moored HEO culture is compatible with high tissue condition in triploid oysters, and that tissue biochemical composition at this site differed from that of the two coastal sites. However, because site, culture system, and environmental conditions varied simultaneously, the findings should not be interpreted as an isolated test of hydrodynamic exposure or proximity to the offshore wind farm.

papers.title: Influence of biodegradable microplastic alteration during composting and drying/rewetting cycles on soil physicochemical properties
papers.abstract: Biodegradable microplastics (MPs) may enter soils either as pristine materials during agricultural plastic use or through organic fertilizers after partial degradation during composting. Their impacts on soil properties may be influenced by climatic conditions. The aim of this study was to investigate how (i) MP degradation state (pristine or composted) and (ii) physical stress cycles (alternating freeze–thaw, drying–rewetting) influence soil properties. To this end, one Cambisol was exposed in controlled conditions to three types of MPs at a concentration of 1% (w/w), with four soil incubation replicates: a conventional polyethylene (PE) film, and two biodegradable films, a poly(butylene adipate terephthalate) and starch (PBAT/starch) film, and an ethylcellulose-based (EC-based) film. MPs were introduced either as pristine or after composting, then visible fragments were removed after a 59-day incubation period, to evaluate the effects of incubation on soil physical properties after removal of visible plastic fragments, rather than their physical presence. However, some leachates or small plastic fragments may still be present. Incubation was conducted either under constant conditions or under alternating physical stress cycles. Soil physicochemical and aggregation properties were measured and SOC composition analyzed using Rock-Eval ® pyrolysis. Soil responses varied primarily according to plastic type and degradation state. No significant effects on the measured properties were observed during the 59-day incubation with PE MPs, whether pristine or composted, whereas state-dependent responses were observed for biodegradable MPs. Pristine PBAT/starch and EC-based MPs changed soil pH and electrical conductivity, and increased mean weight diameter (MWD). Composting attenuated several of these effects, particularly for PBAT/starch. For EC-based MPs, composting attenuated responses for mean weight diameter and SOC content, whereas pH and electrical conductivity showed opposite trends between pristine and composted MP treatments. Alternating physical stress cycles selectively modulated specific soil properties in a treatment- and plastic composition-dependent manner, with effects mainly observed for MWD, soil pH, and electrical conductivity.
papers.summary: Biodegradable microplastics (MPs) may enter soils either as pristine materials during agricultural plastic use or through organic fertilizers after partial degradation during composting. The aim of this study was to investigate how (i) MP degradation state (pristine or composted) and (ii) physical stress cycles (alternating freeze–thaw, drying–rewetting) influence soil properties. For EC-based MPs, composting attenuated responses for mean weight diameter and SOC content, whereas pH and electrical conductivity showed opposite trends between pristine and composted MP treatments.

papers.title: Energy expenditure, body composition, and nutrient adequacy in personnel of a Chilean Antarctic expedition: an occupational comparison
papers.abstract: Background Antarctic expeditions expose personnel to extreme environmental conditions that may compromise nutritional status, energy metabolism, and body composition. This exploratory study characterized these parameters in Chilean Antarctic personnel and assessed dietary macro- and micronutrient adequacy. Methods Twenty participants (14 men, 6 women; median age 41 [IQR 35–46] years) deployed for at least 15 days to Escudero and Yelcho stations (November 2024–March 2025) were assessed before and after deployment. Resting metabolic rate (RMR) and respiratory quotient (RQ) were measured by indirect calorimetry, body composition by bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA), handgrip strength by dynamometry, and dietary intake by 24-h recall compared with Dietary Reference Intakes. Solar radiation was obtained from the INACH sensor network. Results RMR, body composition, and handgrip strength did not change after the expedition. RQ showed a nominal increase (median 0.74 to 0.80) that was not significant after correction for multiple comparisons. At baseline, 45% of participants were obese and 65% had excess body fat. Energy, protein, and lipid intakes were close to reference values, whereas intakes of vitamin D (median 5% of the reference value; all participants below it), folate, fiber, vitamin C, and carbohydrate were below reference values. Daily solar radiation at Escudero had a median of 147 W/m 2 and fell by more than half between December and March. Conclusion Chilean Antarctic personnel showed a high risk of inadequate intake of several micronutrients, particularly vitamin D, together with a high prevalence of baseline adiposity. Because vitamin D status was not measured biochemically, these findings indicate risk rather than confirmed deficiency. They support biochemical monitoring, preventive vitamin D supplementation protocols, and improved food provisioning for Antarctic personnel.

papers.title: Feasibility and safety of dual-wavelength 980/1470 nm laser for laparoscopic fenestration of hepatic cysts: a preliminary clinical study
papers.abstract: Background Laparoscopic fenestration and drainage is the standard treatment for symptomatic hepatic cysts. Conventional high-frequency electrocautery and ultrasonic scalpels have inherent limitations in simultaneously achieving efficient cutting and hemostasis, complete epithelial ablation, and preservation of intrahepatic vascular structures, leading to thermal injury, incomplete cyst wall treatment, and recurrence. The 980/1470 nm dual-wavelength laser leverages differential photothermal absorption by hemoglobin and water to enable layered, targeted therapy, offering a novel approach to optimizing minimally invasive hepatic cyst treatment, though clinical evidence remains limited. This study explores the feasibility, safety, and early efficacy of 980/1470 nm dual-wavelength laser in laparoscopic hepatic cyst fenestration, summarizes its technical essentials, and reports a preliminary single-port laparoscopic application of this laser system as an illustrative case. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted of 10 patients who underwent laparoscopic hepatic cyst fenestration and drainage using 980/1470 nm dual-wavelength laser between May 2024 and September 2026. Intraoperatively, the 980/1470 nm dual-wavelength laser was used for cyst fenestration, combined with 1470 nm laser for precise superficial epithelial ablation of the cyst wall. Preoperative demographics, laser parameters, operative time, intraoperative blood loss, postoperative hospital stay, and complications were analyzed. Short-term imaging follow-up was performed to assess cyst recurrence and cavity healing. Results Ten patients were enrolled, all of whom underwent successful laparoscopic surgery, including one case performed with a flexible single-port laparoscope. Postoperative pathology confirmed biliary hepatic cysts in all patients. Intraoperative blood loss was minimal, surgical trauma and stress were low, and no severe complications such as bile leakage, intra-abdominal hemorrhage, or infection occurred. All patients recovered uneventfully. Short-term imaging at a mean follow-up of 3 months demonstrated cyst cavity reduction or closure in all patients. Conclusion In this small pilot cohort, 980/1470 nm dual-wavelength laser laparoscopic fenestration and drainage appeared feasible and safe, with no severe perioperative complications and favorable short-term imaging outcomes; the single-port application described here represents a single illustrative case. Given the small sample size, absence of a comparator group, and short follow-up, these findings are preliminary and require confirmation in larger controlled studies with longer-term surveillance.

Conclusion In this small pilot cohort, 980/1470 nm dual-wavelength laser laparoscopic fenestration and drainage appeared feasible and safe, with no severe perioperative complications and favorable short-term imaging outcomes; the single-port application described here represents a single illustrative case.

papers.title: Normalized RGB imaging and transfer learning predict surface moisture at exposed earthen sites
papers.abstract: Abstract Repeated assessment of moisture content is essential for the preventive conservation of open-air earthen sites, yet conventional contact-based methods cannot readily provide dense spatial coverage. This study proposes a non-destructive method that predicts surface moisture content from chromatic features. A laboratory reference model was first developed using normalized RGB features (R_norm, G_norm, B_norm) that are insensitive to illuminance variation, and the model was then adapted to complex field lighting conditions through transfer learning. The transferred model yielded high prediction accuracy for the silty clay and silt tested in this study under conditions of low surface roughness (PEDI ≤0.3). Within the tested conditions, this workflow enables low-cost, non-contact assessment of surface moisture content and offers a practical tool for the field investigation and preventive conservation of open-air earthen sites.

papers.title: Aloe vera-mediated green-synthesized silver nanoparticles enhance physiological performance and yield in bread wheat
papers.abstract: Green-synthesized silver nanoparticles (GS-AgNPs) have emerged as promising nano-biostimulant for improving crop productivity; however, their physiological effects under field conditions remain insufficiently understood. This study synthesized Aloe vera-mediated GS-AgNPs and characterized them using UV-Vis spectroscopy, FTIR, DLS, zeta potential, XRD, SEM, and EDX analyses. The synthesized GS-AgNPs exhibited concentration-dependent antioxidants, antifungal, antihemolytic, and phytostimulatory activities. Their agronomic potential was evaluated through foliar application at 5, 10, and 15 ppm to four bread wheat cultivars under field conditions. GS-AgNP application significantly enhanced growth, photosynthetic pigments, antioxidant defense, nitrogen metabolism, nutrient accumulation, grain nutritional quality, and yield in a cultivar-dependent manner. The 15 ppm treatment produced the greatest responses for several measured traits, although some trait-specific maxima occurred at 10 ppm. Grain yield in Borlaug-16 increased from 2.35 ± 0.11 to 6.93 ± 1.10 g plant −1 , corresponding to a 194.9% increase, while biological yield in Wafaq-23 increased by 94.25%, chlorophyll a in Zincol-16 by 216.4%, carotenoids in Wafaq-23 by 274.3%, urease activity in Zincol-16 by 169.3%, protein content in Borlaug-16 by 63.1%, and stem phosphorus in Wafaq-23 by 222.5%. Malondialdehyde, hydrogen peroxide, proline, and electrolyte leakage were reduced by 50.0%, 33.0%, 50.7%, and 26.6%, respectively. Multivariate analyses revealed strong associations among physiological, biochemical, nutritional, and yield-related traits. Collectively, low-dose Aloe vera-mediated GS-AgNPs improved wheat performance with no apparent phytotoxic effects under the tested conditions and concentrations, highlighting their potential as nano-biostimulant for wheat production.
